problems.detail: "East to west" is wrong: the north and south sides run east to west and are a hundred cubits (27:9-11). The fifty-cubit width is the east and west ends, which is measured north to south.
"A hundred cubits" is the east-to-west distance the question asks about, so it could fairly be picked.

review.why: The question said "east to west," but the courtyard's sides running east to west are a hundred cubits long, while fifty cubits is its width; the question now asks simply for the width in Exodus 27:18, and the choice "A hundred cubits" was replaced with "Fifteen cubits."

problems.detail: Ebed-melech did rescue Jeremiah from the cistern (Jer 38), a true detail of his story that a reader who knows it could fairly pick, even though the LORD's message gives trust as the reason.

review.why: The LORD gave trust in Him as the reason (Jer 39:18), but the choice about rescuing Jeremiah was a true act of Ebed-melech and could be picked, so it was replaced with a clearly wrong choice.

problems.detail: The question says the leader would "encourage and then be encouraged". The BSB has the LORD tell Moses to encourage Joshua, because he will enable Israel to inherit the land.

review.why: The question garbled the text ("encourage and then be encouraged") and said the LORD was angry with Israel here. I reworded it to say the LORD was angry with Moses and told him to encourage Joshua, who would enable Israel to inherit the land.

problems.detail: The question says Josiah removed the abominations 'throughout his reign after renewing the covenant', but in 2 Chr 34:33 'throughout his reign' belongs to the people not turning aside, and the removal is not dated after the covenant.
The answer's 'them' is vague, and the question's mention of 'the lands' almost gives the answer away.

review.why: The question put "throughout his reign" on Josiah's removing the abominations, but the verse says that about the people not turning from the LORD; it now asks what Josiah required of everyone in Israel, which the verse states plainly.

written:EXO-16-1:5.question: When the Israelites first saw the thin flakes on the desert floor, what did they ask one another?
written:EXO-16-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-16-1:6.question: In Exodus 16, what happened to the manna that some people kept until morning against Moses' command?
written:EXO-16-1:6.answer: It became infested with maggots and began to smell
written:EXO-16-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-17-1:1.question: When God told Moses to go ahead of the people to get water at Rephidim, which item from Egypt did God tell him to take in his hand?
written:EXO-17-1:1.answer: The staff with which he struck the Nile
written:EXO-17-1:1.why: also right: A: A is arguably the same staff. Exodus 4:2-4 and 7:9-10 describe the staff of God turning into a snake, and the text names it as Moses' staff in 4:20 and 17:9, though 7:12 calls the snake-staff Aaron's. C is stated directly in 17:5.

written:EXO-17-1:2.question: When the Israelites complained of thirst at Rephidim, what did Moses say they were doing to the LORD by quarreling with him?
written:EXO-17-1:2.why: also right: A: Moses says 'Why do you test the LORD?' (17:2), and 17:7 repeats it. Psalm 78:17-18 describes this same Massah/Meribah episode as rebelling against the Most High and putting God to the test, so A is a fair alternative from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:EXO-18-13:3.question: Why did Jethro tell Moses that he and the people with him would wear themselves out?
written:EXO-18-13:3.answer: The task was too heavy for Moses to handle alone
written:EXO-18-13:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-19-1:5.question: Why did the LORD tell Moses He would come to him in a dense cloud at Mount Sinai?
written:EXO-19-1:5.answer: So the people would hear Him speak with Moses and always trust Moses

written:EXO-20-18:2.question: At Mount Sinai, according to Moses, why had God come to the people?
written:EXO-20-18:2.answer: To test them so the fear of Him would keep them from sinning

written:EXO-20-22:2.question: In Exodus 20, what did the LORD say would defile an altar of stones if the Israelites used it on the stones?
written:EXO-20-22:2.why: not clear on its own: Exodus 20:25 says the altar is profaned if the Israelites 'wield your tool' on the stones. English translations say 'tool', not 'chisel'. The Hebrew word (chereb) can mean 'sword' (D), while the hewing context suggests a chisel (A). The question does not settle which one it means.

written:EXO-21-12:3.question: In Exodus 21, if two men quarreled and one struck the other with a stone or fist so that he was confined to bed but recovered, what must the one who struck him pay?
written:EXO-21-12:3.answer: Compensation for his lost work, and see that he is completely healed
written:EXO-21-12:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-23-20:2.question: In God's instructions about the angel He would send before Israel, why were the people told not to defy the angel?
written:EXO-23-20:2.answer: He will not forgive rebellion, since God's Name is in him
written:EXO-23-20:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-24-1:2.question: When Moses read the Book of the Covenant to the people at Mount Sinai, how did they reply?
written:EXO-24-1:2.answer: “All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.”

written:EXO-24-1:4.question: In Exodus 24, what was under the feet of the God of Israel when Moses and the elders saw Him?
written:EXO-24-1:4.answer: A work like a pavement made of sapphire
written:EXO-24-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-25-10:2.question: According to God's instructions in Exodus 25, what was to be placed inside the ark of the covenant?
written:EXO-25-10:2.why: also right: A, B: Exodus 25:16 names only the Testimony, so C is the answer for this section. Hebrews 9:4 says the ark held a golden jar of manna and Aaron's staff, so A and B are also true of the ark elsewhere in Scripture, though not in these instructions.

written:EXO-27-9:3.question: How was the curtain for the gate of the tabernacle courtyard decorated?
written:EXO-27-9:3.answer: Embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen
written:EXO-27-9:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-28-6:1.question: In God's instructions for the High Priest's ephod, where was Aaron to bear the names of the sons of Israel as a memorial before the LORD?
written:EXO-28-6:1.why: not clear on its own: Exodus gives two accurate answers. Exodus 28:12 has Aaron bear the names of the children of Israel "before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial" (A). Exodus 28:29 has him bear the names of the sons of Israel "upon his heart" in the breastpiece "for a memorial before the LORD" (heart part of B). Choice B's "on the sash" is inaccurate, since the breastpiece was fastened to the ephod with chains and cords, but the question does not say which passage it means.

written:EXO-28-6:2.question: In the instructions for the ephod, how were the names of the sons of Israel to be divided between the two stones?
written:EXO-28-6:2.answer: Six names on one stone and six on the other, in order of birth

written:EXO-28-15:2.question: In Exodus 28, what was engraved on each of the twelve stones of the breastpiece, like a seal?
written:EXO-28-15:2.answer: The name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel
written:EXO-28-15:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-28-31:3.question: According to Exodus 28, why was Aaron to wear the robe with bells whenever he ministered in the sanctuary?
written:EXO-28-31:3.answer: So that its sound would be heard and he would not die
written:EXO-28-31:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-29-1:3.question: When Aaron was consecrated as priest, what was Moses told to do with the anointing oil?
written:EXO-29-1:3.answer: Anoint him by pouring it on his head
written:EXO-29-1:3.why: also right: D: Section 29:7 settles A. D is arguably true elsewhere: Leviticus 8:30 says Moses sprinkled anointing oil and blood on Aaron and his garments, which include the ephod and breastplate, though it is not the instruction given in this section.

written:EXO-29-31:1.question: In God's instructions for ordaining Aaron and his sons, what was to be done with any ordination meat or bread left until the morning?
written:EXO-29-31:1.answer: It was to be burned up
written:EXO-29-31:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-29-38:3.question: In Exodus 29, what did God say would happen at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting where the daily burnt offering was made?
written:EXO-29-38:3.answer: He would meet Israel and speak with Moses
written:EXO-29-38:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-29-45:2.question: In Exodus 29, from which land does the LORD say He brought the Israelites so that He might dwell among them?
written:EXO-29-45:2.why: also right: D: Goshen was a region within Egypt where the Israelites lived (Genesis 47:27; Exodus 8:22), and they set out from Rameses in Goshen (Exodus 12:37), so D is a narrower, arguably correct form of the answer. The section itself names only 'the land of Egypt.'

written:EXO-30-1:2.question: Where was the altar of incense to be placed, according to God's instructions in Exodus 30?
written:EXO-30-1:2.answer: In front of the veil before the ark of the Testimony
written:EXO-30-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-30-1:4.question: In Exodus 30, what did God say Aaron must do on the horns of the altar of incense once a year?
written:EXO-30-1:4.answer: Make atonement with the blood of the sin offering
written:EXO-30-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-31-1:3.question: According to the LORD's words about Bezalel, with what did God fill him, along with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship?
written:EXO-31-1:3.why: also right: C: The section says Bezalel was filled with the Spirit of God. Choice C is a near-match to other passages: Exodus 28:3 says skilled craftsmen were filled with a spirit of wisdom, and Deuteronomy 34:9 says Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom. Neither says 'wisdom and counsel' or applies to Bezalel, so B is the intended answer.

written:EXO-31-12:3.question: In Exodus 31, what reason did the LORD give for the Sabbath being a sign forever between Him and the Israelites?
written:EXO-31-12:3.answer: In six days He made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh He rested

written:EXO-33-1:1.question: In Exodus 33, why did the LORD say He would not go up with the Israelites to the promised land?
written:EXO-33-1:1.answer: They were a stiff-necked people, and He might destroy them on the way

written:EXO-33-12:3.question: What did Moses ask the LORD to show him after the LORD agreed to do what he had asked?
written:EXO-33-12:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-34-10:3.question: In the LORD's renewed covenant with Israel, what did He tell them to do to the altars, sacred stones, and Asherah poles of the inhabitants of the land?
written:EXO-34-10:3.answer: Tear down the altars, smash the stones, and chop down the poles
written:EXO-34-10:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-35-1:2.question: In Moses' instructions about the Sabbath in Exodus 35, what was forbidden in all the dwellings of the Israelites on the Sabbath day?
written:EXO-35-1:2.why: also right: A, B: The section explicitly forbids only lighting a fire in the dwellings. Baking and cooking are not named here, but they require fire, so they follow by implication; Exodus 16:23 also has bread baked and food boiled on the sixth day for the Sabbath. The question asks for the stated prohibition, so D is the pick.

written:EXO-35-10:1.question: In Moses' instructions in Exodus 35, whom does he call to come and make everything the LORD has commanded?
written:EXO-35-10:1.answer: Every skilled craftsman among the Israelites
written:EXO-35-10:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EXO-35-20:2.question: In Exodus 35, what did the skilled women do and bring for the work on the Tent of Meeting?
written:EXO-35-20:2.answer: They spun yarn and goat hair with their hands and brought it
written:EXO-35-20:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-38-21:1.question: In the inventory of the tabernacle materials, which man of the tribe of Judah made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses?
written:EXO-38-21:1.answer: Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur
written:EXO-38-21:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EXO-40-1:2.question: When Moses set up the tabernacle, what did he place inside the ark of the Testimony?

written:EXO-40-1:8.question: According to Exodus 40, when did Moses, Aaron, and his sons wash their hands and feet at the basin?
written:EXO-40-1:8.answer: Whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar
written:EXO-40-1:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-3-1:5.question: In Leviticus 3, which part of a lamb, besides the fat on the entrails, was to be burned for the LORD in the peace offering?
written:LEV-3-1:5.answer: The entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone
written:LEV-3-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-4-1:7.question: In Leviticus 4, where was the rest of the priest's bull, its hide and flesh, taken and burned?
written:LEV-4-1:7.answer: Outside the camp, to a clean place where ashes are poured out
written:LEV-4-1:7.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-7-28:5.question: According to Leviticus 7:37-38, where did the LORD give Moses the laws of the offerings?
written:LEV-7-28:5.why: also right: B: Lev 7:38 names Mount Sinai. Horeb is another name for the same mountain elsewhere in Scripture (e.g., Deut 1:6; Ex 3:1), so B is arguably right too; the section's own text points to A.

written:LEV-9-1:2.question: When Moses told Aaron what to offer for himself in Leviticus 9, which animals did he command Aaron to take for his sin offering and his burnt offering?
written:LEV-9-1:2.answer: A young bull and a ram, both without blemish
written:LEV-9-1:2.why: also right: B: 9:2 says Aaron's own offerings are a young bull and a ram, both without blemish. Option B (an ox and a ram, both without blemish) is a broader term for the same kind of animal, and the ram matches. The text uses 'ox' only for the people's peace offering in 9:4, so B is a weaker fit.

written:LEV-9-1:3.question: What reason did Moses give the Israelites for the offerings, saying the LORD would do this on that day?
written:LEV-9-1:3.answer: The LORD would appear to them
written:LEV-9-1:3.why: not clear on its own: "Do this" has no antecedent in the question. Reword to ask what the LORD would do, e.g. "the LORD would appear to them." Lev 9:4 and 9:6 support C.

written:LEV-11-1:4.question: In Leviticus 11, which flying insects with four legs were the Israelites allowed to eat?
written:LEV-11-1:4.answer: Those with jointed legs above their feet for hopping, such as locusts
written:LEV-11-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-11-1:6.question: In Leviticus 11, what had to be done with a clay pot into which a carcass of an unclean crawling creature fell?
written:LEV-11-1:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LEV-16-1:1.question: In Leviticus 16, why was Aaron told not to enter the Most Holy Place freely at any time?
written:LEV-16-1:1.answer: Because he would die; the LORD appears in the cloud above the mercy seat

written:LEV-16-1:2.question: On the Day of Atonement, what animals did Aaron bring for his own sin offering and for his burnt offering?
written:LEV-16-1:2.answer: A young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering

written:LEV-16-1:4.question: On the Day of Atonement, what did Aaron do over the head of the live goat before it was sent into the wilderness?
written:LEV-16-1:4.answer: He laid both hands on it and confessed all Israel's iniquities
written:LEV-16-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LEV-16-1:6.question: What did the LORD command Israel to do on the tenth day of the seventh month, along with resting from work?
written:LEV-16-1:6.why: also right: A: Leviticus 25:9 separately commands trumpet blasts on the Day of Atonement, so option A is arguably also commanded elsewhere in Scripture, though this section does not mention it. D is the answer this section states.

written:LEV-19-19:5.question: In Leviticus 19, what will happen to the land if a man defiles his daughter by making her a prostitute?
written:LEV-19-19:5.answer: The land will be prostituted and filled with depravity
written:LEV-19-19:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-20-1:1.question: In Leviticus 20, what is to happen to an Israelite or foreigner living in Israel who gives any of his children to Molech?
written:LEV-20-1:1.answer: He must be put to death; the people of the land stone him

written:LEV-21-1:2.question: In Leviticus 21, what reason does the LORD give for why priests must be holy?
written:LEV-21-1:2.answer: They present the LORD's offerings made by fire, the food of their God

written:LEV-21-1:3.question: According to the LORD's instructions in Leviticus 21, what three things must priests not do to their bodies?
written:LEV-21-1:3.answer: Make bald spots on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or cut their bodies

written:LEV-21-1:4.question: Under the LORD's commands in Leviticus 21, what kind of woman may an ordinary priest not marry?
written:LEV-21-1:4.answer: A woman defiled by prostitution or divorced by her husband
written:LEV-21-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LEV-22-1:5.question: In Leviticus 22, which slaves of a priest may eat his food?
written:LEV-22-1:5.answer: One he bought with his own money or one born in his household

written:LEV-22-1:7.question: In Leviticus 22, what must a person do who eats a sacred offering in error?
written:LEV-22-1:7.answer: Add a fifth to its value and give the offering to the priest

written:LEV-23-15:2.question: In Leviticus 23, what were the Israelites told to leave at the edges of their fields and not gather when they reaped the harvest of their land?
written:LEV-23-15:2.answer: The edges of the field and the gleanings, for the poor and the foreign resident

written:LEV-25-23:1.question: In the law of redemption in Leviticus 25, why did God say the land must not be sold permanently?
written:LEV-25-23:1.answer: Because the land is God's, and Israel are foreigners and residents with Him

written:LEV-25-39:2.question: According to Leviticus 25, until what time does a destitute Israelite who sold himself work for his master, after which he and his children go free?
written:LEV-25-39:2.why: also right: C: Leviticus 25:40 names the Year of Jubilee. Exodus 21:2 and Deuteronomy 15:12 give a seventh-year release for Hebrew servants, so C is true elsewhere in Scripture; the question's 'according to Leviticus 25' points to A.

written:LEV-27-1:3.question: In Leviticus 27, what must a man do if he vows a person's value but is too poor to pay the valuation?
written:LEV-27-1:3.answer: Present the person before the priest, who sets the value by what he can afford

written:LEV-27-1:6.question: In Leviticus 27, how is a consecrated field's value set if the man consecrates it after the Year of Jubilee?
written:LEV-27-1:6.answer: The priest calculates the price by the years left until the next Jubilee

written:LEV-27-1:8.question: In Leviticus 27, what is the status of everything a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns?
written:LEV-27-1:8.answer: It cannot be sold or redeemed and is most holy to the LORD

written:NUM-5-11:7.question: After the priest read the oath and curses to the woman in Numbers 5, what was she to say?
written:NUM-5-11:7.why: also right: D: 5:22 gives the words exactly as "Amen, Amen." D is a paraphrase of what amen means, not the words the text specifies, so it is arguable but not the stated answer. Also, the text has the priest speaking the oath and curses (5:19-22), not reading them from a scroll; the scroll comes later (5:23).

written:NUM-5-11:8.question: According to Numbers 5, how did the priest put the curses into the bitter water?
written:NUM-5-11:8.answer: He wrote them on a scroll and washed them off into the water

written:NUM-6-1:3.question: While keeping the Nazirite vow, a man must abstain from wine and from what else that comes from the grapevine?
written:NUM-6-1:3.answer: Fresh grapes, raisins, and even seeds or skins
written:NUM-6-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-6-1:4.question: Why was a Nazirite not to defile himself by going near even his father, mother, brother, or sister who had died?
written:NUM-6-1:4.answer: The crown of consecration to his God was upon his head
written:NUM-6-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-7-1:8.question: After Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, from where did he hear the voice speaking to him?
written:NUM-7-1:8.answer: From between the two cherubim above the mercy seat
written:NUM-7-1:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-8-5:8.question: According to the LORD in Numbers 8, when did He set apart every firstborn in Israel for Himself?
written:NUM-8-5:8.answer: The day He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt
written:NUM-8-5:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-10-11:6.question: When Moses invited Hobab to come with Israel, what reason did he give for asking him not to leave?
written:NUM-10-11:6.answer: Hobab knew where to camp in the wilderness and could serve as their eyes

written:NUM-10-11:8.question: After leaving the mountain of the LORD, what did the ark of the covenant do during a three-day journey?
written:NUM-10-11:8.answer: It traveled ahead of the people to seek a resting place for them

written:NUM-11-16:2.question: Why did the LORD tell Moses He would put some of the Spirit that was on Moses on the seventy elders?
written:NUM-11-16:2.answer: So they would help Moses bear the burden of the people
written:NUM-11-16:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-11-16:6.question: When Moses doubted that there could be enough meat, how did the LORD answer him?
written:NUM-11-16:6.why: not clear on its own: A and C say the same thing: Numbers 11:23 ("Is the LORD's hand shortened?") is rendered "arm too short" in NIV and "hand not strong enough" in paraphrase, so two choices match. B is from Genesis 18:14 / Jeremiah 32:17, not Numbers 11.

written:NUM-13-1:3.question: When the spies came to Hebron, which people's descendants did they find living there?
written:NUM-13-1:3.why: also right: A: Section settles it: Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai are 'the descendants of Anak' who dwelled in Hebron. Heth is also arguable from elsewhere: Genesis 23 has the sons of Heth (Hittites) at Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, so Hittites lived there too, though this section doesn't mention them.

written:NUM-14-1:3.question: When Joshua and Caleb heard the people's complaints, how did they show their distress?
written:NUM-14-1:3.why: also right: A: In this scene Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes (14:6); it was Moses and Aaron who fell facedown (14:5). Joshua does fall facedown in distress on another occasion (Josh 7:6), so A is not right for this scene but could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:NUM-14-13:2.question: In Moses' prayer in Numbers 14, what did he say the nations would claim if the LORD killed the people as one man?
written:NUM-14-13:2.answer: That the LORD was unable to bring them into the promised land
written:NUM-14-13:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-14-20:2.question: In Numbers 14, why did the LORD say He would bring Caleb into the land he had entered?
written:NUM-14-20:2.answer: Caleb had a different spirit and followed the LORD wholeheartedly
written:NUM-14-20:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-14-20:3.question: After the people's rebellion at Kadesh, what did the LORD say would become of the Israelites' children, whom the people had said would become plunder?
written:NUM-14-20:3.answer: He would bring them into the land, and they would enjoy it
written:NUM-14-20:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-14-20:4.question: In Numbers 14, how did the LORD explain the forty years the Israelites must bear their guilt?
written:NUM-14-20:4.answer: A year for each of the forty days they spied out the land

written:NUM-14-40:3.question: After the Israelites went up to the ridge of the hill country against Moses' warning, who came down and attacked them?
written:NUM-14-40:3.answer: The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country

written:NUM-15-1:1.question: In Numbers 15, when the LORD gave Moses laws about offerings, when were these offerings to begin to be presented?
written:NUM-15-1:1.answer: After they entered the land the LORD was giving them
written:NUM-15-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-15-1:3.question: In Numbers 15, what was to be presented along with a ram offering, besides the wine?
written:NUM-15-1:3.answer: A grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil

written:NUM-15-1:6.question: In Numbers 15, what did the LORD say about a foreigner residing among the Israelites who wanted to present an offering made by fire?
written:NUM-15-1:6.answer: He was to do exactly as the Israelites do
written:NUM-15-1:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-16-1:2.question: When Korah and his followers rebelled, what reason did they give for saying Moses and Aaron had taken too much upon themselves?
written:NUM-16-1:2.answer: Everyone in the congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst

written:NUM-16-28:2.question: In Numbers 16, what happened to the 250 men who were offering the incense?
written:NUM-16-28:2.answer: Fire came forth from the LORD and consumed them
written:NUM-16-28:2.why: also right: B: Verse 16:35 says fire from the LORD consumed the 250 incense offerers. Choice B is a conflation: the earth swallowed Korah's men and households (16:32-33), not the 250. Numbers 26:10 puts the earth and the fire in one sentence, and some readers identify the 250 with Korah's men, so B is flagged as arguable, though the section keeps the two groups distinct.

written:NUM-16-41:2.question: When the congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron, what appeared at the Tent of Meeting?
written:NUM-16-41:2.answer: The cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared
written:NUM-16-41:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-16-41:3.question: When the plague began among the Israelites, what did Moses tell Aaron to do to make atonement for the congregation?
written:NUM-16-41:3.answer: Take his censer with fire from the altar and incense, and go quickly

written:NUM-17-1:3.question: Where did Moses place the twelve staffs overnight, in front of the Testimony, in the account of Aaron’s staff?
written:NUM-17-1:3.answer: In the Tent of the Testimony

written:NUM-18-1:4.question: In Numbers 18, how did the LORD describe the Levites whom He had selected from the Israelites for Aaron?
written:NUM-18-1:4.answer: A gift to Aaron, dedicated to the LORD
written:NUM-18-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-19-11:5.question: When a person dies in a tent, according to Numbers 19, what else in the tent becomes unclean?
written:NUM-19-11:5.answer: Any open container without a lid fastened on it
written:NUM-19-11:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-20-14:2.question: In his message to the king of Edom, what did Moses say Israel would do to avoid damaging Edom's land while passing through?
written:NUM-20-14:2.answer: Stay on the King's Highway, not cutting through fields or vineyards or drinking from wells

written:NUM-20-14:3.question: When Israel asked to pass through Edom, how did Edom first answer?
written:NUM-20-14:3.answer: They would come out against Israel with the sword
written:NUM-20-14:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-20-22:1.question: At Mount Hor, why did the LORD say Aaron would not enter the land given to the Israelites?
written:NUM-20-22:1.answer: Because he and Moses rebelled against the LORD's command at the waters of Meribah

written:NUM-22-1:3.question: What request did King Balak of Moab send to Balaam at Pethor?
written:NUM-22-1:3.answer: To come and put a curse on Israel
written:NUM-22-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-22-22:1.question: In the story of Balaam and his donkey, what was the angel of the LORD holding in his hand when the donkey first saw him standing in the road?

written:NUM-22-22:4.question: According to the angel of the LORD, what would have happened to Balaam if the donkey had not turned away from the angel?
written:NUM-22-22:4.answer: The angel would have killed Balaam and let her live
written:NUM-22-22:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-22-22:5.question: After the angel of the LORD confronted him, what did the angel tell Balaam to do when Balaam offered to go back home?
written:NUM-22-22:5.answer: Go with the men, but speak only what the angel says
written:NUM-22-22:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-23-13:7.question: For the third attempt to curse Israel, to which place did Balak take Balaam?
written:NUM-23-13:7.why: the section does not settle it: Peor is the correct answer for the third attempt per the chronology in Numbers 22:41 (Bamoth-baal, then Pisgah, then Peor), but this section never numbers the attempts; it shows only Pisgah followed by Peor, so 'third' depends on text outside the section. No other option is right: Pisgah is a summit of the Nebo range, but that was the second site, not the third.

written:NUM-24-1:3.question: In Balaam's third oracle, to what does he compare Israel's dwellings that spread out, along with gardens beside a stream?
written:NUM-24-1:3.why: not clear on its own: Most English translations (ESV, KJV, NIV) say Israel's tents are like 'valleys that stretch out', and none of the choices says valleys. The NRSV renders the image as 'palm groves that stretch far away', which matches D, so the answer depends on the translation. The question should name the translation or the image.

written:NUM-25-1:2.question: After Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor at Shittim, what did the LORD tell Moses to do so that His fierce anger would turn away from Israel?
written:NUM-25-1:2.answer: Execute all the leaders of the people in broad daylight before the LORD

written:NUM-25-6:2.question: According to Numbers 25, how many people died in the plague against the Israelites at Peor?
written:NUM-25-6:2.why: also right: C: Numbers 25:9 gives 24,000. 1 Corinthians 10:8 gives 23,000 fell in one day, referring to this same Peor incident, so C could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture; the question's 'according to Numbers 25' wording makes D the answer.

written:NUM-26-12:2.question: In the Numbers 26 census, how many clans are listed for the tribe of Simeon, counting the Nemuelite, Jaminite, Jachinite, Zerahite and Shaulite clans?
written:NUM-26-12:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NUM-26-15:1.question: In the registration of Israel in Numbers 26, how many men were counted in the clans of Gad?
written:NUM-26-15:1.why: the section does not settle it: The section gives the Gadite registration as 40,500 but does not say the count was of men; the 'men' qualifier comes from the wider census context (Numbers 26:2), not this section alone. Choice A (32,500) is Ephraim's count in Numbers 26:37, not Gad's.

written:NUM-27-1:3.question: According to the LORD's ruling for the Israelites, to whom should a man's inheritance go if he dies and leaves no son?
written:NUM-27-1:3.why: not clear on its own: The question leaves out the condition 'and no daughter.' The ruling gives the inheritance to a daughter first, and to brothers only if there is no daughter, so D would be correct for a man with no children. Add 'and no daughter' to the question to make it one answer.

written:NUM-27-18:2.question: When Moses commissioned Joshua, how would Joshua learn the LORD's will, through Eleazar the priest?
written:NUM-27-18:2.answer: By the judgment of the Urim
written:NUM-27-18:2.why: also right: A: The text names the Urim, so C is the answer. A is arguable only because the Urim is often understood as a lot-casting device (cf. Prov. 16:33), though the text never mentions lots or a tent for this purpose.

written:NUM-31-25:5.question: In the count of the plunder taken from Midian, how many sheep were there?
written:NUM-31-25:5.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: Num 31:32 gives the total spoil as 675,000 sheep, but Num 31:36 gives the soldiers' half share as 337,500 sheep, so D is a defensible reading if 'the plunder' is taken as one half. Wording 'in total' would remove the ambiguity.

written:NUM-32-1:3.question: In Numbers 32, when Moses warned the Gadites and Reubenites, which earlier event did he compare their request to?
written:NUM-32-1:3.answer: The fathers discouraging Israel after seeing the land from the Valley of Eshcol

written:NUM-32-1:6.question: What did the Gadites and Reubenites promise to do for the other Israelites before returning to their own homes?
written:NUM-32-1:6.answer: Arm themselves and go ahead of Israel until every Israelite had his inheritance

written:NUM-32-1:8.question: Which kingdoms did Moses give to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh?
written:NUM-32-1:8.answer: The kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan

written:NUM-33-1:2.question: As the Israelites left Rameses, what were the Egyptians doing, according to Numbers 33?
written:NUM-33-1:2.answer: Burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down
written:NUM-33-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-33-50:1.question: In the LORD's instructions on the plains of Moab, what did He say would happen to the inhabitants of Canaan that the Israelites allowed to remain?
written:NUM-33-50:1.answer: They would become barbs in their eyes and thorns in their sides
written:NUM-33-50:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-35-1:4.question: How did the LORD say the number of cities each tribe gave to the Levites should be decided?
written:NUM-35-1:4.answer: In proportion to its inheritance: more from a larger tribe, less from a smaller one

written:DEU-4-1:1.question: In Deuteronomy 4, what did Moses say happened to those who followed Baal of Peor?
written:DEU-4-1:1.answer: The LORD destroyed them from among Israel
written:DEU-4-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-4-15:3.question: Why did Moses tell Israel he would not be crossing the Jordan into the good land?
written:DEU-4-15:3.answer: The LORD was angry with him on account of the people, and he must die in the land

written:DEU-4-15:4.question: According to Moses, what would happen to Israel if, after a long time in the land, they made an idol of any form?
written:DEU-4-15:4.answer: They would quickly perish from the land and be scattered among the peoples

written:DEU-4-32:4.question: In Deuteronomy 4, what did Moses say God would do to nations greater and mightier than Israel when He brought Israel into the land?
written:DEU-4-32:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-4-32:5.question: In Deuteronomy 4, why did Moses tell Israel to keep God's statutes and commandments?
written:DEU-4-32:5.answer: So that they and their children may prosper and live long in the land

written:DEU-7-1:1.question: In Moses' instructions about the seven nations in Canaan, what did God tell Israel not to do with their daughters and sons regarding those nations?
written:DEU-7-1:1.answer: Do not give daughters to their sons or take their daughters for sons

written:DEU-7-1:2.question: In Deuteronomy 7, why did Moses say the LORD set His affection on Israel and chose them?
written:DEU-7-1:2.answer: Because the LORD loved them and kept the oath He swore to their fathers

written:DEU-7-1:3.question: In Deuteronomy 7, what did Moses say Israel must do to the altars, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles of the nations in Canaan?
written:DEU-7-1:3.answer: Tear down the altars, smash the pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles

written:DEU-10-12:2.question: In Deuteronomy 10, how many members of Israel's family went down to Egypt, according to Moses?
written:DEU-10-12:2.why: also right: D: Deut 10:22 says seventy, but Acts 7:14 (Stephen) gives seventy-five for Jacob's household that went down to Egypt, so D is also supported elsewhere in Scripture. The question's 'according to Moses' wording points to A.

written:DEU-11-8:1.question: In Moses' words about the land Israel was entering, how did the land of Egypt differ from the land across the Jordan in the way it was watered?
written:DEU-11-8:1.answer: In Egypt they irrigated on foot; Canaan drinks in rain from heaven
written:DEU-11-8:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-11-8:2.question: In Moses' address to Israel in Deuteronomy 11, what did the LORD promise to provide in season if they carefully obeyed His commandments?
written:DEU-11-8:2.answer: The autumn and spring rains, so they could gather grain, new wine, and oil

written:DEU-11-8:3.question: In Deuteronomy 11, what did Moses warn would happen if Israel turned aside to worship and bow down to other gods?
written:DEU-11-8:3.answer: The LORD would shut the heavens so there would be no rain
written:DEU-11-8:3.why: also right: D: Deuteronomy 11:17 says the LORD would shut the heavens so there would be no rain. D is not stated in this section, but Deuteronomy 28:38-42 lists locusts consuming the land's produce among the covenant curses for disobedience, which includes turning to other gods (28:14, 36, 64).

written:DEU-11-18:4.question: If the Israelites carefully kept God's commandments, what did Moses promise the LORD would do to the nations in the land?
written:DEU-11-18:4.answer: Drive them out before Israel, though greater and stronger
written:DEU-11-18:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-12-1:3.question: According to Moses in Deuteronomy 12, where were Israel to bring their burnt offerings and sacrifices?
written:DEU-12-1:3.answer: The place the LORD would choose as a dwelling for His Name
written:DEU-12-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-12-1:4.question: In Deuteronomy 12, Moses said Israel must not do "as we are doing here today." What did he say was happening then?
written:DEU-12-1:4.answer: Everyone does what seems right in his own eyes
written:DEU-12-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-12-1:7.question: In Deuteronomy 12, what did Moses say Israel could do if the chosen place was too far away?
written:DEU-12-1:7.answer: Slaughter animals and eat the meat within their own gates
written:DEU-12-1:7.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-13-1:4.question: In Deuteronomy 13, how was a person who secretly enticed someone to worship other gods to be put to death?
written:DEU-13-1:4.answer: By stoning, with the enticed person's hand first against him
written:DEU-13-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-13-12:2.question: In Deuteronomy 13, what was to be done with the plunder of an idolatrous city that Israel destroyed?
written:DEU-13-12:2.answer: Gather it in the public square and burn it completely
written:DEU-13-12:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-15-7:2.question: In Deuteronomy 15, what will the LORD do for an Israelite who gives generously to a poor brother without a grieved heart?
written:DEU-15-7:2.answer: Bless him in all his work and everything he puts his hand to

written:DEU-18-1:1.question: In Deuteronomy 18, what does Moses say is the inheritance of the tribe of Levi, as the LORD promised them?
written:DEU-18-1:1.answer: The LORD Himself, along with the offerings made by fire
written:DEU-18-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-18-1:2.question: In Deuteronomy 18, which portions of a bull or sheep sacrifice are the people to give to the priests?
written:DEU-18-1:2.answer: The shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach
written:DEU-18-1:2.why: also right: A: Choice A (breast and right thigh) is the priests' portion from peace offerings in Leviticus 7:30-34 and 10:14-15, so it is also true elsewhere in Scripture. Deuteronomy 18:3 specifically names the shoulder, jowls, and stomach, so C is the answer the section shows.

written:DEU-18-9:1.question: In Deuteronomy 18, why does the LORD say He is driving out the nations before Israel as they enter the land?
written:DEU-18-9:1.answer: Because of their detestable practices, such as sorcery and divination
written:DEU-18-9:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-18-15:1.question: In Deuteronomy 18, Moses says the LORD will raise up a prophet like him. From among whom will this prophet come?
written:DEU-18-15:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-18-15:2.question: At Horeb on the day of the assembly, what did the people ask of the LORD, which He said they had spoken well?
written:DEU-18-15:2.answer: Not to hear His voice or see the great fire anymore
written:DEU-18-15:2.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: Deuteronomy 18:16-17 matches exactly: at Horeb 'in the day of the assembly' the people asked not to hear the LORD's voice or see the great fire again, and the LORD said they 'have well spoken.' B is a weaker alternative: Deuteronomy 5:27-28 also has the LORD saying they 'have well said' about their request for Moses to go near and hear, but that passage does not use the 'day of the assembly' wording.

written:DEU-18-15:3.question: According to Moses, how can the people recognize a message that the LORD has not spoken?
written:DEU-18-15:3.answer: The prophet speaks in the LORD's name, but the message does not come true

written:DEU-20-1:2.question: According to Deuteronomy 20, why should Israel not be afraid when facing horses, chariots, and a larger army?
written:DEU-20-1:2.answer: The LORD their God, who brought them out of Egypt, is with them

written:DEU-20-1:7.question: In Deuteronomy 20, what was to happen to the people of a distant city that accepted Israel's offer of peace and opened its gates?
written:DEU-20-1:7.answer: They would become forced laborers serving Israel
written:DEU-20-1:7.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-21-1:3.question: In the ritual for an unsolved murder in Deuteronomy 21, what must the heifer be like?
written:DEU-21-1:3.answer: One that has never been yoked or used for work
written:DEU-21-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-21-1:4.question: In Deuteronomy 21, after the elders wash their hands over the heifer, what do they declare?
written:DEU-21-1:4.answer: “Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it.”

written:DEU-23-1:1.question: In Deuteronomy 23, why were Ammonites and Moabites barred from the assembly of the LORD, besides hiring Balaam to curse Israel?
written:DEU-23-1:1.answer: They did not meet Israel with food and water on the way out of Egypt

written:DEU-23-1:2.question: When Balaam son of Beor was hired to curse Israel, what did the LORD do, according to Moses?
written:DEU-23-1:2.answer: He turned the curse into a blessing for Israel
written:DEU-23-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-24-6:2.question: In Moses' laws about infectious skin diseases, which past event involving Miriam were the Israelites told to remember?
written:DEU-24-6:2.answer: What the LORD their God did to Miriam on the journey after leaving Egypt

written:DEU-30-1:1.question: In Moses' promise of restoration in Deuteronomy 30, what will the LORD do to the hearts of the people and their descendants so that they love Him?
written:DEU-30-1:1.why: also right: B: Verse 6 says the LORD will circumcise their hearts. B is not the answer given here, but Hebrews 10:22 speaks of hearts sprinkled clean and bodies washed with pure water, so it is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:DEU-30-1:5.question: In Deuteronomy 30, with how much of themselves must the people turn to the LORD and obey Him?
written:DEU-30-1:5.answer: With all their heart and all their soul
written:DEU-30-1:5.why: also right: C: Verse 2 and verse 10 say 'with all your heart and all your soul,' so B is the answer. C is not in this section, but Luke 10:27 and Mark 12:30 list mind and strength alongside heart and soul when describing love for God, so it is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:DEU-30-11:4.question: In Deuteronomy 30, what did Moses declare would happen if Israel's heart turned away and they bowed down to other gods?
written:DEU-30-11:4.answer: They would surely perish and not prolong their days in the land
written:DEU-30-11:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-31-14:3.question: What did the LORD say Israel would do after Moses rested with his fathers and they entered the land?
written:DEU-31-14:3.answer: Forsake Him and break His covenant by following foreign gods
written:DEU-31-14:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-31-14:4.question: What did the LORD tell Moses to do with the song, so that it would be a witness against Israel?
written:DEU-31-14:4.answer: Write it down and teach it to the Israelites
written:DEU-31-14:4.why: not clear on its own: "The song" is never identified in the question, so a quiz-taker cannot tell which song is meant. Reword to name it, e.g., "the song the LORD gave Moses in Deuteronomy 31" or "the Song of Moses." Bible answer is B (Deut. 31:19), since the law book goes beside the ark (31:26), not the song.

written:DEU-31-14:6.question: When the LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun, what reason did He give for Joshua to be strong and courageous?
written:DEU-31-14:6.answer: Joshua would bring the Israelites into the land, and the LORD would be with him

written:DEU-31-24:2.question: According to Moses in Deuteronomy 31, for what purpose was the Book of the Law to be placed beside the ark of the covenant?
written:DEU-31-24:2.answer: To remain there as a witness against Israel
written:DEU-31-24:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-32-48:2.question: According to the LORD's words to Moses on Mount Nebo, why would Moses and Aaron not enter the land of Canaan?
written:DEU-32-48:2.answer: They broke faith with Him at Meribah-kadesh by failing to treat Him as holy

written:DEU-33-1:2.question: In his blessing of Levi, what did Moses say Levi would teach to Jacob and Israel?
written:DEU-33-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-33-1:4.question: In Moses' blessing of Joseph, whose favor did he ask to rest on Joseph's head?
written:DEU-33-1:4.answer: Him who dwelt in the burning bush
written:DEU-33-1:4.why: also right: A, C: The section names 'Him who dwelt in the burning bush' (33:16), so B is the answer. A and C also refer to the LORD: the section says the LORD came from Sinai (33:2), and Psalm 18:10 says He rode on a cherub. Both describe the same God, so a strict reader could argue for them. D (Peniel) is a figure Hosea 12:4 calls an angel, so it is weaker.

written:JOS-3-1:3.question: At the Jordan, why did the LORD say He would begin to exalt Joshua in the sight of all Israel?
written:JOS-3-1:3.answer: So they would know He was with Joshua as He was with Moses

written:JOS-4-1:4.question: According to Joshua, what were the children to be told about why the Jordan's waters were cut off?
written:JOS-4-1:4.answer: They were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD

written:JOS-4-1:8.question: What happened to the waters of the Jordan when the priests carrying the ark came up and their feet touched the dry land?
written:JOS-4-1:8.answer: The waters returned to their course and overflowed all the banks as before

written:JOS-6-1:3.question: Before the seventh day at Jericho, what did Joshua command the people not to do while marching?
written:JOS-6-1:3.answer: Give a battle cry or let their voice be heard
written:JOS-6-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-6-1:5.question: What oath did Joshua make at that time about anyone who would rebuild Jericho?
written:JOS-6-1:5.answer: The man who rebuilds it would be cursed at the cost of his sons

written:JOS-7-1:5.question: In the LORD's instructions to find the guilty one in Israel, how was the one caught with the devoted things to be punished?
written:JOS-7-1:5.answer: He must be burned, along with all that belongs to him
written:JOS-7-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-7-16:2.question: When Joshua urged Achan to confess, what did he tell him to give to the LORD, the God of Israel?
written:JOS-7-16:2.why: also right: A: The text says 'give glory,' but 'honor' is a near synonym and could be argued for as a loose paraphrase; the section's wording favors C.

written:JOS-8-1:3.question: How many mighty men of valor did Joshua choose and send out at night to lie in ambush against Ai?
written:JOS-8-1:3.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: Joshua 8:3 says he chose 30,000 mighty men of valor and sent them out by night (C). Joshua 8:12 later says he set about 5,000 men to ambush between Bethel and Ai, so D is arguable if a reader takes that as the ambush force rather than the full night detachment.

written:JOS-8-1:4.question: In Joshua's plan to take Ai, what were the main troops with him to do when the men of Ai came out against them?
written:JOS-8-1:4.answer: Flee from them as they did the first time
written:JOS-8-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-8-1:6.question: When the LORD told Joshua to hold out his battle lance toward Ai, what did the men in ambush do?
written:JOS-8-1:6.answer: They rose quickly, entered the city, captured it, and set it on fire

written:JOS-8-1:8.question: After Israel took Ai, what did Joshua do with the king of Ai's body at sunset?
written:JOS-8-1:8.answer: Had it thrown at the city gate entrance and covered with a large pile of rocks

written:JOS-9-1:4.question: After the Israelites learned that the Gibeonites were neighbors, why did they not attack the Gibeonite cities?
written:JOS-9-1:4.answer: The leaders had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel

written:JOS-9-1:5.question: What task did Joshua assign to the Gibeonites after the deception was discovered?
written:JOS-9-1:5.answer: Woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and the altar
written:JOS-9-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-9-1:6.question: When the Gibeonites explained to Joshua why they had deceived Israel, what did they say they feared?
written:JOS-9-1:6.answer: They feared for their lives because the LORD had commanded Moses to wipe out the land's inhabitants

written:JOS-10-1:3.question: When Joshua came to help Gibeon against the five Amorite kings, what did the LORD tell him?
written:JOS-10-1:3.answer: "Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand."

written:JOS-10-16:2.question: When Joshua learned that the five kings were hiding in the cave at Makkedah, what did he order done at the cave?
written:JOS-10-16:2.answer: Roll large stones against its mouth and post men to guard it
written:JOS-10-16:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-13-1:3.question: In Joshua 13, what did the LORD promise to do to the Sidonians and the other inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim?
written:JOS-13-1:3.answer: He Himself would drive them out before the Israelites
written:JOS-13-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOS-13-29:1.question: In Joshua 13, what does the text say was the inheritance of the tribe of Levi, since Moses gave them no land?
written:JOS-13-29:1.answer: The LORD, the God of Israel

written:JOS-16-1:4.question: In Joshua 16, where did the border of the Ephraimites' inheritance end on the east, after it reached Jericho?
written:JOS-16-1:4.why: not clear on its own: The question's wording is muddled: Joshua 16:1 says the Joseph lot extends from the Jordan at Jericho (where it starts, not where it ends), and 16:5 describes Ephraim's eastern boundary as running to Upper Beth-horon. Both C and D can be defended, so the question needs rewording.

written:JOS-17-1:2.question: How many daughters did Zelophehad son of Hepher have, who asked for an inheritance in the land?
written:JOS-17-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOS-17-1:5.question: Besides Eleazar the priest and the leaders, to whom did the daughters of Zelophehad bring their request for an inheritance?
written:JOS-17-1:5.why: also right: A: The section names only Joshua as the other party, so D is settled by the text. But Numbers 27:1-5 says the daughters first approached Moses, Eleazar, the leaders, and the congregation, so Moses is also right from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOS-19-40:1.question: In Joshua 19, after the territory of the Danites was lost to them, which city did the Danites go up and fight against, capture, and settle?
written:JOS-19-40:1.why: also right: D: The section names Leshem directly. Judges 18:29 identifies the same city as Laish, which the Danites renamed Dan, so D is also defensible as another name for the same place.

written:JOS-19-49:1.question: After the Israelites finished distributing the land, which city in the hill country of Ephraim did they give Joshua son of Nun as his inheritance?
written:JOS-19-49:1.why: also right: C: Joshua 19:50 names Timnath-serah. Judges 2:9 and some Joshua manuscripts call the same city Timnath-heres, so C is another name for the same place elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOS-22-1:3.question: When Joshua sent the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh home, which command of Moses did he urge them to be very careful to observe?
written:JOS-22-1:3.answer: To love the LORD, walk in His ways, and serve Him with all their heart

written:JOS-22-9:2.question: Whom did the Israelites send to the land of Gilead to confront the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh about their altar?
written:JOS-22-9:2.answer: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, with ten chiefs
written:JOS-22-9:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-22-9:5.question: What did the delegation suggest the eastern tribes do if their own land of inheritance was unclean?
written:JOS-22-9:5.answer: Cross over to the LORD’s land, where His tabernacle stands, and take possession

written:JOS-22-9:6.question: When the eastern tribes explained their altar by the Jordan, what did they say it was meant to be?
written:JOS-22-9:6.answer: A witness between them and the Israelites to come
written:JOS-22-9:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOS-23-1:4.question: In Joshua 23, which of these did Joshua forbid Israel to do with the gods of the nations that remained?
written:JOS-23-1:4.answer: Call on their names or swear by them

written:2SA-16-1:3.answer: The house of Israel would restore to him the kingdom of his grandfather

written:2SA-16-5:3.question: When Abishai wanted to kill Shimei, why did David say Shimei should be left alone to curse him?
written:2SA-16-5:3.answer: Because the LORD had told Shimei to curse David
written:2SA-16-5:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2SA-16-15:2.question: In Jerusalem, what advice did Ahithophel give Absalom to do with his father's concubines?
written:2SA-16-15:2.answer: Sleep with them, so all Israel would hear he had become a stench to his father

written:2SA-17-1:6.question: According to 2 Samuel 17:14, why did Absalom and the men of Israel prefer Hushai's advice to Ahithophel's?
written:2SA-17-1:6.answer: The LORD had purposed to thwart Ahithophel's good counsel to bring disaster on Absalom.

written:2SA-17-15:3.question: After Hushai told the priests Zadok and Abiathar what advice had been given, what message did he tell them to send quickly to David?
written:2SA-17-15:3.answer: Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but cross over

written:2SA-18-19:5.question: When the watchman saw a man running alone, what did King David say?
written:2SA-18-19:5.answer: "If he is alone, he bears good news."
written:2SA-18-19:5.why: a quotation not word for word in the BSB text

written:2SA-19-8:4.question: What position did David promise Amasa in place of Joab if he did not become commander of his army?

written:2SA-19-31:4.question: When Barzillai declined to go to Jerusalem with David, where did he say he wanted to die?
written:2SA-19-31:4.answer: In his own city, near his parents' tomb
written:2SA-19-31:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-20-1:1.question: When Sheba son of Bichri blew the ram’s horn and called Israel to rebel against David, which tribe was Sheba from?
written:2SA-20-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2SA-20-1:3.question: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem after Sheba's revolt began, what did he do with the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace?
written:2SA-20-1:3.answer: He placed them in a house under guard and provided for them
written:2SA-20-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-20-1:5.question: At the great stone in Gibeon, how did Joab kill Amasa?
written:2SA-20-1:5.answer: He stabbed him in the stomach with a dagger while greeting him
written:2SA-20-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-20-1:6.question: When Joab besieged Abel-beth-maacah, how was the city saved from destruction?
written:2SA-20-1:6.answer: The people cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab over the wall

written:2SA-21-1:5.question: When David handed over Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites, why did he spare Mephibosheth son of Jonathan?
written:2SA-21-1:5.answer: Because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan
written:2SA-21-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-21-15:4.question: At the battle at Gath, who killed the giant with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot after he taunted Israel?
written:2SA-21-15:4.answer: Jonathan the son of David's brother Shimei
written:2SA-21-15:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-22-1:3.question: In David's song, what did the LORD draw David out of when He reached down from on high and took hold of him?
written:2SA-22-1:3.why: also right: C: Psalm 40:2, also by David, says the LORD lifted him out of a miry bog. That is not part of this song, which says deep waters (22:17).

written:2SA-22-1:5.question: In David's song, what does David say the LORD is to him, as he speaks of darkness?
written:2SA-22-1:5.answer: His lamp, who lights up his darkness
written:2SA-22-1:5.why: also right: B: The song says the LORD is his lamp (22:29). Psalm 23, also by David, calls the LORD his shepherd who leads him through the valley of the shadow, so B is a stretch but arguable.

written:2SA-22-1:6.question: In David's song, how does David describe the word of the LORD?
written:2SA-22-1:6.why: also right: A, C, D: The song says the word is flawless (22:31). Elsewhere the word is called two-edged (Heb 4:12), sweeter than honey (Ps 19:10; 119:103), and hidden in the heart (Ps 119:11), though David does not say these in this song.

written:2SA-23-1:1.question: In David's last words in 2 Samuel 23, what does David say the Spirit of the LORD did?
written:2SA-23-1:1.answer: Spoke through him, with His word on David's tongue
written:2SA-23-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2SA-23-1:2.question: In David's last words, what is the ruler who rules the people with justice, in the fear of God, compared to?
written:2SA-23-1:2.answer: The light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn
written:2SA-23-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-23-8:1.question: When Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the Three, wielded his spear at one time, how many men did he kill?
written:2SA-23-8:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: 2 Samuel 23:8 (the source of the spelling "Josheb-basshebeth" and "Tahchemonite") says he wielded his spear against 800 men and killed them at one time. The parallel in 1 Chronicles 11:11 ("Jashobeam") gives 300, so B is right in that account.

written:2SA-23-8:5.question: Why did David say he could not drink the water the three mighty men brought him from the well at Bethlehem?
written:2SA-23-8:5.answer: It was the blood of the men who risked their lives
written:2SA-23-8:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-23-8:7.question: Which exploit is told of Benaiah son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel?
written:2SA-23-8:7.answer: On a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion

written:2SA-24-10:2.question: When the prophet Gad offered David a choice of judgments for the census, which was one of the three options?
written:2SA-24-10:2.answer: Three days of plague upon the land
written:2SA-24-10:2.why: also right: D: The BSB offer is three years of famine, not seven. D is not an option here, but the Septuagint reads 'seven years' at 2 Samuel 24:13, and a seven-year famine occurs elsewhere (2 Samuel 21:1), so a strict reader could raise it. The BSB text settles C.

written:2SA-24-18:2.question: When David went to Araunah's threshing floor, why did he say he wanted to buy it?
written:2SA-24-18:2.answer: To build an altar to the LORD so the plague would be halted

written:2SA-24-18:3.question: When Araunah offered to give David the oxen and the threshing floor for free, what reason did David give for insisting on paying?
written:2SA-24-18:3.answer: He would not offer burnt offerings to the LORD that cost him nothing

written:2SA-24-18:4.question: How much did David pay for Araunah's threshing floor and oxen?
written:2SA-24-18:4.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: C: 2 Samuel 24:24 gives fifty shekels of silver for the threshing floor and oxen. 1 Chronicles 21:25 gives six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place, so a reader who blends the two accounts could argue C, but the question's wording matches 2 Samuel.

written:1KI-1-11:2.question: When Nathan advised Bathsheba how to approach King David, what did he tell her to remind David that he had sworn?
written:1KI-1-11:2.answer: That her son Solomon would reign after him and sit on his throne

written:1KI-1-41:2.question: Who arrived at Adonijah's feast and told him that King David had made Solomon king?
written:1KI-1-41:2.answer: Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest
written:1KI-1-41:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-2-1:2.question: In David's charge to Solomon, what did David say Solomon must do so that he would prosper in all he did?
written:1KI-2-1:2.answer: Keep the charge of the LORD and walk in His ways
written:1KI-2-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-2-1:3.question: According to the promise David quoted to Solomon, what would the LORD give if David's descendants walked faithfully before Him with all their heart and soul?
written:1KI-2-1:3.answer: Never failing to have a man on the throne of Israel
written:1KI-2-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-2-1:5.question: In David's charge to Solomon, why did David say the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite should eat at Solomon's table?
written:1KI-2-1:5.answer: They stood by David when he fled from Absalom
written:1KI-2-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-2-13:3.question: When Adonijah spoke with Bathsheba, what reason did he give for the kingship having turned to Solomon?
written:1KI-2-13:3.answer: It had come to Solomon from the LORD
written:1KI-2-13:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-2-13:4.question: When Bathsheba came to King Solomon, how did he honor her?
written:1KI-2-13:4.answer: He bowed to her and had a throne brought for her at his right hand

written:1KI-4-20:1.question: In 1 Kings 4, how many stalls did Solomon have for his chariot horses?
written:1KI-4-20:1.why: picked C without the text, not the writer's A: 1 Kings 4:26 (Hebrew text) gives 40,000 stalls. Parallel 2 Chronicles 9:25 gives 4,000, and some textual traditions (e.g., the Septuagint) read 4,000 in 1 Kings, so A is arguable, though C is the standard reading of 1 Kings 4.

written:1KI-5-7:1.question: When Hiram, King of Tyre, received Solomon's message about building the temple, how did he react?
written:1KI-5-7:1.answer: He rejoiced greatly and blessed the LORD for giving David a wise son

written:1KI-7-1:2.question: In Solomon's palace complex, what was the Hall of Justice built for?
written:1KI-7-1:2.answer: The throne, where Solomon was to judge
written:1KI-7-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-7-13:2.question: In 1 Kings 7, from which tribe did the mother of the bronze craftsman Huram come?
written:1KI-7-13:2.why: also right: B: 2 Chronicles 2:14 says Huram's mother was 'of the daughters of Dan,' so Dan is also argued from elsewhere in Scripture; this section explicitly says Naphtali.

written:1KI-7-23:2.question: In 1 Kings 7, how many baths could the Sea of cast metal hold?
written:1KI-7-23:2.why: also right: A: 2 Chronicles 4:5 says the Sea held three thousand baths, so A could fairly be argued from elsewhere in Scripture; the question is scoped to 1 Kings 7, where the section says two thousand.

written:1KI-7-48:1.question: In Solomon's temple, how many lampstands of pure gold stood in front of the inner sanctuary, on the right side and the left side together?
written:1KI-7-48:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-8-12:3.question: According to Solomon, what had the LORD not done since the day He brought Israel out of Egypt, until choosing David?
written:1KI-8-12:3.answer: Chosen a city from any tribe to build a house for His Name

written:1KI-8-22:1.question: In his prayer of dedication, what did Solomon say about God compared with other gods, as he stood before the altar?
written:1KI-8-22:1.answer: There is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below

written:1KI-8-22:6.question: In Solomon's prayer, what result did he ask for among all the peoples of the earth when God answers the foreigner who prays toward the temple?
written:1KI-8-22:6.answer: They will know God's name and fear Him, as Israel does
written:1KI-8-22:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-8-54:4.question: According to Solomon's blessing, why did he ask that his petition be near the LORD day and night, upholding the cause of Israel?
written:1KI-8-54:4.answer: So all the peoples of the earth may know the LORD is God

written:1KI-8-62:2.question: At the dedication of the temple, why did Solomon consecrate the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD to offer the sacrifices?
written:1KI-8-62:2.answer: The bronze altar was too small to hold all the offerings.
written:1KI-8-62:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-9-1:5.question: What did the LORD say He would do to Israel if Solomon or his sons turned away to serve and worship other gods?
written:1KI-9-1:5.answer: Cut Israel off from the land He had given them
written:1KI-9-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-9-10:2.question: Why did King Solomon give twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre?
written:1KI-9-10:2.answer: Hiram had supplied him with cedar, cypress, and gold
written:1KI-9-10:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-9-10:4.question: Whom did Solomon conscript as forced laborers from among the people living in the land?
written:1KI-9-10:4.answer: The remaining descendants of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
written:1KI-9-10:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-9-10:6.question: How many supervisors were chief officers over the people who did Solomon's work?
written:1KI-9-10:6.why: not clear on its own: 1 Kings 9:23 gives 550 chief officers over the workers, but 2 Chronicles 8:10 gives 250 chief officers who ruled over the people. The question does not say which account it means, so it has two right answers.

written:1KI-11-9:2.question: When the LORD told Solomon He would tear the kingdom away, what did He say He would do for the sake of David during Solomon's lifetime?
written:1KI-11-9:2.answer: He would not tear the kingdom away in Solomon's lifetime
written:1KI-11-9:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-12-1:3.question: When Jeroboam and the assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam, what did they ask him to lighten?
written:1KI-12-1:3.answer: The heavy yoke and burden of his father’s service
written:1KI-12-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-12-1:5.question: What advice did the elders who had served Solomon give Rehoboam about answering the people?
written:1KI-12-1:5.answer: Be a servant to them and speak kind words
written:1KI-12-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-12-1:7.question: According to 1 Kings 12:15, why did Rehoboam not listen to the people?
written:1KI-12-1:7.answer: The turn of events was from the LORD, fulfilling His word through Ahijah

written:1KI-13-1:6.question: Why did the man of God from Judah refuse to eat bread or drink water at Bethel?
written:1KI-13-1:6.answer: The LORD had commanded him not to eat or drink there or return the way he came

written:1KI-13-11:2.question: When the old prophet of Bethel persuaded the man of God from Judah to come home with him, what false claim did he make?
written:1KI-13-11:2.answer: That an angel had told him by the word of the LORD to bring him back

written:1KI-13-11:5.question: After the lion killed the man of God from Judah, what was unusual about the lion and the donkey standing by his body?
written:1KI-13-11:5.answer: The lion had not eaten the body or mauled the donkey
written:1KI-13-11:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1KI-13-11:7.question: Why did the old prophet tell his sons to lay his bones beside the bones of the man of God?
written:1KI-13-11:7.answer: The man of God's message against the altar and the high places would surely come to pass

written:1KI-14-1:4.question: According to Ahijah in 1 Kings 14, why was Jeroboam's son the only one of his house to receive a proper burial?
written:1KI-14-1:4.answer: Only in him had the LORD found any good in Jeroboam's house

written:1KI-14-19:1.question: How many years did Jeroboam reign over Israel before he rested with his fathers?
written:1KI-14-19:1.why: not clear on its own: Ambiguous: two kings named Jeroboam over Israel both 'slept with their fathers.' Jeroboam I (son of Nebat) reigned 22 years (1 Kings 14:20, D); Jeroboam II reigned 41 years (2 Kings 14:23, C). The question should name which Jeroboam.

written:1KI-14-25:2.question: When Shishak attacked Jerusalem in Rehoboam's reign, which items made by Solomon did he take along with the treasures of the LORD's house and the palace?
written:1KI-14-25:2.why: also right: A: The section names only the gold shields, but 'He took everything' could arguably cover Solomon's golden lampstands in the house of the LORD, which the text never names.

written:1KI-18-1:5.question: Why was Obadiah afraid to tell Ahab that Elijah was there?
written:1KI-18-1:5.answer: The Spirit of the LORD might carry Elijah away, and Ahab would kill him

written:1KI-20-1:3.question: When Ben-hadad's messengers returned a second time, what did they say his servants would do the next day?
written:1KI-20-1:3.answer: Search Ahab's palace and his servants' houses and carry away all that was precious

written:1KI-20-1:5.question: When Ben-hadad threatened that there would not be enough dust in Samaria for each of his men to have a handful, how did Ahab reply?
written:1KI-20-1:5.answer: “The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.”

written:1KI-20-26:1.question: In 1 Kings 20, why did the man of God say the LORD would hand the great Aramean army over to the king of Israel?
written:1KI-20-26:1.answer: The Arameans thought the LORD was a god of the hills, not the valleys

written:1KI-20-35:4.question: In the story the disguised prophet told King Ahab, what penalty was he warned of if the captive went missing?
written:1KI-20-35:4.answer: His life for the man's life, or a talent of silver

written:1KI-20-35:5.question: What message did the prophet give Ahab from the LORD after removing his bandage?
written:1KI-20-35:5.answer: Ahab's life would be exchanged for Ben-hadad's life, and his people for Ben-hadad's people

written:1KI-21-17:2.question: In the LORD's message through Elijah about Ahab's murder of Naboth, what was to happen to Ahab in the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood?
written:1KI-21-17:2.answer: The dogs would lick up Ahab's blood there too
written:1KI-21-17:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-21-17:3.question: When Elijah met Ahab in Naboth's vineyard, why did Elijah say he had found Ahab out?
written:1KI-21-17:3.answer: Ahab had sold himself to do evil in the sight of the LORD

written:1KI-21-25:2.question: After Ahab humbled himself, what did the LORD tell Elijah the Tishbite He would do about the calamity coming on Ahab's house?
written:1KI-21-25:2.answer: Not bring it in Ahab's days, but in his son's days

written:1KI-22-1:3.question: Why did Ahab say he hated the prophet Micaiah son of Imlah?
written:1KI-22-1:3.answer: He never prophesies anything good for Ahab, only bad
written:1KI-22-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-22-29:2.question: What order did the king of Aram give his thirty-two chariot commanders before the battle at Ramoth-gilead?
written:1KI-22-29:2.answer: Fight no one except the king of Israel
written:1KI-22-29:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1KI-22-29:3.question: In the battle at Ramoth-gilead, how was King Ahab of Israel wounded?
written:1KI-22-29:3.answer: A man drew his bow without special aim and struck him between the joints of his armor

written:1KI-22-29:4.question: After Ahab died and was brought to Samaria, what happened when his chariot was washed at the pool of Samaria?
written:1KI-22-29:4.answer: The dogs licked up Ahab's blood, according to the word of the LORD

written:2KI-3-1:3.question: When the kings ran out of water, which prophet did Jehoshaphat ask for so they could inquire of the LORD?
written:2KI-3-1:3.why: also right: C: In this section Jehoshaphat asks for an unnamed prophet and the servant names Elisha, so D is settled by the text. Elsewhere (1 Kings 22:7-8) Jehoshaphat asks for Micaiah son of Imlah to inquire of the LORD, so C is true of a different episode.

written:2KI-4-8:3.question: What did Elisha promise the Shunammite woman as she stood in the doorway?
written:2KI-4-8:3.answer: At this time next year she would hold a son in her arms.

written:2KI-4-18:2.question: Where did the Shunammite woman lay her dead son before she shut the door and went out to find Elisha?
written:2KI-4-18:2.answer: On the bed of the man of God
written:2KI-4-18:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-4-18:5.question: When the Shunammite woman clung to Elisha's feet and Gehazi tried to push her away, why did Elisha say to leave her alone?
written:2KI-4-18:5.answer: Her soul was in deep distress, and the LORD had hidden it from him

written:2KI-5-15:3.question: What did Naaman promise he would never again do after being healed?
written:2KI-5-15:3.answer: Offer a burnt offering or sacrifice to any god but the LORD
written:2KI-5-15:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-5-15:6.question: What false story did Gehazi tell Naaman to get silver and clothing?
written:2KI-5-15:6.answer: Two young men from the sons of the prophets had come to Elisha

written:2KI-6-24:3.question: When a woman cried out “Help me, my lord the king!” as he passed by on the wall of Samaria, what did the king answer first?
written:2KI-6-24:3.answer: “If the LORD does not help you, where can I find help for you?”

written:2KI-6-24:4.question: In the woman’s complaint to the king of Israel during the siege of Samaria, why was she upset with the other woman?
written:2KI-6-24:4.answer: The other woman hid her son after they had eaten the first woman’s son

written:2KI-7-3:3.question: Why did the four men with leprosy decide to go over to the Aramean camp instead of entering the city?
written:2KI-7-3:3.answer: They would die of famine in the city, and also if they stayed where they were

written:2KI-7-3:7.question: When the king heard the lepers' report in the night, what did he think the Arameans had done?
written:2KI-7-3:7.answer: Left the camp to hide in the field and ambush the Israelites
written:2KI-7-3:7.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2KI-7-3:8.question: When the scouts followed the Aramean army, how far did they track them, and what did they find along the way?
written:2KI-7-3:8.answer: As far as the Jordan, with the road littered with clothing and equipment

written:2KI-7-16:3.question: When Elisha foretold cheap flour and barley, what did the king's officer say in reply?
written:2KI-7-16:3.answer: “Even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?”

written:2KI-8-1:3.question: When the woman returned after the famine and came to appeal to the king for her house and her land, whom was the king speaking with?
written:2KI-8-1:3.answer: Gehazi, the servant of the man of God
written:2KI-8-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-8-1:4.question: After the woman confirmed Gehazi's account of her son, what did the king command an officer to restore to her?
written:2KI-8-1:4.answer: All that was hers, with the proceeds of the field since she left

written:2KI-9-1:2.question: After Jehu was anointed at Ramoth-gilead, what did the commanders do when he told them what the young prophet had said?
written:2KI-9-1:2.answer: They put their garments under him on the bare steps and blew the ram’s horn

written:2KI-9-14:6.question: How did Jehu kill Joram king of Israel?
written:2KI-9-14:6.answer: He shot him between the shoulders with a bow, piercing his heart
written:2KI-9-14:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-9-14:7.question: Why did Jehu order Bidkar to throw Joram's body into the field of Naboth?
written:2KI-9-14:7.answer: To fulfill the LORD's word that He would repay Ahab on that plot

written:2KI-10-1:2.question: When Jehu told the leaders in Samaria to choose a son of Ahab as king and fight, why were they afraid to do it?
written:2KI-10-1:2.answer: They reasoned that if two kings could not stand against Jehu, they could not

written:2KI-10-1:4.question: After the heads of Ahab's sons arrived, what did Jehu order be done with them?
