written:2KI-10-1:4.answer: Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning

written:2KI-10-1:6.question: At Beth-eked of the Shepherds, whom did Jehu meet and then have taken alive and slaughtered, forty-two men in all?
written:2KI-10-1:6.answer: Relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah
written:2KI-10-1:6.why: also right: C: The section names them as relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah, so A is settled. C is arguable from outside the section: Ahaziah's mother Athaliah was Ahab's daughter, so Jehoram of Israel was her brother and the uncle of Ahaziah, which makes the men his kin too (2 Kgs 8:18, 26; 2 Chr 22:2). The section does not say this.

written:2KI-11-13:2.question: Why did Jehoiada the priest order that Athaliah be brought out between the ranks before she was put to death?
written:2KI-11-13:2.answer: She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD

written:2KI-12-1:6.question: How did Jehoiada the priest arrange to collect the money brought into the house of the LORD?
written:2KI-12-1:6.answer: He bored a hole in a chest's lid and set it beside the altar

written:2KI-12-17:1.question: When Hazael king of Aram decided to attack Jerusalem, what did King Joash of Judah do to make him withdraw?
written:2KI-12-17:1.answer: He sent Hazael the sacred objects and the gold from the temple and palace

written:2KI-14-1:2.question: After Amaziah of Judah executed his father's murderers, why did he not put their sons to death?
written:2KI-14-1:2.answer: He followed the command written in the Book of the Law of Moses

written:2KI-14-8:1.question: In Jehoash's message to Amaziah, what did the thistle in Lebanon ask of the cedar in Lebanon?
written:2KI-14-8:1.answer: That the cedar give its daughter to the thistle's son in marriage

written:2KI-14-17:2.question: After Amaziah of Judah was killed at Lachish, where was he buried?
written:2KI-14-17:2.answer: In Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David
written:2KI-14-17:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-16-1:2.question: To pay the king of Assyria for help, what did Ahaz send him as a gift?
written:2KI-16-1:2.answer: Silver and gold from the LORD's house and the king's treasuries

written:2KI-16-10:5.question: When King Ahaz changed the temple furnishings, what did he take down from the bronze oxen and put on a stone base?
written:2KI-16-10:5.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: The Sea (2 Kings 16:17) is itself a large bronze basin, so D could be argued; the question's 'from the bronze oxen' points to the Sea, so C is the intended answer.

written:2KI-17-24:4.question: How did the king of Assyria respond to the settlers' report about the lions in Samaria?
written:2KI-17-24:4.answer: He commanded that one of the exiled priests be sent back to teach them

written:2KI-19-20:5.question: According to the LORD's word through Isaiah, which of these would the king of Assyria NOT do against Jerusalem?
written:2KI-19-20:5.why: also right: D: The section explicitly says he will not shoot an arrow into the city (C). Choices A, B and D are not mentioned in this section either way. Elsewhere in Scripture Hezekiah is not carried off to Nineveh (D), so D is also true in the wider account; A and B are not recorded as Assyrian acts at all, and B is a deed Hezekiah himself did (2 Chr 32:3-4).

written:2KI-20-1:2.question: Besides adding years to Hezekiah's life, what else did the LORD promise Hezekiah in 2 Kings 20?
written:2KI-20-1:2.answer: To deliver him and Jerusalem from the king of Assyria
written:2KI-20-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2KI-20-12:1.question: Why did Merodach-baladan king of Babylon send letters and a gift to King Hezekiah of Judah?
written:2KI-20-12:1.answer: He had heard about Hezekiah’s illness
written:2KI-20-12:1.why: also right: C: C is not stated in 2 Kings 20, but 2 Chronicles 32:31 says the Babylonian envoys were sent to inquire about the sign that had happened in the land, which was the shadow going back (2 Kings 20:9-11). So C is supported elsewhere in Scripture, though this section gives illness as the stated reason.

written:2KI-20-12:4.question: When Isaiah told Hezekiah that the word of the LORD about Babylon was coming, how did Hezekiah respond?
written:2KI-20-12:4.answer: He said the word of the LORD was good, thinking of peace in his lifetime

written:2KI-22-14:1.question: In Huldah's message to King Josiah in 2 Kings 22, why did the LORD say the calamity would come on Jerusalem and its people?
written:2KI-22-14:1.answer: They forsook Him and burned incense to other gods
written:2KI-22-14:1.why: also right: C: B is the reason given in 22:17. C is not in this section, but elsewhere Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood is cited as a cause of Judah's judgment (2 Kings 21:16; 24:3-4), and 2 Chronicles 36:21 ties the exile to the land's unkept sabbaths, so C could fairly be argued.

written:2KI-23-1:2.question: After reading the Book of the Covenant, what did King Josiah do as he stood by the pillar before the LORD?
written:2KI-23-1:2.answer: He made a covenant to follow the LORD and keep His commandments
written:2KI-23-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-23-21:3.question: According to 2 Kings 23, what did Josiah say or do to carry out the words of the law found by Hilkiah the priest?
written:2KI-23-21:3.answer: He removed the mediums, spiritists, household gods, and idols from Judah and Jerusalem

written:2KI-23-31:3.question: What did Pharaoh Neco impose on Judah after he imprisoned Jehoahaz?
written:2KI-23-31:3.answer: A levy of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold

written:2KI-24-6:1.question: How old was Jehoiachin when he became king of Judah?
written:2KI-24-6:1.why: also right: C: 2 Kings 24:8 gives eighteen. 2 Chronicles 36:9 says Jehoiachin was eight years old, so C is also supported by another passage in Scripture. The section itself settles the answer as A.

written:1CH-3-10:1.question: In the list of Solomon's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3, who was Solomon's son and the first king named after him?
written:1CH-3-10:1.why: the section does not settle it: The section says Solomon's son was Rehoboam, but it never says he was a king or the first king after Solomon. That part of the question needs outside knowledge (1 Kings 11-12).

written:1CH-6-1:4.question: Which descendant of Aaron is said to have served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem?
written:1CH-6-1:4.why: also right: B: 6:10 names Azariah son of Johanan as the priest in Solomon's temple. Zadok son of Ahitub was also a priest under Solomon (1 Kings 1:39, 2:35), though this section does not say he served in the temple, so B is arguable from other Scripture.

written:1CH-6-31:2.question: Until what event did the Levite singers minister with song before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting?
written:1CH-6-31:2.answer: Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem
written:1CH-6-31:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-6-48:1.question: In the list of Aaron's descendants in 1 Chronicles 6, who is named as Aaron's son and first in the line?
written:1CH-6-48:1.why: not clear on its own: Aaron's sons are listed in 1 Chr 6:3 as Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar, so the first son named is Nadab, who is not an option. Eleazar is the choice whose line continues in 6:4 ("Eleazar begat Phinehas"), so C is the intended answer, but "first in the line" is open to the reading that points to Nadab.

written:1CH-7-20:3.question: Which daughter of Ephraim built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, as well as Uzzen-sheerah?

written:1CH-12-1:2.question: What skill did the Benjamite mighty men who came to David at Ziklag have with their hands?
written:1CH-12-1:2.answer: They could use both right and left hands to sling stones and shoot arrows

written:1CH-16-37:1.question: When David arranged worship after bringing the ark to Jerusalem, who did he leave before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister regularly?
written:1CH-16-37:1.why: also right: D: 16:37 says David left Asaph and his brothers before the ark to minister regularly. D is partly true too: 16:38 places Obed-edom and his relatives with that group, and Obed-edom and Hosah are named as gatekeepers, but they are not the ones named as left to minister regularly.

written:1CH-22-6:4.question: When David charged Solomon, what did he ask the LORD to give Solomon so that he could keep the Law?
written:1CH-22-6:4.why: not clear on its own: David asks God for 'a whole heart' to keep the commandments (1 Chronicles 29:19). B gets the heart part but adds 'many sons,' which is not in the text. C is Solomon's own request in 2 Chronicles 1:10, not David's. No option matches exactly.

written:1CH-22-6:7.question: What did David tell the leaders of Israel to do for the sanctuary, so that the ark of the covenant could be brought into the temple?
written:1CH-22-6:7.answer: Set their heart and soul to seek the LORD and begin building
written:1CH-22-6:7.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-23-24:1.question: In 1 Chronicles 23, why did David say the Levites no longer needed to carry the tabernacle or its articles?
written:1CH-23-24:1.answer: The LORD had given His people rest and come to dwell in Jerusalem forever

written:1CH-23-24:2.question: According to David's final instructions in 1 Chronicles 23, what age or older were the Levites who were counted for service in the house of the LORD?
written:1CH-23-24:2.answer: Twenty years of age or older
written:1CH-23-24:2.why: also right: A: The section (23:27) says the Levites twenty years or older were counted under David's final instructions. A is also true elsewhere: 1 Chronicles 23:3 says Levites thirty years old and above were counted in an earlier census, and Numbers 4:3 sets service at thirty.

written:1CH-24-20:2.question: In the list of the remaining Levites in 1 Chronicles 24, which two sons of Merari are named?
written:1CH-24-20:2.why: also right: C: Section names Mahli and Mushi as Merari's sons (24:26). Libni and Shimei are also sons of Merari elsewhere (Exodus 6:19, Numbers 3:20), though not in this list. Hebron and Uzziel are Kohath's sons, and Amram and Izhar are Kohath's sons too.

written:1CH-26-20:3.question: In 1 Chronicles 26, Shebuel, officer in charge of the treasuries, was a descendant of which son of Moses?
written:1CH-26-20:3.why: also right: B: Eliezer is also a son of Moses elsewhere (1 Chronicles 23:15; Exodus 18:4), though this section ties Shebuel to Gershom.

written:1CH-27-1:3.question: In David's army rotation, who was chief for the third month, and was also over the Thirty?
written:1CH-27-1:3.answer: Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest
written:1CH-27-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-27-1:5.question: In David's army rotation, who was commander for the sixth month?
written:1CH-27-1:5.answer: Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite
written:1CH-27-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-27-16:1.question: In 1 Chronicles 27, why did David not count the men of Israel aged twenty or under?
written:1CH-27-16:1.answer: The LORD had said He would make Israel as numerous as the stars

written:1CH-27-25:2.question: In 1 Chronicles 27, who was put in charge of the vineyards of King David?
written:1CH-27-25:2.why: also right: A: Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine vats, a narrower role that is arguably related to the vineyards. Shimei is the one put in charge of the vineyards themselves.

written:1CH-29-10:2.question: In his prayer before the assembly, what did David ask God to give his son Solomon?
written:1CH-29-10:2.answer: A whole heart to keep all God's commandments
written:1CH-29-10:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-13-4:4.question: In Abijah's speech, who did he say were the priests serving the LORD in Judah?
written:2CH-13-4:4.answer: The sons of Aaron, with the Levites attending to their duties
written:2CH-13-4:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-16-11:2.question: After King Asa of Judah died, where was he buried?
written:2CH-16-11:2.answer: In the tomb he had cut out for himself in the City of David

written:2CH-19-1:2.question: When Jehu confronted King Jehoshaphat, what good thing did he say was found in Jehoshaphat?
written:2CH-19-1:2.answer: He had removed the Asherah poles and set his heart on seeking God

written:2CH-25-5:4.question: After Amaziah dismissed the troops from Ephraim, what did those troops do while he was fighting at the Valley of Salt?
written:2CH-25-5:4.answer: They raided the cities of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon, killing 3,000 people

written:2CH-25-5:5.question: In the battle at the Valley of Salt, how many men of Seir did Amaziah's army strike down?
written:2CH-25-5:5.why: also right: A: Verse 25:11 says 10,000 were struck down, but 25:12 says another 10,000 were captured and thrown from a cliff, so 20,000 men of Seir died in total. Option A is a defensible reading of the total killed, though the question's wording ('strike down') points to C.

written:2CH-30-1:3.question: Why was Hezekiah's Passover not observed at the regular time?
written:2CH-30-1:3.answer: Not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem

written:2CH-30-13:1.question: In Hezekiah's Passover celebration, into which valley did the people throw the altars and incense altars they removed from Jerusalem?
written:2CH-30-13:1.why: also right: D: The text names the Kidron Valley. The Valley of Jehoshaphat (D) is traditionally identified with the Kidron, but Scripture does not say so; Joel 3:2 names it without linking it to Kidron.

written:2CH-30-13:3.question: When Hezekiah interceded for the people who ate the Passover without purifying themselves, what did he ask the LORD to provide?
written:2CH-30-13:3.answer: Atonement for everyone who sets his heart on seeking God
written:2CH-30-13:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-31-1:1.question: After the Passover celebration in Hezekiah's reign, what did the Israelites in attendance do throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh?
written:2CH-31-1:1.answer: They broke up the sacred pillars and tore down the high places and altars

written:EZR-2-1:3.question: Why were the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai excluded from the priesthood after returning from Babylon?
written:EZR-2-1:3.answer: They searched for their family records but could not find them
written:EZR-2-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZR-2-1:4.question: Until what time did the governor order the excluded priestly families not to eat the most holy things?
written:EZR-2-1:4.answer: Until there was a priest to consult the Urim and Thummim
written:EZR-2-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZR-3-1:1.question: When the Israelites gathered in Jerusalem after settling in their towns, what did Jeshua and Zerubbabel and their associates begin to build?
written:EZR-3-1:1.answer: The altar of the God of Israel
written:EZR-3-1:1.why: picked D without the text, not the writer's A: Ezra 3:8-10 has Zerubbabel, Jeshua and their kin begin the work on the house of the LORD, and the builders lay the temple foundation. But Ezra 3:2 says they built the altar of the God of Israel right after the people gathered in Jerusalem, so A could be argued.

written:EZR-4-1:1.question: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin asked to help build the temple, what reason did they give for joining in?
written:EZR-4-1:1.answer: They sought the same God and had sacrificed to Him
written:EZR-4-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EZR-4-1:2.question: When the enemies asked to build the temple with them, how did Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other family heads answer?
written:EZR-4-1:2.answer: They refused, saying the Jews alone must build it for the LORD
written:EZR-4-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EZR-4-6:3.question: According to the letter to Artaxerxes, what would happen if Jerusalem were rebuilt and its walls restored?
written:EZR-4-6:3.answer: The people would not pay tribute, duty, or toll, and the royal treasury would suffer

written:EZR-4-17:1.question: In Ezra 4, what order did King Artaxerxes send to Rehum and Shimshai about the Jews' work in Jerusalem?
written:EZR-4-17:1.answer: Make the men stop, so the city is not rebuilt until he orders

written:EZR-6-1:6.question: In Darius's decree, what would happen to any man who interfered with his directive?
written:EZR-6-1:6.answer: A beam would be torn from his house and he would be impaled on it

written:EZR-6-16:2.question: When the exiles dedicated the rebuilt house of God, how did they appoint the priests and Levites to the service of God in Jerusalem?
written:EZR-6-16:2.answer: According to what is written in the Book of Moses
written:EZR-6-16:2.why: also right: B: The section says the priests were divided and appointed according to what is written in the Book of Moses, so D is settled by the text. B is also defensible from elsewhere: David set the priestly and Levitical divisions (1 Chronicles 23-26), and Solomon kept that arrangement (2 Chronicles 8:14). A and C are not supported: Haggai and Zechariah urged the rebuilding but did not appoint priests, and Darius's decree provided for the work and sacrifices, not the appointments.

written:EZR-7-11:4.question: In Artaxerxes' letter, what was Ezra to buy with the silver and gold and offer on the altar at the house of God in Jerusalem?
written:EZR-7-11:4.answer: Bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings
written:EZR-7-11:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZR-7-11:8.question: In Artaxerxes' letter, why did the king say everything commanded by the God of heaven must be done diligently for His house?
written:EZR-7-11:8.answer: So that wrath would not fall on the realm of the king and his sons

written:EZR-7-27:2.question: After Ezra said the hand of the LORD his God was upon him, what did he do?
written:EZR-7-27:2.answer: He took courage and gathered the leaders of Israel to return with him

written:EZR-8-21:2.question: Why was Ezra ashamed to ask King Artaxerxes for an escort of soldiers and horsemen on the road to Jerusalem?
written:EZR-8-21:2.answer: He had told the king that God's hand is gracious to all who seek Him

written:EZR-9-1:1.question: In Ezra 9, what did the leaders report to Ezra about the Israelites' marriages to people of the surrounding lands?
written:EZR-9-1:1.answer: They had taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons

written:EZR-9-1:2.question: When Ezra heard the report about the exiles' unfaithfulness, how did he react?
written:EZR-9-1:2.answer: He tore his tunic and cloak, pulled out some hair, and sat down in horror

written:EZR-9-5:1.question: When Ezra began his prayer of confession at the evening offering, what did he say about his guilt and the guilt of the people?
written:EZR-9-5:1.answer: Their iniquities were higher than their heads, and their guilt reached the heavens

written:EZR-9-5:4.question: In Ezra's prayer, what commandment from the prophets did he say the people had forsaken concerning the peoples of the land?
written:EZR-9-5:4.answer: Not to give their daughters to their sons or take their daughters for theirs

written:EZR-10-6:5.question: In Ezra 10, what two things did Ezra command the people to do in response to their unfaithfulness?
written:EZR-10-6:5.answer: Confess to the LORD and separate from the people of the land and foreign wives

written:EZR-10-18:3.question: In Ezra 10, how many gatekeepers were named among those who had married foreign women?
written:EZR-10-18:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EZR-10-18:4.question: At the end of the list of men in Ezra 10 who had married foreign women, what does the text say about some of them?
written:EZR-10-18:4.answer: Some of them had children by these wives

written:NEH-2-1:2.question: When King Artaxerxes noticed Nehemiah's sad face, what reason did Nehemiah give for his sadness?
written:NEH-2-1:2.answer: The city where his fathers were buried lay in ruins, its gates burned

written:NEH-2-1:3.question: What did Nehemiah ask King Artaxerxes to do for him regarding Judah?
written:NEH-2-1:3.answer: Send him to Judah to rebuild the city of his fathers' graves
written:NEH-2-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-3-1:3.question: In the rebuilding of the wall, what did the nobles of the Tekoites fail to do?
written:NEH-3-1:3.answer: They did not put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors.
written:NEH-3-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-4-9:2.question: In Nehemiah 4, what did the people of Judah say was the problem that made them think they could never rebuild the wall?
written:NEH-4-9:2.answer: The laborer's strength was failing and there was so much rubble
written:NEH-4-9:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-4-9:3.question: In Nehemiah 4, what did the enemies say they would do to stop the work on the wall?
written:NEH-4-9:3.answer: Come into their midst, kill them, and put an end to the work

written:NEH-4-9:5.question: When Nehemiah told the nobles, officials, and people not to be afraid of the enemies, whom did he tell them to remember?
written:NEH-4-9:5.answer: The Lord, who is great and awesome
written:NEH-4-9:5.why: also right: A: Choice A names 'the LORD' (the same God Nehemiah says to remember), and Pharaoh's army being destroyed is true of the LORD elsewhere in Scripture (Exodus 14). Nehemiah does not mention Pharaoh here, so D is the answer the section gives.

written:NEH-5-1:6.question: In Nehemiah 5, what did Nehemiah do after the nobles and officials promised to restore what they had taken?
written:NEH-5-1:6.answer: He summoned the priests and required an oath of them
written:NEH-5-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-6-1:2.question: When Sanballat and Geshem invited Nehemiah to come down and meet, why did Nehemiah say he could not come?
written:NEH-6-1:2.answer: He was doing a great work and would stop it
written:NEH-6-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-6-1:4.question: In the unsealed letter Sanballat sent Nehemiah, what did he claim Nehemiah and the Jews were plotting?
written:NEH-6-1:4.answer: To revolt, with Nehemiah becoming their king
written:NEH-6-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NEH-6-1:6.question: When Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to meet him in the temple and shut its doors, what reason did he give?
written:NEH-6-1:6.answer: Men were coming by night to kill Nehemiah
written:NEH-6-1:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:NEH-9-1:2.question: In Nehemiah 9, the Levites' prayer says God chose Abram and brought him out of which city?
written:NEH-9-1:2.why: also right: B: The prayer names Ur of the Chaldeans, but Scripture elsewhere also links Abram to Haran (Acts 7:2-4; Genesis 11:31-12:5), a city he left before Canaan, so Haran is arguable.

written:NEH-9-1:5.question: According to the Levites' prayer in Nehemiah 9, from where did God speak to the Israelites when He came down on Mount Sinai?
written:NEH-9-1:5.why: also right: C, D: The prayer says heaven, which settles it. Weaker alternatives: God spoke from the tabernacle at Sinai (Leviticus 1:1), and from the burning bush on Horeb, which is the same mountain as Sinai (Exodus 3:1-4). Both are arguable but not what the Sinai event describes.

written:NEH-10-28:3.question: In the covenant in Nehemiah 10, what did the people promise to do when the people of the land brought merchandise or grain to sell on the Sabbath?
written:NEH-10-28:3.answer: They would not buy from them on the Sabbath or a holy day

written:NEH-10-28:4.question: In the covenant in Nehemiah 10, what did the people promise to do every seventh year?
written:NEH-10-28:4.answer: Let the fields lie fallow and cancel every debt
written:NEH-10-28:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-12-27:4.question: In the dedication of the wall, who led the first thanksgiving choir along the top of the wall?
written:NEH-12-27:4.why: also right: A, C: Verse 36 says Ezra the scribe led the procession of the first choir. But Hoshaiah is named first in the group that followed it (v. 32), and Jezrahiah directed both choirs (v. 42), so both are arguable. The explicit 'led the procession' wording settles it for Ezra.

written:NEH-13-15:2.question: When Nehemiah saw the Sabbath being profaned in Jerusalem, what did he order done as the evening shadows began to fall just before the Sabbath?
written:NEH-13-15:2.answer: The gates were to be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath

written:EST-1-13:2.question: When King Xerxes asked his advisors what to do about Queen Vashti, what had she done that made it a matter for the law?
written:EST-1-13:2.answer: She refused to obey the king's command delivered by the eunuchs
written:EST-1-13:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EST-1-13:5.question: How did King Xerxes announce his decree to the provinces of his kingdom?
written:EST-1-13:5.answer: Letters sent to each province in its own script and each people in their own language

written:EST-6-1:5.question: What did Haman suggest should be done for the man the king was delighted to honor, thinking the king meant him?
written:EST-6-1:5.answer: Dress him in the king's robe, set him on the king's horse, and parade him through the city square

written:EST-8-7:1.question: In Esther 8, why did King Xerxes say that a new decree written in his name and sealed with the royal signet ring was needed to help the Jews, rather than simply cancelling Haman's earlier decree?
written:EST-8-7:1.answer: A decree written in the king's name and sealed with his ring cannot be revoked

written:EST-8-7:7.question: When Mordecai left the king's presence in Esther 8, what was he wearing?
written:EST-8-7:7.answer: Royal garments of blue and white, a large gold crown, and a purple robe

written:EST-9-1:2.question: In Esther 9, how many men did the Jews kill and destroy in the citadel of Susa?
written:EST-9-1:2.why: also right: B, C: 9:6 gives 500 for Susa on the 13th. Elsewhere in the chapter (9:15, outside this section), the Jews killed 300 more in Susa on the 14th, so 300 and the Susa total of 800 are also true of the story. The question's wording and 9:6 point to 500.

written:EST-10-1:2.question: According to Esther 10, where were the accomplishments of Mordecai and the greatness the king gave him written down?
written:EST-10-1:2.answer: In the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia

written:JOB-1-6:1.question: When the LORD gave Satan permission to test Job, what limit did He set on what Satan could do?
written:JOB-1-6:1.answer: He must not lay a hand on Job himself
written:JOB-1-6:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-3-1:2.question: In Job's lament, what did he say should happen to the day of his birth, with regard to light?
written:JOB-3-1:2.answer: It should turn to darkness, with no light shining on it
written:JOB-3-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-3-1:3.question: In Job 3:11, what question did Job ask about his birth?
written:JOB-3-1:3.answer: Why did he not perish at birth and die coming from the womb?

written:JOB-4-1:4.question: In Job 4, when did Eliphaz say the spirit appeared to him, causing fear and trembling?
written:JOB-4-1:4.answer: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men
written:JOB-4-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-5-1:3.question: What does Eliphaz say he would do if he were in Job's place?
written:JOB-5-1:3.answer: Appeal to God and lay his cause before Him
written:JOB-5-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-7-1:3.question: In Job 7, what does Job say his flesh is clothed with and encrusted with because of his affliction?
written:JOB-7-1:3.why: not clear on its own: Job 7:5 differs by translation: ESV says flesh is clothed with worms and dust, NIV says worms and scabs. B (worms and dirt) and D (dust and sores) each match half of the verse, so neither is clearly the single answer. The question should name the translation or give the expected answer.

written:JOB-7-1:6.question: In Job 7:12, what two things does Job ask whether he is, that God must keep him under guard?
written:JOB-7-1:6.answer: The sea or the monster of the deep
written:JOB-7-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-9-1:5.question: In Job 9, which of these does Job say God does alone?
written:JOB-9-1:5.answer: Stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea
written:JOB-9-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-10-1:5.question: In Job 10:18-19, what does Job wish had happened instead of his being brought from the womb?
written:JOB-10-1:5.answer: That he had died and been carried from the womb to the grave

written:JOB-10-1:6.question: In Job 10:21-22, how does Job describe the land he will go to, never to return?
written:JOB-10-1:6.answer: A land of darkness and gloom where even the light is like darkness

written:JOB-13-1:1.question: In Job 13, what does Job call his three friends when he says they "smear with lies"?
written:JOB-13-1:1.why: also right: D: Job 13:4 says "you are all worthless physicians," which is the answer for this passage. Job also calls the friends "miserable comforters" in Job 16:2, so D is a fair alternative if the question is read as asking for any name Job gives them elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOB-14-1:5.question: In Job 14, what does Job say would happen to his transgression if God restored him, as it is "sealed" away?
written:JOB-14-1:5.answer: It would be sealed in a bag
written:JOB-14-1:5.why: not clear on its own: Job 14:17 says the transgression is sealed up in a bag, but the verse is not stated as conditional on God restoring him; the question adds an 'if' the text does not contain. The answer (a bag) is still the only sealing option.

written:JOB-15-1:1.question: In Job 15, which of Job's friends begins the second round of speeches by replying to Job?
written:JOB-15-1:1.why: the section does not settle it: Section shows 'Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied' (15:1), so B is the speaker. But the section does not say this is the second round; that framing depends on chapters outside the section.

written:JOB-15-1:4.question: In Job 15, Eliphaz asks Job whether he was the first man ever born. What does he ask next?
written:JOB-15-1:4.answer: Whether Job was brought forth before the hills
written:JOB-15-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-15-1:5.question: In Job 15, how does Eliphaz say the age of the wise men on his side compares with Job's father?
written:JOB-15-1:5.answer: They are men much older than Job's father
written:JOB-15-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-18-1:5.question: In Job 18, what does Bildad say rains down on the dwelling of the wicked man?
written:JOB-18-1:5.why: also right: C: Job 18:15 settles that Bildad says burning sulfur rains down. Blazing coals is not in Job 18, but Psalm 11:6 says God will rain fiery coals and sulfur on the wicked, so C could fairly be argued for from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOB-20-1:4.question: In Zophar's speech, to what does he compare the wicked man's flying away, never to be found?
written:JOB-20-1:4.answer: A dream and a vision in the night
written:JOB-20-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-20-1:7.question: In Zophar's speech, what sin of the wicked man does he give as a reason for his downfall?
written:JOB-20-1:7.answer: He oppressed and forsook the poor and seized houses he did not build

written:JOB-22-1:6.question: In Job 22, what did Eliphaz urge Job to lay up in his heart?
written:JOB-22-1:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-23-1:2.question: In Job 23, what does Job say he has treasured more than his daily bread?
written:JOB-23-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-23-1:4.question: In Job 23, when Job looks east, west, north and south, what is his problem in finding God?
written:JOB-23-1:4.answer: He cannot find or see God in any direction
written:JOB-23-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-28-1:6.question: In Job's poem about wisdom, what is the price of wisdom said to be beyond?
written:JOB-28-1:6.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: Job 28:18 says wisdom's price is above/beyond rubies in KJV and NIV, but ESV and some other translations render the word as pearls, so pearls (B) could be argued.

written:JOB-29-1:1.question: In Job 29, when Job longs for the days when God watched over him, what does he say God's lamp did?
written:JOB-29-1:1.answer: It shone above his head, and he walked by its light through darkness

written:JOB-29-1:2.question: In Job's description of his former days, what did Job do for the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper?
written:JOB-29-1:2.why: also right: A, D: Job 29:12 says he rescued the poor and fatherless, which settles C. Job 31:17 and 31:19-20 say he shared his bread with the fatherless and clothed the needy, so A and D are arguably true of Job elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOB-30-1:3.question: In Job 30, where did the outcast men who now mock Job live, according to Job?
written:JOB-30-1:3.answer: On the slopes of the wadis, among rocks and in holes in the ground

written:JOB-30-15:2.question: In Job 30, what does Job say happens when he cries out to God for help?
written:JOB-30-15:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-31-1:3.question: In Job 31, what did Job say should happen to his arm if he had lifted his hand against the fatherless because he had support in the gate?
written:JOB-31-1:3.answer: It should fall from his shoulder and be torn from its socket
written:JOB-31-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-31-1:5.question: In Job 31, what did Job say he would do with the indictment written by his accuser?
written:JOB-31-1:5.answer: Carry it on his shoulder and wear it like a crown
written:JOB-31-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-31-1:6.question: In Job 31:32, what did Job say about strangers and travelers who came to his house?
written:JOB-31-1:6.answer: No stranger had to lodge on the street, for his door was open to the traveler

written:JOB-31-1:7.question: In Job 31, what did Job say should grow instead of wheat and barley if he had wronged his land and its tenants?
written:JOB-31-1:7.why: picked C without the text, not the writer's B: Job 31:38-40 says thistles grow instead of wheat and cockle (a weed) instead of barley. C matches the thistles; D's 'tares' could stand for the cockle, but 'wild grapes' is not in the text, and the options don't match the passage exactly.

written:JOB-32-1:5.question: According to Elihu, what gives a person understanding?
written:JOB-32-1:5.answer: A spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty
written:JOB-32-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-33-1:1.question: In Job 33, what does Elihu say he was formed from, to show he is just like Job before God?
written:JOB-33-1:1.why: also right: B: Elihu says "I was also formed from clay" (33:6). B, "dust of the ground," is not his wording, but it is arguably also right: Genesis 2:7 says God formed man from the dust of the ground, and Elihu seems to allude to that account.

written:JOB-33-1:2.question: In Job 33, which words of Job does Elihu say he heard, claiming Job said, "I am pure, without transgression"?
written:JOB-33-1:2.answer: Job had said he was clean, with no iniquity in him.
written:JOB-33-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-33-1:4.question: According to Elihu, in what ways does God speak to men while they slumber on their beds?
written:JOB-33-1:4.answer: In a dream, in a vision in the night
written:JOB-33-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-33-1:5.question: In Job 33, what does Elihu say a mediator, one in a thousand, would tell God on behalf of a man near the Pit?
written:JOB-33-1:5.answer: "Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom"

written:JOB-35-1:1.question: In Job 35, Elihu tells Job to look at the heavens and gaze at the clouds high above. What point is Elihu making about God by this?
written:JOB-35-1:1.answer: Job's sin or righteousness cannot harm or benefit God
written:JOB-35-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-35-1:2.question: In Job 35, whom does Elihu say is affected by a man's wickedness and righteousness?
written:JOB-35-1:2.answer: Only a man like yourself, and a son of man
written:JOB-35-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-36-1:3.question: According to Elihu, what happens to those who obey and serve God when He speaks to them in their affliction?
written:JOB-36-1:3.answer: They end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness
written:JOB-36-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-37-1:5.question: At the end of Job 37, why does Elihu say men fear God?
written:JOB-37-1:5.answer: He is not partial to the wise in heart
written:JOB-37-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-38-1:8.question: In Job 38, who does the LORD say provides food for the raven when its young cry out?
written:JOB-38-1:8.answer: The LORD Himself, as the one who feeds the raven
written:JOB-38-1:8.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-39-1:2.question: In God's speech to Job, what does the wild ox refuse to do for a man, according to God's questions about the wild ox?
written:JOB-39-1:2.answer: Serve him by plowing and bringing in grain
written:JOB-39-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOB-40-6:3.question: In the LORD's challenge to Job, what did He say He would confess if Job could humble the proud and bury the wicked?
written:JOB-40-6:3.answer: That Job's own right hand can save him
written:JOB-40-6:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-42-1:1.question: In Job 42, after the LORD spoke to him, what did Job say now saw God, in contrast to what his ears had heard before?
written:JOB-42-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JOB-42-7:2.question: In Job 42, after the LORD told Eliphaz and his two friends to offer a burnt offering, who was to pray for them?
written:JOB-42-7:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-6-1:1.question: In Psalm 6, why does David say the dead cannot praise the LORD from Sheol?
written:PSA-6-1:1.answer: There is no mention of the LORD in death
written:PSA-6-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-6-1:2.question: In Psalm 6, what does David say he does all night because he is weary from groaning?
written:PSA-6-1:2.answer: He floods his bed with weeping and drenches his couch with tears
written:PSA-6-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-8-1:1.question: In Psalm 8, the psalmist says God made man "a little lower than" whom?
written:PSA-8-1:1.why: also right: B: Heavenly host is Scripture's term for the angelic host (e.g., Luke 2:13), so it could fairly be argued as the same beings. Cherubim and archangels are specific subclasses the psalm does not name, so they are not included.

written:PSA-8-1:2.question: In Psalm 8, when the psalmist looks at the heavens, what does he say they are the work of?
written:PSA-8-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-9-1:3.question: In Psalm 9, what does the psalmist say the LORD is for the oppressed?
written:PSA-9-1:3.answer: A refuge and a stronghold in times of trouble
written:PSA-9-1:3.why: also right: D: Psalm 9:9 says 'a refuge... a stronghold.' D's 'fortress' is a near synonym of stronghold, and Psalm 18:2 calls the LORD my fortress and shield, so D is arguable, though its 'against every enemy' wording is not in Psalm 9.

written:PSA-9-1:5.question: In Psalm 9, what does the psalmist say happens to the nations that fall into a pit and are caught in a net?
written:PSA-9-1:5.answer: They are caught in what they made and hid themselves
written:PSA-9-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-10-1:4.question: In Psalm 10, whom does the psalmist call the helper of the one who has no father?
written:PSA-10-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-11-1:2.question: According to Psalm 11, what will the LORD rain down on the wicked?
written:PSA-11-1:2.why: also right: C: Psalm 11:6 names fiery coals and sulfur, which settles D. Choice C (hailstones and fire) is not in Psalm 11, but Ezekiel 38:22 has the LORD raining down hailstones, fire and sulfur, so C could fairly be argued from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:PSA-15-1:1.question: In Psalm 15, what will happen to the one who does these things: walks with integrity, speaks truth, lends without interest and refuses bribes?
written:PSA-15-1:1.why: also right: A: Psalm 15:5 states directly that the one who does these things will never be shaken. Choice A is arguably supported elsewhere (John 8:51 and 11:26 say believers will never see or die), though not as a claim about this psalm's person, so it is a weak alternative that the quiz should be aware of.

written:PSA-17-1:4.question: In Psalm 17, what does David say he will do when he awakes?
written:PSA-17-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-17-1:5.question: In Psalm 17, by what does David say he has avoided the ways of the violent?
written:PSA-17-1:5.answer: By the word of God's lips
written:PSA-17-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-20-1:2.question: In Psalm 20, from where do the people pray that the LORD will send help and sustain the one in the day of trouble?
written:PSA-20-1:2.answer: From the sanctuary and from Zion
written:PSA-20-1:2.why: not clear on its own: Psalm 20:2 says help comes "from the sanctuary" and strength "out of Zion," so B is right. But the question says "the one in the day of trouble" without naming who that is (the king, in the psalm), so it leans on context the quiz-taker doesn't have.

written:PSA-20-1:3.question: In Psalm 20, what does the psalmist say the LORD does for His anointed, answering him from His holy heaven?
written:PSA-20-1:3.answer: He saves him with the saving power of His right hand
written:PSA-20-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-21-1:4.question: According to Psalm 21, why will the king not be shaken?
written:PSA-21-1:4.answer: He trusts in the LORD, and the Most High shows loving devotion
written:PSA-21-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-25-1:4.question: In Psalm 25, why does the psalmist ask the LORD to forgive his iniquity?
written:PSA-25-1:4.answer: For the sake of the LORD’s name, and because his iniquity is great

written:PSA-27-1:2.question: In Psalm 27, what is the one thing the psalmist has asked of the LORD and desires?
written:PSA-27-1:2.answer: To dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of his life

written:PSA-40-1:2.question: In Psalm 40, what does the psalmist say God put in his mouth after lifting him from the miry clay?
written:PSA-40-1:2.answer: A new song, a hymn of praise to our God
written:PSA-40-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-41-1:3.question: In Psalm 41, what does the psalmist say he knows because his enemy does not triumph over him?
written:PSA-41-1:3.answer: That the LORD delights in him
written:PSA-41-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-43-1:1.question: In Psalm 43, what does the psalmist ask God to send out so that they can lead him to God's holy mountain?
written:PSA-43-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-44-1:5.question: In Psalm 44, what do the people say they have not done, even though disaster has come upon them?
written:PSA-44-1:5.answer: Forgotten God or betrayed His covenant
written:PSA-44-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-47-1:1.question: In Psalm 47:9, the nobles of the nations assemble as the people of which God?
written:PSA-47-1:1.why: also right: B, C, D: The text says 'the people of the God of Abraham,' so A is the answer. B, C and D name the same LORD (Yahweh), who is also the God of David (2 Sam 7), Noah (Gen 9) and Moses (Ex 3:6), so they are true of God elsewhere in Scripture, though not the wording of this verse.

written:PSA-49-1:4.question: In Psalm 49, what does the psalmist say God will do for him, in contrast to those who trust in wealth?
written:PSA-49-1:4.answer: Redeem his life from Sheol and take him to Himself
written:PSA-49-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-61-1:1.question: In Psalm 61, what does the psalmist ask God to lead him to when his heart is faint?
written:PSA-61-1:1.answer: The rock that is higher than I
written:PSA-61-1:1.why: also right: B: Verse 2 says "Lead me to the rock that is higher than I." Choice B is a fair metaphorical equivalent, since Psalm 18:2 calls God "my rock, my fortress," but the section does not use the word fortress or the phrase "cannot be shaken."

written:PSA-67-1:1.question: In Psalm 67, why does the psalmist say the nations should be glad and sing for joy?
written:PSA-67-1:1.answer: Because God judges the peoples justly and leads the nations
written:PSA-67-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-68-1:5.question: In Psalm 68, which mountain does the psalmist say God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will dwell forever, while other mountains of many peaks gaze in envy?
written:PSA-68-1:5.answer: The mountain God chose, not Bashan
written:PSA-68-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-69-1:1.question: In Psalm 69, what does the psalmist say has consumed him, bringing the insults of those who insult God down on him?
written:PSA-69-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-71-1:1.question: In Psalm 71, the psalmist asks God to be what kind of place "where I can always go"?
written:PSA-71-1:1.why: also right: A: Psalm 61:3 and Proverbs 18:10 call God a 'strong tower' where the one who runs is safe, so 'tower of strength' could fairly be argued elsewhere in Scripture, though this section says 'rock of refuge' and 'fortress,' not 'tower.'

written:PSA-74-1:6.question: In Psalm 74, what does the psalmist say God did to Leviticus's namesake... the heads of Leviathan, whom He fed to the creatures of the desert?
written:PSA-74-1:6.why: not clear on its own: The question's premise is false: Leviticus is not named after Leviathan (the name comes from the Levites). Remove that clause. Psalm 74:14 supports A, 'He crushed them,' regardless.

written:PSA-76-1:1.question: In Psalm 76, where does the psalmist say God's dwelling place is?
written:PSA-76-1:1.why: also right: D: Verse 76:2 says His dwelling place is in Zion. Shiloh (D) is also argued elsewhere: Ps 78:60 and Jer 7:12 describe God's tabernacle and name dwelling at Shiloh.

written:PSA-76-1:2.question: In Psalm 76, what did God shatter in Salem and Zion?
written:PSA-76-1:2.answer: The flaming arrows, shield, sword and weapons of war
written:PSA-76-1:2.why: not clear on its own: Psalm 76:3 lists the weapons (flaming arrows, shield, sword, weapons of war) that God breaks, but the verse does not say he broke anything in Salem and Zion. Verse 2 only places his tent/dwelling there, so the question's premise is off.

written:PSA-77-1:2.question: In Psalm 77, which people does the psalmist say God redeemed with power?
written:PSA-77-1:2.answer: The sons of Jacob and Joseph
written:PSA-77-1:2.why: also right: D: Psalm 77:15 names the sons of Jacob and Joseph. D is a looser broader-descent reading: Jacob was Isaac's son, so Israel is descended from Abraham and Isaac, but the psalm does not say that.

written:PSA-77-1:5.question: In Psalm 77, what does the psalmist say about God's path as it led through the mighty waters of the sea?
written:PSA-77-1:5.answer: His footprints were not to be found
written:PSA-77-1:5.why: also right: A, B: The psalm says only that God's footprints were not found (77:19). A (dry ground) and B (walls of water) are true details of the Exodus crossing (Ex 14:16, 22, 29) but are not what the psalmist says. D is not included: the pillar of cloud was present at the sea (Ex 14:19-20), but it stood between the camps rather than marking the path.

written:PSA-80-1:1.question: In Psalm 80, whom does the psalmist address as the one who leads Joseph like a flock?
written:PSA-80-1:1.why: also right: D: D ("The Rock of Jacob") is another title for the same God, and Genesis 49:24 pairs the Shepherd with the Rock of Israel, so it could fairly be argued for.

written:PSA-83-1:1.question: In Psalm 83, what do the enemies of God's people say they want to do to Israel?
written:PSA-83-1:1.answer: Erase them as a nation so Israel is remembered no more
written:PSA-83-1:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-88-1:3.question: In Psalm 88, what does the psalmist say God has done to his friends, so that he is confined and cannot escape?
written:PSA-88-1:3.answer: Removed them from him and made him repulsive to them
written:PSA-88-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-93-1:1.question: In Psalm 93, what is the LORD said to be robed in?
written:PSA-93-1:1.why: also right: C: Psalm 93:1 says the LORD is robed in majesty. Option C is arguably also true elsewhere: Psalm 104:2 says God is clothed with splendor and majesty and wrapped in light.

written:PSA-94-1:4.question: In Psalm 94, what promise does the psalmist give about the LORD and His people?
written:PSA-94-1:4.answer: The LORD will not forsake His people and will never abandon His heritage.

written:PSA-101-1:1.question: In Psalm 101, what does the psalmist say he will not set before his eyes?
written:PSA-101-1:1.why: also right: B: Psalm 101:3 says "I will set no worthless thing before my eyes." Choice B (idols of the nations) is arguable as a narrower form of "worthless thing," since Scripture calls idols worthless (e.g., Ps 31:6), but this psalm never mentions idols.

written:PSA-106-1:2.question: According to Psalm 106, why did the LORD save Israel at the Red Sea despite their rebellion?
written:PSA-106-1:2.answer: For the sake of His name, to make His power known
written:PSA-106-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-107-1:1.question: In Psalm 107, why were the prisoners who sat in darkness and the shadow of death in affliction and chains?
written:PSA-107-1:1.answer: They rebelled against the words of God and despised the counsel of the Most High

written:PSA-109-1:6.question: In Psalm 109, on what basis does the psalmist ask God to deal kindly with him and deliver him?
written:PSA-109-1:6.answer: For the sake of God's name and the goodness of His loving devotion

written:PSA-109-1:8.question: In Psalm 109, what does the psalmist say will happen when his enemies curse and he is blessed by the LORD?
written:PSA-109-1:8.answer: They will be put to shame, but God's servant will rejoice
written:PSA-109-1:8.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-114-1:1.question: In Psalm 114, what does the psalmist say Judah became when Israel departed from Egypt?
written:PSA-114-1:1.why: also right: D: Verse 2 says Judah became God's sanctuary, so B is settled by the text. D is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture, since Zion/Jerusalem in Judah is called God's holy mountain (e.g., Psalm 2:6).

written:PSA-118-1:3.question: In Psalm 118, how does the psalmist say he dealt with the nations that surrounded him on every side?
written:PSA-118-1:3.answer: In the name of the LORD he cut them off
written:PSA-118-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-118-1:4.question: In Psalm 118, what does the psalmist call the LORD when he says, "The LORD is ___ and my song, and He has become my salvation"?
written:PSA-118-1:4.why: a quotation not word for word in the BSB text

written:PSA-119-1:1.question: In Psalm 119, how does the psalmist say a young man can keep his way pure?
written:PSA-119-1:1.answer: By guarding it according to God's word
written:PSA-119-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-119-1:2.question: In Psalm 119, why does the psalmist say he has hidden God's word in his heart?
written:PSA-119-1:2.answer: That he might not sin against God
written:PSA-119-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-132-1:3.question: In Psalm 132, what does the psalmist pray that the LORD's priests be clothed with?
written:PSA-132-1:3.why: also right: C: Verse 16 says the LORD will clothe her priests with salvation, but that is a divine promise, not the psalmist's prayer; the question asks what is prayed for, so B is the answer.

written:PSA-132-1:4.question: In Psalm 132, what condition did the LORD give for David's sons' sons to sit on his throne forever?
written:PSA-132-1:4.answer: That David's sons keep His covenant and the testimony He teaches them

written:PSA-134-1:2.question: In Psalm 134:3, how is the LORD, who blesses from Zion, described?
written:PSA-134-1:2.answer: The Maker of heaven and earth
written:PSA-134-1:2.why: also right: B, C, D: Verse 3 names the LORD only as Maker of heaven and earth (A). B, C and D are also true of the LORD elsewhere: 'King over all the nations' (Ps 47:8), 'the Rock of our salvation' (Ps 95:1), and 'Shepherd of Israel' (Ps 80:1), though 'forever' in D is an added phrase. The section itself settles the answer as A.

written:PSA-140-1:3.question: In Psalm 140, what does David say the LORD does for him in the day of battle?
written:PSA-140-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-143-1:1.question: In Psalm 143, why does the psalmist ask God not to bring His servant into judgment?
written:PSA-143-1:1.answer: No one alive is righteous before God
written:PSA-143-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-146-1:1.question: In Psalm 146, whom does the psalmist warn people not to put their trust in?
written:PSA-146-1:1.answer: Princes, mortal man, who cannot save
written:PSA-146-1:1.why: also right: A: Psalm 146:3 says, "Put not your trust in princes, in mortal man, who cannot save." Choice A is arguable because princes are rulers and kings of the nations fall within that warning, though the text says "princes," not "kings," and never says "cannot rule." Choices B and C are not warned against in this psalm.

written:PRO-1-8:1.question: In Proverbs 1:8-9, what does the teacher say a son's father's instruction and mother's teaching are like?
written:PRO-1-8:1.answer: A garland of grace on his head and a pendant around his neck

written:PRO-1-20:3.question: In Proverbs 1, what does Wisdom say will happen to those who listen to her?
written:PRO-1-20:3.answer: They will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil
written:PRO-1-20:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PRO-2-1:3.question: In Proverbs 2, what does the LORD do for those who walk with integrity?
written:PRO-2-1:3.answer: He is a shield to them
written:PRO-2-1:3.why: also right: B: Section says 'He is a shield to those who walk with integrity' (2:7), so D is the section's answer. B is arguable from elsewhere: the LORD is called a 'rock of refuge' in Psalm 31:2 and similar protective metaphors recur in the Psalms, so a strict reader could accept it too.

written:PRO-3-13:2.question: In Proverbs 3, what does the LORD give to the humble?
written:PRO-3-13:2.why: also right: A, C: Verse 34 settles it (grace). Elsewhere, Proverbs 22:4 says the reward of humility is riches, honor and life, so riches and honor are arguably also given to the humble, though not by this section.

written:PRO-6-1:1.question: In Proverbs 6:16, how many things does the LORD hate, according to the saying that adds one more, "seven that are detestable to Him"?
written:PRO-6-1:1.why: the section does not settle it: The text says the LORD hates six things and that seven are detestable to Him. The question's wording points to the 'seven' saying, and seven is not among the choices. Six is the literal number of things the LORD hates, but the question is ambiguous.

written:PRO-6-20:2.question: In Proverbs 6, what two questions does the teacher ask to show that a man who sleeps with another man's wife will be punished?
written:PRO-6-20:2.answer: Can a man embrace fire without burning his clothes, or walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?

written:PRO-6-20:3.question: According to Proverbs 6, how much must a thief pay if he is caught?
written:PRO-6-20:3.why: also right: D: Proverbs 6:31 says sevenfold. Fourfold is also a thief's restitution rule elsewhere (Exodus 22:1, a stolen sheep; Luke 19:8, Zacchaeus), so D could be argued by other Scripture, though the question asks specifically about Proverbs 6.

written:PRO-17-1:1.question: According to Proverbs 17:3, who is the tester of hearts, as a crucible tests silver and a furnace tests gold?
written:PRO-17-1:1.why: also right: C: "The righteous judge" is another designation for God, who tests hearts elsewhere (Jer 17:10; Ps 7:9; 2 Tim 4:8), so it could fairly be argued for. The section itself names the LORD.

written:PRO-19-1:4.question: According to Proverbs 19:23, what does the fear of the LORD lead to?
written:PRO-19-1:4.why: also right: B, C: 19:23 says the fear of the LORD leads to life, which settles the answer. But Proverbs 22:4 says the fear of the LORD brings riches and honor, so B and C are also true elsewhere in Scripture, though this section does not state them.

written:PRO-19-1:5.question: According to Proverbs 19:24, what does the slacker do with his hand in the dish?
written:PRO-19-1:5.answer: He buries it there and will not bring it back to his mouth

written:PRO-22-1:2.question: According to Proverbs 22:2, what do the rich and the poor have in common?
written:PRO-22-1:2.answer: The LORD is Maker of them all
written:PRO-22-1:2.why: also right: A: The section's answer is C (Maker). A is a true statement elsewhere in Scripture (e.g., Ps 75:7, Heb 12:23): God judges rich and poor alike, so it is a shared fact, though not the one Prov 22:2 states.

written:PRO-22-17:1.question: In Proverbs 22:23, why does the writer say not to rob a poor man or crush the afflicted at the gate?
written:PRO-22-17:1.answer: The LORD will take up their case and plunder those who rob them

written:PRO-24-1:4.question: In Proverbs 24:17-18, why should you not gloat when your enemy falls?
written:PRO-24-1:4.answer: The LORD may disapprove and turn His wrath away from him
written:PRO-24-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PRO-29-1:2.question: According to Proverbs 29:23, what will a humble spirit obtain?
written:PRO-29-1:2.why: also right: B, D: Proverbs 22:4 says humility and the fear of the LORD bring riches, honor and life, so 'great wealth' (riches) and 'long life' (life) are also true elsewhere, though this verse names only honor.

written:PRO-29-1:4.question: According to Proverbs 29:18, who is blessed when the people cast off restraint where there is no vision?
written:PRO-29-1:4.why: also right: A: Other verses call the giver to the poor blessed (Prov 14:21, 22:9), though 29:18 itself names only the keeper of the Law.

written:PRO-29-1:5.question: According to Proverbs 29:11, what does a wise man do with his anger, in contrast to a fool?
written:PRO-29-1:5.why: also right: C: 'Holds it back' could fairly be read as hiding it in silence, but the verse says nothing about silence, so this is a loose paraphrase rather than a match.

written:PRO-30-1:1.question: In the words of Agur in Proverbs 30, what does he say God is to those who take refuge in Him?
written:PRO-30-1:1.why: also right: A, B, C: The section says God is 'a shield to those who take refuge in Him' (30:5). Rock, strong tower, and fortress are also used of God elsewhere (e.g., Deut 32:4, Psalm 18:2, Proverbs 18:10), so they could be argued for by anything else in the Bible, though they are not Agur's words here.

written:PRO-30-1:3.question: In Proverbs 30, what does Agur say will happen to the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother?
written:PRO-30-1:3.answer: Ravens of the valley will pluck it out and young vultures devour it

written:PRO-31-10:2.question: In Proverbs 31, what does the woman of noble character do for the poor and needy?
written:PRO-31-10:2.answer: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy

written:PRO-31-10:4.question: In Proverbs 31, what does the woman of noble character buy with her earnings after appraising a field?
written:PRO-31-10:4.why: the section does not settle it: Verse 31:16 says she appraises and buys a field, not any of the listed items. The vineyard (A) is what she plants from her earnings, so the question's wording doesn't match the text. A is the closest choice, but the question is mis-worded and should be fixed before it's shown.

written:ECC-2-1:1.question: In Ecclesiastes 2, when the Preacher tested himself with pleasure and enjoyment, how did he judge it?
written:ECC-2-1:1.why: also right: A: Ecclesiastes 2:24-25 later calls eating, drinking and enjoying one's toil a gift from God's hand, so A is arguable from elsewhere in the book, though the test itself is judged futile in 2:1 and 2:11.

written:ECC-2-1:4.question: In Ecclesiastes 2, after considering all his works and toil, what did the Preacher conclude?
written:ECC-2-1:4.answer: Everything was a pursuit of the wind, with nothing to be gained
written:ECC-2-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ECC-2-12:1.question: In Ecclesiastes 2:13, wisdom is said to exceed folly just as what exceeds darkness?
written:ECC-2-12:1.why: also right: C: The text says wisdom exceeds folly 'just as light exceeds darkness.' Day over night is a loose paraphrase of the same light-over-darkness idea, so C is arguable, though 'day' does not appear in the text.

written:ECC-2-18:4.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:26, what task does God assign to the sinner?
written:ECC-2-18:4.answer: Gathering and accumulating what he will hand over to one who pleases God

written:ECC-8-14:2.question: In Ecclesiastes 8:14, what futility did the Preacher observe happening on the earth with righteous men and wicked men?
written:ECC-8-14:2.answer: Righteous men get what the wicked deserve, and wicked men what the righteous deserve

written:ECC-9-7:1.question: In Ecclesiastes 9:10, the Preacher says to do whatever you find to do with your hands with all your might. What reason does he give?
written:ECC-9-7:1.answer: In Sheol there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom
written:ECC-9-7:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ECC-9-13:1.question: In the story Solomon tells in Ecclesiastes 9 of a small city with few men attacked by a mighty king, who saved the city?

written:SNG-2-1:2.question: In Song of Songs 2:3, to what tree does the bride compare her beloved among the trees of the forest?
written:SNG-2-1:2.why: not clear on its own: Song 2:3 says 'apple tree' (tappuach), which is not offered. Apricot (D) is the nearest choice, since some scholars identify the Hebrew word as apricot, so the item has no clean correct answer.

written:SNG-3-1:2.question: After the bride found the one she loved in Song of Songs 3, where did she bring him?
written:SNG-3-1:2.answer: To her mother's house, the chamber of the one who conceived her

written:SNG-6-1:2.question: In Song of Songs 6:2, where does the woman say her beloved has gone down to pasture his flock and gather lilies?
written:SNG-6-1:2.answer: To his garden, to the beds of spices
written:SNG-6-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:SNG-7-1:1.question: In Song of Songs 7:4, to what is the beloved's neck compared?
written:SNG-7-1:1.why: also right: A: The section says 7:4 'Your neck is like a tower made of ivory.' Choice A is a neck-as-tower comparison, but it is Song 4:4 ('Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields') and applies to the same beloved.

written:SNG-7-1:5.question: In Song of Songs 7:10, what does the woman say about herself and her beloved?
written:SNG-7-1:5.answer: “I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.”
written:SNG-7-1:5.why: also right: A, B: D is the verbatim line of 7:10. A and B are near-verbatim statements the woman makes elsewhere: A condenses 6:3 ('I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine; he feeds his flock among the lilies'), and B matches 2:16 and 6:3 ('My beloved is mine, and I am his'). C is not a quotation; its first clause resembles 1:5 but the second clause is not stated anywhere, so I left it out.

written:SNG-8-1:1.question: In Song of Songs 8:6, what does the woman ask her beloved to set her as over his heart and upon his arm?
written:SNG-8-1:1.why: also right: A: 8:6 says 'Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm.' A signet ring is a kind of seal, so A is arguable, but the text says 'seal', not 'signet ring'.

written:SNG-8-1:4.question: In Song of Songs 8:4, whom does the woman charge not to arouse or awaken love until the time is right?
written:SNG-8-1:4.why: also right: A: 8:4 says 'O daughters of Jerusalem'. 'Daughters of Zion' (A) names the same group in Song 3:11, and Zion is a part of Jerusalem, so A is arguable.

written:ISA-1-21:4.question: In Isaiah 1, what will happen to those who forsake the LORD?
written:ISA-1-21:4.why: also right: B, D: Verse 1:28-30 says those who forsake the LORD will perish, so A is the section's answer. Elsewhere in Scripture, forsaking the LORD is also tied to scattering among the nations (Deut 4:27; 28:64) and exile (Lev 26:33; Deut 28:36), so B and D could be argued from other passages, though this section does not state them.

written:ISA-3-1:5.question: In Isaiah 3, what does the LORD say will happen to the righteous?
written:ISA-3-1:5.answer: It will be well with them; they will enjoy the fruit of their labor

written:ISA-5-8:2.question: In Isaiah's woe against drinkers, what is missing from the feasts where the lyre and harp are played, according to Isaiah 5:12?
written:ISA-5-8:2.answer: They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see His handiwork

written:ISA-9-13:1.question: In Isaiah 9, whom does the text say is the "tail" that the LORD will cut off from Israel?

written:ISA-10-5:5.question: In Isaiah 10, why does the Lord say He will punish the king of Assyria?
written:ISA-10-5:5.answer: For the fruit of his arrogant heart and the proud look in his eyes

written:ISA-10-20:1.question: In Isaiah 10, what does God say will happen to the survivors of the house of Jacob "on that day" regarding the one who struck them?
written:ISA-10-20:1.answer: They will no longer depend on him but will rely on the LORD

written:ISA-11-1:4.question: In Isaiah 11:5, what will be the sash around the waist of the coming Branch of Jesse?
written:ISA-11-1:4.why: picked B without the text, not the writer's C: Isaiah 11:5 says righteousness is the belt of his waist and faithfulness the belt of his loins, so faithfulness (C) is also a belt in the same verse; the question's 'waist' points to righteousness.

written:ISA-13-1:6.question: In Isaiah 13, what will happen to the sun, moon, and stars on the Day of the LORD?
written:ISA-13-1:6.answer: They will not give their light
written:ISA-13-1:6.why: also right: B, C: Isaiah 13:10 says the stars and moon will not give light and the sun will be darkened, so A is the closest match. B (moon turns to blood) and C (stars fall) are not in Isaiah 13, but Joel 2:31 and Acts 2:20 put the moon turning to blood on the Day of the LORD, and Matthew 24:29 and Revelation 6:13 have stars falling. A strict key should note this.

written:ISA-13-1:7.question: In Isaiah 13, the LORD says He will make mankind rarer than the gold of which place?
written:ISA-13-1:7.why: also right: A, B, D: Isaiah 13:12 names only Ophir, so C is the answer in this text. Other places are linked to gold elsewhere: Havilah has gold (Genesis 2:11), Sheba brought gold to Solomon (1 Kings 10:2, 10), and ships of Tarshish brought gold (1 Kings 10:22). None is the place named in Isaiah 13, but a strict key should note them.

written:ISA-14-1:1.question: In Isaiah 14:1, what will the LORD feel toward Jacob as He once again chooses Israel and settles them in their own land?
written:ISA-14-1:1.why: also right: D: Isaiah 14:1 says the LORD "will have compassion on Jacob." Great delight (D) is not stated in this section, but other passages say God rejoices over or takes great delight in Israel (e.g., Zephaniah 3:17), so it could fairly be argued.

written:ISA-14-3:8.question: In Isaiah 14, what does the LORD of Hosts say He will make Babylon into when He sweeps her away with the broom of destruction?
written:ISA-14-3:8.answer: A place for owls and for swamplands
written:ISA-14-3:8.why: not clear on its own: Isaiah 14:23 says Babylon becomes a possession of the hedgehog and pools of water, and no option names a hedgehog. D is closest (pools of water ~ swamplands; owls appear in Isaiah 13:21 about Babylon), but the keyed answer does not match the verse, so the question or choices need revising.

written:ISA-14-24:2.question: In Isaiah 14:25, what does the LORD say will happen to Assyria's yoke and burden as He breaks Assyria in His land?
written:ISA-14-24:2.answer: They will be taken off and removed from His people's shoulders
written:ISA-14-24:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-18-1:4.question: In Isaiah 18, at the time of judgment, where will gifts from the tall, smooth-skinned people be brought to the LORD of Hosts?
written:ISA-18-1:4.answer: Mount Zion, the place of the Name of the LORD of Hosts
written:ISA-18-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-19-1:3.question: In the LORD's message against Egypt, how will He stir up the Egyptians against one another?
written:ISA-19-1:3.answer: Egyptian against Egyptian, brother against brother, city against city
written:ISA-19-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-21-1:2.question: In Isaiah 21, which two peoples are called on to go up and lay siege against the city whose groaning God will end?
written:ISA-21-1:2.why: not clear on its own: The question never names the city; it refers only to 'the city whose groaning God will end,' and the phrasing is garbled. A reader would have to already know the passage is about Babylon. The Bible answer is Elam and Media (Isaiah 21:2).

written:ISA-26-1:3.question: In Isaiah 26:4, how is GOD the LORD described as a reason to trust in Him forever?
written:ISA-26-1:3.why: also right: A, C: 26:4 names only 'the Rock eternal,' but the Bible elsewhere calls God a fortress for Jacob (Ps 46:7, 11) and an everlasting light (Isa 60:19-20), so those options are true of God, though not the description given in this verse.

written:ISA-27-1:2.question: In Isaiah's song about the fruitful vineyard, what does the LORD say He does for it continually?
written:ISA-27-1:2.why: not clear on its own: The watering line ("every moment I water it") is in Isaiah 27:2-3, but "fruitful vineyard" points to Isaiah 5:1 ("a very fruitful hill"), and the Isaiah 5 song has no line about the LORD watering it. The question should name which vineyard song it means.

written:ISA-27-1:4.question: According to Isaiah 27:6, what will Israel do in the days to come, when Jacob takes root?
written:ISA-27-1:4.answer: Bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit
written:ISA-27-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-27-1:6.question: In Isaiah 27, what will happen when the great ram's horn sounds "in that day"?
written:ISA-27-1:6.answer: Those perishing in Assyria and exiles in Egypt will come and worship the LORD in Jerusalem

written:ISA-29-1:2.question: In Isaiah's message against Ariel, what will the LORD do to the city, building towers and siege works against it?
written:ISA-29-1:2.answer: Camp in a circle around it and besiege it
written:ISA-29-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-29-1:3.question: In Isaiah 29, how will Ariel's voice sound when it is brought low?
written:ISA-29-1:3.answer: Like a spirit from the ground, whispering out of the dust
written:ISA-29-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-30-18:1.question: In Isaiah 30:18, what does the LORD long to be toward his people, according to the verse?

written:ISA-30-18:7.question: In Isaiah 30:31, what nation will be shattered at the voice of the LORD?
written:ISA-30-18:7.why: also right: C: Section names Assyria as the nation shattered at the LORD's voice. Babylon is also said to be shattered by the LORD elsewhere (Jeremiah 51:8), though not at His voice in the same wording, so C is a weak but arguable alternative; the section itself settles A.

written:ISA-31-1:3.question: In Isaiah 31:4, to what animal does the LORD compare Himself as He comes down to do battle on Mount Zion?
written:ISA-31-1:3.answer: A lion roaring over its prey
written:ISA-31-1:3.why: also right: C: Isaiah 31:4 settles it as a lion. Hosea 13:8 elsewhere has the LORD compared to a bear robbed of her cubs, so C is true of the LORD in another passage, though not in this verse.

written:ISA-32-9:3.question: According to Isaiah 32, what event will end the desolation of the land, turning the desert into an orchard?
written:ISA-32-9:3.answer: The Spirit being poured out from on high
written:ISA-32-9:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-40-6:1.question: In Isaiah 40, what does the voice say "stands forever" while the grass withers and the flowers fall?
written:ISA-40-6:1.why: also right: A: Choice A is not what the voice says in Isaiah 40, but other Scripture says David's kingdom or house endures forever (2 Samuel 7:16; Psalm 89:36-37), so it could be argued for. The section itself settles B: 'the word of our God stands forever.'

written:ISA-40-9:2.question: In Isaiah 40, to what are the nations compared when set before the LORD?
written:ISA-40-9:2.answer: A drop in a bucket and a speck of dust on the scales

written:ISA-40-9:3.question: In Isaiah 40, what does the prophet say a craftsman does when making an idol to compare to God?
written:ISA-40-9:3.answer: Casts it, and a metalworker overlays it with gold and fits it with silver chains

written:ISA-40-9:5.question: In Isaiah 40, what does God ask people to look up at in order to see who created all things, and how does He lead them forth?
written:ISA-40-9:5.answer: The starry host, which He leads forth by number and calls each by name

written:ISA-40-9:6.question: In Isaiah 40, what complaint did Jacob and Israel make that the LORD answers?
written:ISA-40-9:6.answer: "My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God"

written:ISA-41-21:2.question: In Isaiah 41, how does the LORD describe the idols and their work when he challenges them to present their case?
written:ISA-41-21:2.answer: They are nothing and their work is of no value
written:ISA-41-21:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-44-1:5.question: In Isaiah 44, the LORD tells Israel, “You are My witnesses!” What does He say there is besides Himself?
written:ISA-44-1:5.why: also right: B: 44:8 gives "There is no other Rock." B is not stated here, but Isaiah 43:11 says "there is no savior besides Me" and 44:6 calls Him "King and Redeemer," so "no other Savior-King" could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture, though it is not the wording of this verse.

written:ISA-46-1:4.question: In Isaiah 46:7, what happens when people cry out to the idol they have set in its place?
written:ISA-46-1:4.answer: It does not answer and saves no one from trouble
written:ISA-46-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-47-1:2.question: In Isaiah 47:4, what does the prophet call the LORD of Hosts, who judges Babylon?
written:ISA-47-1:2.answer: Our Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel
written:ISA-47-1:2.why: also right: B: 47:4 gives 'Our Redeemer... Holy One of Israel' (C). B's titles are not in this verse, but 'Mighty One of Jacob' is a real title for God elsewhere in Isaiah (49:26, 60:16) and 'Deliverer' is close in sense to 'Redeemer'.

written:ISA-47-1:3.question: According to Isaiah 47, why did the LORD place His people under Babylon's control?
written:ISA-47-1:3.answer: He was angry with His people and profaned His heritage
written:ISA-47-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-51-1:8.question: In Isaiah 51:12-13, what has Zion forgotten that leaves her living in terror of the oppressor?
written:ISA-51-1:8.answer: The LORD, her Maker, who stretched out the heavens
written:ISA-51-1:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-52-1:4.question: In Isaiah 52:12, as the people leave, who does the LORD say will be their rear guard?
written:ISA-52-1:4.why: also right: A: Isaiah 52:12 names the God of Israel as rear guard. Exodus 14:19 says the angel of God moved to the rear of Israel's camp between them and Egypt, so A has a fair scriptural argument, though this section does not mention the angel.

written:ISA-54-1:3.question: In Isaiah 54, what name is given to the One who is the Redeemer of the afflicted woman?
written:ISA-54-1:3.why: also right: D: 54:5 names the Holy One of Israel as Redeemer, so B is settled by the text. But Isaiah 49:26 calls the LORD 'your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob,' so D is also a fair answer from elsewhere in Scripture. The question's 'afflicted woman' wording is loose, since the afflicted city appears only in 54:11.

written:ISA-57-3:3.question: According to Isaiah 57, to which false god did the people go with oil and multiplied perfumes?
written:ISA-57-3:3.why: not clear on its own: Isaiah 57:9 says only "the king" (Hebrew melek), and no god is named in the chapter. Molech is the usual reading, but the question's premise that the chapter names a false god is not met, and Baal (choice D) is not mentioned in chapter 57.

written:ISA-57-14:2.question: In Isaiah 57:20, to what does the LORD compare the wicked because they cannot be still?
written:ISA-57-14:2.answer: The storm-tossed sea churning up mire and muck
written:ISA-57-14:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-61-1:1.question: In Isaiah 61, what does the speaker say he will be given to replace ashes for those who mourn in Zion?
written:ISA-61-1:1.why: not clear on its own: Isaiah 61:3 (NIV) has the mourners in Zion receiving 'a crown of beauty instead of ashes,' but the question says the speaker will be given it, which misstates the recipient.

written:ISA-62-1:6.question: In Isaiah 62, what does the LORD say is with Him when Daughter Zion's Savior comes?
written:ISA-62-1:6.why: also right: C, D: Verse 11 says 'His reward is with Him,' so A is the stated answer. Elsewhere Scripture describes the LORD coming with holy ones/angels (Zech 14:5; 2 Thess 1:7), so D is true of the coming LORD, though not what this verse says. C (sword) is weaker: Rev 19:15 shows a sharp sword from the mouth of the returning Christ, so it is arguable but a stretch.
