written:ISA-63-7:2.question: In Isaiah 63, who saved Israel in all their distress, according to the prophet's recollection of the LORD's mercies?
written:ISA-63-7:2.why: also right: A: 63:9 names the Angel of His Presence as the one who saved them. A, the Angel of the covenant (Mal 3:1), is a different title; some identify it with the same divine messenger, so it is arguable but not the section's answer.

written:ISA-63-15:2.question: In the prayer of Isaiah 63:17-18, what do the people say their enemies have done to the LORD's sanctuary after Israel possessed His holy place for a short while?
written:ISA-63-15:2.why: also right: A: Choice A is not said in this prayer, but Psalm 74:7 says the enemies 'burned Your sanctuary to the ground,' so it is true elsewhere in Scripture; this section's wording ('trampled') settles the answer.

written:ISA-65-1:1.question: In Isaiah 65:1, what does the LORD say about those who found Him, though they did not seek Him?
written:ISA-65-1:1.answer: He revealed Himself to those who did not ask for Him
written:ISA-65-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:ISA-65-1:4.question: In Isaiah 65:5, what do the rebellious people say to others because they think themselves holy?
written:ISA-65-1:4.answer: “Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!”

written:ISA-65-17:3.question: In Isaiah 65:24, what does the LORD promise about His people's calling and speaking to Him?
written:ISA-65-17:3.answer: He will answer before they call and hear while they are still speaking

written:ISA-66-1:1.question: In Isaiah 66:1, what does the LORD say is His footstool?
written:ISA-66-1:1.why: also right: A: Isaiah 66:1 says earth is God's footstool. Scripture elsewhere calls the temple or sanctuary His footstool (1 Chronicles 28:2; Psalm 132:7; Lamentations 2:1), so the temple choice has a fair argument from other passages, though this section does not say it.

written:ISA-66-1:2.question: In Isaiah 66:2, whom does the LORD say He will esteem?
written:ISA-66-1:2.answer: The one humble and contrite in spirit who trembles at His word
written:ISA-66-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-1-1:3.question: After Jeremiah protested that he did not know how to speak, what did the LORD do to him?
written:JER-1-1:3.answer: He touched Jeremiah's mouth with His hand
written:JER-1-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-1-1:5.question: In Jeremiah's vision of the boiling pot, from which direction was the pot tilting toward them?
written:JER-1-1:5.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: C: Jeremiah 1:13-14 says evil breaks out from the north. Some translations (e.g., ESV) say the pot is tilting away from the north, so a reader could argue the tilt points south toward Judah.

written:JER-2-1:3.question: In Jeremiah 2:3, what does the LORD call Israel, and what happened to those who devoured her?
written:JER-2-1:3.answer: Holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest; they were found guilty

written:JER-2-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 2:5-6, what did the people's fathers fail to ask about the LORD, who had brought them out of Egypt?
written:JER-2-1:4.answer: “Where is the LORD who brought us up from the land of Egypt?”

written:JER-3-11:7.question: In the days of restoration, what will Jerusalem be called?
written:JER-3-11:7.why: also right: C: Section names Jerusalem 'The Throne of the LORD' (3:17). Choice C is not the section's name, but Psalm 48:1 calls Jerusalem/Zion 'His holy mountain' and Zechariah 8:3 speaks of Jerusalem and 'the Holy Mountain', so C is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JER-4-1:1.question: In Jeremiah 4, what does the LORD warn will happen to Judah and Jerusalem if they do not circumcise their hearts?
written:JER-4-1:1.answer: His wrath will break out like fire with no one to extinguish it

written:JER-4-5:3.question: When the LORD warns of the coming disaster in Jeremiah 4, what are the people told to blow throughout the land?
written:JER-4-5:3.why: also right: D: The section says ram's horn, which is C. D is also a ram's horn in the broader Bible (Leviticus 25:9 jubilee trumpet, yobel), but this section does not mention Jubilee, so the section alone rules D out.

written:JER-5-14:4.question: In Jeremiah 5, when the people ask why the LORD has done these things to them, what are they to be told?
written:JER-5-14:4.answer: As they served foreign gods in their land, they will serve foreigners in a land not their own

written:JER-5-14:6.question: In Jeremiah 5, what does the LORD say the people have not said in their hearts about the rains?
written:JER-5-14:6.answer: Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rains in season

written:JER-5-14:8.question: In Jeremiah 5, what do the wicked men fail to do for the fatherless and the needy?
written:JER-5-14:8.answer: Take up the cause of the fatherless and defend the rights of the needy

written:JER-6-1:5.question: Why does Jeremiah say he cannot get the people of Jerusalem to listen to his warning?
written:JER-6-1:5.answer: Their ears are closed, and the LORD's word offends them
written:JER-6-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-7-1:3.question: What deceptive words did the people of Judah chant, trusting that the temple would keep them safe?
written:JER-7-1:3.answer: “This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.”

written:JER-7-30:3.question: In Jeremiah 7, what did the LORD say He would remove from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
written:JER-7-30:3.answer: The sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of bride and bridegroom

written:JER-8-1:3.question: In the LORD's message in Jeremiah 8:4-5, what two questions about falling and turning away does He ask to show how strange Jerusalem's behavior is?
written:JER-8-1:3.answer: Do men fall and not get up again? Does one turn away and not return?

written:JER-9-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 9, when the people ask why the land is destroyed and scorched, what reason does the LORD give?
written:JER-9-1:4.answer: They forsook His law and did not obey His voice
written:JER-9-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-10-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 10, what does the LORD tell Israel not to be terrified by, though the nations are terrified by them?
written:JER-10-1:4.why: also right: B: Verse 2 names the signs in the heavens, and the question's clause 'though the nations are terrified by them' matches that verse. Verse 5 also tells Israel 'Do not fear' the idols, so B can be argued, but the nations-terrified clause points to the signs.

written:JER-10-17:1.question: In Jeremiah 10, what does the LORD say He will do to the inhabitants of the land at this time, so that they may be captured?
written:JER-10-17:1.why: also right: A: The section says the LORD will "sling out the inhabitants of the land." A is not in this section, but Jeremiah 13:24 has the LORD say "I will scatter them like chaff," so it is a fair paraphrase from elsewhere in the book.

written:JER-10-17:2.question: In Jeremiah 10, why have the shepherds not prospered and their flock been scattered?
written:JER-10-17:2.answer: They became senseless and did not seek the LORD
written:JER-10-17:2.why: also right: A: The section states the reason directly: the shepherds "have become senseless; they do not seek the LORD." A is arguable from the preceding verses of the same chapter (10:3-9 describe idols of wood overlaid with silver, and 10:8 calls idol-makers "senseless"), but the section does not connect the shepherds to those idols.

written:JER-10-17:4.question: In Jeremiah's prayer in chapter 10, what does he say about a man's way and his steps?
written:JER-10-17:4.answer: A man's way is not his own; no one directs his own steps

written:JER-11-1:1.question: In Jeremiah 11, what curse does the LORD pronounce on the man who does not obey the words of the covenant?
written:JER-11-1:1.answer: “Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant”

written:JER-11-1:3.question: When the LORD told Jeremiah about the covenant given to the forefathers, what promise did He attach to obeying Him?
written:JER-11-1:3.answer: “You will be My people, and I will be your God”
written:JER-11-1:3.why: also right: A, B: Section gives D. A (Exodus 19:5-6) and B (Deuteronomy 28:13) are also promises the LORD attached to obedience elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JER-11-1:6.question: According to Jeremiah 11, why did the LORD bring all the curses of the covenant on the forefathers?
written:JER-11-1:6.answer: They would not obey but followed the stubbornness of their evil hearts
written:JER-11-1:6.why: also right: B: Section gives A (disobedience and stubborn hearts). B, neglect of Sabbath years, is a cause of covenant curses and exile elsewhere (Leviticus 26:34-35; 2 Chronicles 36:21).

written:JER-12-5:3.question: In Jeremiah 12, what does the LORD say many shepherds have destroyed and trampled?
written:JER-12-5:3.answer: His vineyard, his plot of ground
written:JER-12-5:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-14-1:3.question: What did the prophets tell the people in Jeremiah 14 that Jeremiah reported to the LORD?
written:JER-14-1:3.answer: They would not see sword or famine, but have lasting peace
written:JER-14-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-14-1:5.question: In Jeremiah 14, what will happen to the people who listened to the false prophets, according to the LORD?
written:JER-14-1:5.answer: They will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem with no one to bury them

written:JER-15-10:3.question: In Jeremiah 15, why does Jeremiah say the LORD's words were his joy?
written:JER-15-10:3.answer: Because he bears the LORD's name, the God of Hosts
written:JER-15-10:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-15-10:4.question: Why did Jeremiah say he sat alone and did not sit with the band of revelers?
written:JER-15-10:4.answer: Because the LORD's hand was on him
written:JER-15-10:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-16-1:1.question: In Jeremiah 16, what did the LORD command Jeremiah not to do in that place, as a sign of the coming disaster?
written:JER-16-1:1.answer: Marry or have sons or daughters
written:JER-16-1:1.why: not clear on its own: "That place" has no referent in the question, so a quiz-taker cannot tell which place is meant. Jeremiah 16:2 does command him not to take a wife or have sons or daughters "in this place"; name the place (e.g., Jerusalem or the land of Judah) to fix it.

written:JER-16-1:2.question: In Jeremiah 16, how did the LORD say the sons, daughters, and parents born in the land would die and be left?
written:JER-16-1:2.answer: Deadly diseases, sword, and famine, unburied like dung on the ground
written:JER-16-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-16-1:3.question: In Jeremiah 16, why did the LORD tell Jeremiah not to enter a house of mourning to show sympathy?
written:JER-16-1:3.answer: He had removed His peace, loving devotion, and compassion from the people
written:JER-16-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-16-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 16, what did the LORD say He would remove from the place before the eyes of the people in their days?
written:JER-16-1:4.answer: The sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom

written:JER-16-1:5.question: In Jeremiah 16, when the people asked why the LORD had pronounced such disaster, what was the first reason Jeremiah was to give?
written:JER-16-1:5.answer: Their fathers forsook the LORD and served and worshiped other gods
written:JER-16-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-16-1:7.question: In Jeremiah 16, what did the LORD say He would do to the people because of their sin, and what would they do there?
written:JER-16-1:7.answer: Cast them into an unknown land, where they would serve other gods day and night

written:JER-16-14:1.question: In Jeremiah 16, what will the people say in the days to come, instead of speaking of the LORD who brought the Israelites out of Egypt?
written:JER-16-14:1.answer: The LORD brought them up from the land of the north and all the other lands

written:JER-16-14:3.question: In Jeremiah 16, why does the LORD say He will first repay the people double for their iniquity and sin?
written:JER-16-14:3.answer: They defiled His land with the carcasses of detestable idols and filled His inheritance with abominations

written:JER-18-1:5.question: In Jeremiah 18, what does the LORD tell Jeremiah to say to the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem to do?
written:JER-18-1:5.answer: Turn from their evil ways and correct their deeds
written:JER-18-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-18-1:7.question: In Jeremiah 18, what do the people burn incense to after they have forgotten the LORD?
written:JER-18-1:7.why: also right: B, C, D: The section says worthless idols (A). Elsewhere Jeremiah 19:13 and 44:17-25 mention incense burned to the host of heaven / queen of heaven (B); 2 Kings 18:4 says Israel burned incense to the bronze serpent Nehushtan (D); 1 Kings 12:33 describes incense offered at Jeroboam's golden-calf altar at Bethel (C, the weakest of the three).

written:JER-19-1:3.question: Whom did the LORD tell Jeremiah to take with him when he went out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom with the clay jar?
written:JER-19-1:3.answer: Some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests
written:JER-19-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-19-1:5.question: In Jeremiah 19, what terrible thing had the people done at the high places of Baal that the LORD said He never commanded?
written:JER-19-1:5.answer: Burned their children in the fire as offerings to Baal
written:JER-19-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-20-7:2.question: In his complaint, why does Jeremiah say he is a laughingstock and mocked all day long?
written:JER-20-7:2.answer: The word of the LORD has become a reproach and derision to him

written:JER-21-1:6.question: According to the LORD's message through Jeremiah, what would happen to whoever went out of Jerusalem and surrendered to the Chaldeans?
written:JER-21-1:6.answer: He would live, keeping his life like a spoil of war
written:JER-21-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-21-11:2.question: In Jeremiah 21, what did the LORD say would happen to the house of David if they did not rescue the victim of robbery from the oppressor?
written:JER-21-11:2.answer: His wrath would go forth like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it

written:JER-22-13:3.question: In the LORD's rebuke of Jehoiakim, what did Josiah do that meant "it went well with him"?
written:JER-22-13:3.answer: He administered justice and righteousness and took up the cause of the poor and needy

written:JER-22-13:4.question: In Jeremiah 22:16, according to the LORD, what does it mean to know Him?
written:JER-22-13:4.answer: To take up the cause of the poor and needy
written:JER-22-13:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-22-13:5.question: What did the LORD say would happen to Jehoiakim son of Josiah at his death?
written:JER-22-13:5.answer: He will be buried like a donkey, dragged away and thrown outside Jerusalem's gates

written:JER-23-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 23:7-8, what will people say instead of "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt"?
written:JER-23-1:4.answer: The LORD brought Israel's descendants out of the land of the north and other lands

written:JER-23-9:4.question: In Jeremiah 23, what question does the LORD ask to show that a man cannot hide from Him in secret places?
written:JER-23-9:4.answer: "Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?"
written:JER-23-9:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-23-9:5.question: In Jeremiah 23, what two things does the LORD say His word is like?
written:JER-23-9:5.answer: Fire and a hammer that smashes a rock
written:JER-23-9:5.why: also right: A, D: The section settles C, but A (lamp and light) and D (rain and seed) are also metaphors for God's word elsewhere: Psalm 119:105 (lamp and light), Isaiah 55:10-11 (rain, seed), Luke 8:11 (seed = word).

written:JER-25-1:4.question: In Jeremiah 25, what did the LORD say He would do to the king of Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans when seventy years were complete?
written:JER-25-1:4.answer: Punish them for their guilt and make the land an everlasting desolation
written:JER-25-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-25-15:7.question: In Jeremiah 25:29, why did the LORD say the nations could not go unpunished?
written:JER-25-15:7.answer: He was already beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears His Name

written:JER-26-7:5.question: What did Jeremiah urge the officials and people to do so that the LORD might relent of the disaster He had pronounced?
written:JER-26-7:5.answer: Correct their ways and deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD
written:JER-26-7:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-26-16:1.question: When the officials and all the people answered the priests and prophets who wanted Jeremiah put to death, what reason did they give for sparing him?
written:JER-26-16:1.answer: He had spoken to them in the name of the LORD their God

written:JER-27-1:4.question: According to the LORD's message in Jeremiah 27, how did He say He made the earth and everything on it?
written:JER-27-1:4.answer: By His great power and outstretched arm
written:JER-27-1:4.why: also right: D: Jeremiah 27:5 gives A. Psalm 33:6 teaches that the heavens were made by the word and breath of the LORD, so D is a true creation statement elsewhere, but the question asks for the Jeremiah 27 message, which does not say it.

written:JER-27-1:5.question: What did the LORD say He would do to a nation that would not put its neck under Nebuchadnezzar's yoke?
written:JER-27-1:5.answer: Punish it by sword, famine, and plague until destroyed by his hand
written:JER-27-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-27-1:6.question: Whom did the LORD tell the nations not to listen to when they said, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon'?
written:JER-27-1:6.answer: Their prophets, diviners, interpreters of dreams, mediums, and sorcerers
written:JER-27-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-27-1:8.question: What did the prophets in Jerusalem falsely say would happen very soon, according to Jeremiah's words to the priests and people?
written:JER-27-1:8.answer: The articles from the LORD's house would be brought back from Babylon

written:JER-29-1:1.question: In his letter to the exiles in Babylon, what did the LORD tell them to do for the city to which He had sent them?
written:JER-29-1:1.answer: Seek its prosperity and pray to the LORD on its behalf
written:JER-29-1:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-29-1:4.question: In Jeremiah's letter to the exiles, what did the LORD say about the prophets and diviners among them?
written:JER-29-1:4.answer: They were falsely prophesying in His name, and He had not sent them

written:JER-30-1:7.question: In Jeremiah 30, what did the LORD say would be rebuilt on her own ruins?
written:JER-30-1:7.why: not clear on its own: "Her" has no antecedent in the question; a quiz-taker cannot tell who or what is meant. It should name the city (Jerusalem) or Israel. The answer is D (the city, Jer 30:18), but the wording needs fixing.

written:JER-31-26:5.question: In Jeremiah 31, what saying about sour grapes did the LORD say would no longer be said in those days?
written:JER-31-26:5.answer: "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge."

written:JER-31-26:6.question: In Jeremiah 31, the LORD said Israel's descendants would cease to be a nation before Him only if what happened?
written:JER-31-26:6.answer: If the fixed order of sun, moon, and stars departed from His presence

written:JER-31-26:7.question: In Jeremiah 31, the LORD said He would reject all of Israel's descendants only if what could be done?
written:JER-31-26:7.answer: If the heavens above were measured and the earth's foundations searched out

written:JER-32-16:4.question: In Jeremiah's prayer, how did he say the LORD brought Israel out of the land of Egypt?
written:JER-32-16:4.answer: With signs and wonders, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terror

written:JER-32-26:1.question: When the LORD answered Jeremiah about the city of Jerusalem, what rhetorical question did He ask about Himself?
written:JER-32-26:1.why: also right: A, D: The section (32:27) has the LORD ask "Is anything too difficult for Me?" A is a near paraphrase of Jeremiah 23:24, and D is close to Numbers 11:23 ("Is the LORD's arm too short?"), both rhetorical questions from the LORD elsewhere in Scripture, though not in this answer.

written:JER-32-26:5.question: In Jeremiah 32, where did the people build high places of Baal to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire to Molech?
written:JER-32-26:5.why: also right: B: 32:35 places the high places of Baal in the Valley of Hinnom. B (Mount of Olives) is arguably right elsewhere: 1 Kings 11:7 has Solomon build a high place for Molech on the mountain east of Jerusalem, traditionally identified with the Mount of Olives.

written:JER-33-14:2.question: In Jeremiah's prophecy of the righteous Branch, what will Jerusalem be called?
written:JER-33-14:2.why: also right: A: Ezekiel 48:35 gives the city the name "The LORD Is There" (YHWH Shammah), though that name is not in Jeremiah 33.

written:JER-33-14:3.question: In the LORD's promise through Jeremiah, what will David never lack?
written:JER-33-14:3.answer: A man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel
written:JER-33-14:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-33-14:4.question: In Jeremiah 33, what will the priests who are Levites never fail to have?
written:JER-33-14:4.answer: A man before the LORD to offer sacrifices
written:JER-33-14:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-34-1:2.question: When the LORD spoke to Zedekiah through Jeremiah, what did He say He was about to do to Jerusalem?
written:JER-34-1:2.answer: Deliver it into the hand of the king of Babylon, who would burn it down

written:JER-34-8:3.question: After the officials and people of Judah agreed to the covenant of liberty, what did they later do to the slaves they had freed?
written:JER-34-8:3.answer: They took them back and forced them to become slaves again
written:JER-34-8:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-35-1:5.question: Why did the Rechabites say they were living in Jerusalem when Jeremiah met them?
written:JER-35-1:5.answer: To escape the armies of the Chaldeans and the Arameans
written:JER-35-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-35-12:1.question: In Jeremiah 35, what command of their forefather Jonadab son of Rechab had his sons obeyed to this very day?
written:JER-35-12:1.why: also right: C: Section names wine (35:14). Planting vineyards was also a command of Jonadab, given in Jeremiah 35:7-9 outside this section, so C is arguably right too.

written:JER-35-12:4.question: In Jeremiah 35, what did the LORD say through the prophets that Judah must not do?
written:JER-35-12:4.answer: Go after other gods to serve them
written:JER-35-12:4.why: also right: A, B: Section states C directly (35:15). A is a narrower form of serving other gods and is condemned elsewhere by the prophets, e.g. Jeremiah's and Deuteronomy's teaching on high places. B is arguable because 35:15 also commands them to live in the land, which implies not leaving it. Neither A nor B is stated as a prohibition in this section.

written:JER-35-12:5.question: In Jeremiah 35, what did the LORD promise the house of the Rechabites because they obeyed Jonadab?
written:JER-35-12:5.answer: Jonadab will never fail to have a man to stand before Him
written:JER-35-12:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-36-1:2.question: According to Jeremiah 36:3, why did the LORD want the words written down and heard by the people of Judah?
written:JER-36-1:2.answer: Perhaps each would turn from his wicked way, and God would forgive
written:JER-36-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-36-1:3.question: When Jeremiah had Baruch write his words on a scroll, which words was Baruch to write?
written:JER-36-1:3.answer: All the words the LORD had spoken to Jeremiah since Josiah's reign

written:JER-36-11:1.question: After Micaiah son of Gemariah heard the words of the LORD read from Jeremiah's scroll, where did he go to report them?
written:JER-36-11:1.answer: The scribe's chamber in the king's palace, where the officials sat

written:JER-36-11:3.question: After the officials heard Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll, how did they react, and what did they say they must do?
written:JER-36-11:3.answer: They turned to one another in fear and said they must report the words to the king

written:JER-36-11:4.question: When the officials asked Baruch how he wrote all the words on the scroll, what did Baruch answer?
written:JER-36-11:4.answer: Jeremiah recited the words, and Baruch wrote them in ink on the scroll

written:JER-36-20:2.question: When Jehudi read the scroll to King Jehoiakim, what did the king do as each three or four columns were read?
written:JER-36-20:2.answer: He cut them off with a scribe’s knife and threw them into the firepot

written:JER-36-20:3.question: After Jehoiakim burned the scroll, whom did he command Jerahmeel, Seraiah and Shelemiah to seize, and what happened to them?
written:JER-36-20:3.answer: Baruch and Jeremiah; the LORD had hidden them
written:JER-36-20:3.why: also right: C: C's first half is correct, and Jeremiah 36:19 (outside this section) says the officials told Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. That warning came before the king's command, though, so it is not what happened to them after the seizure order, which the section answers as D.

written:JER-36-27:2.question: In Jeremiah 36, what did Jehoiakim king of Judah object to in the scroll, according to the LORD's message?
written:JER-36-27:2.answer: That it said the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy the land

written:JER-36-27:3.question: What did the LORD say would happen to the body of Jehoiakim king of Judah?
written:JER-36-27:3.answer: It would be thrown out, exposed to heat by day and frost by night

written:JER-37-11:2.question: When King Zedekiah privately asked Jeremiah whether there was a word from the LORD, what did Jeremiah answer?

written:EZK-39-21:4.question: In Ezekiel 39, what will the house of Israel forget when they dwell securely in their land?
written:EZK-39-21:4.answer: Their disgrace and all their treachery against God
written:EZK-39-21:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EZK-40-5:2.question: In Ezekiel's vision, which gate of the temple area did the man go to, climbing its steps, and measure?
written:EZK-40-5:2.why: not clear on its own: Ezekiel 40:6 names the east gate as the first one he climbs and measures, but the question does not say 'first.' The outer north gate also has steps (40:22, seven steps), so the question does not single out one gate.

written:EZK-41-5:5.question: In Ezekiel 41, how wide was the open area between the side rooms and the outer chambers all around the temple?
written:EZK-41-5:5.why: also right: C: 41:10 gives the twenty cubits between the temple's side rooms and the outer chambers, matching the question's wording. But 41:11 says 'the open area was five cubits wide all around,' so the section gives two widths for the open area; C could fairly be argued.

written:EZK-41-15:2.question: In Ezekiel's vision, the carved cherubim on the temple walls each had two faces. One was the face of a man; what was the other?
written:EZK-41-15:2.answer: The face of a young lion
written:EZK-41-15:2.why: also right: A, D: The section settles it (young lion). Ox (A) and eagle (D) faces appear on the living creatures/cherubim of Ezekiel 1 and 10 elsewhere, so they are true of cherubim in general, though not of the cherubim in chapter 41.

written:EZK-43-13:3.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the altar's dedication, what is done with some of the bull's blood to cleanse the altar and make atonement for it?
written:EZK-43-13:3.answer: It is put on the four horns, the ledge corners, and the rim

written:EZK-44-1:1.question: In Ezekiel's vision, why did the LORD say the outer east gate of the sanctuary must remain shut?
written:EZK-44-1:1.answer: Because the LORD, the God of Israel, had entered through it
written:EZK-44-1:1.why: also right: C: Ezekiel 10:19 and 11:1 place the departing glory at the east gate of the LORD's house, so C is partly true elsewhere, but C gives the wrong reason; the section's stated reason is that the LORD entered through the gate.

written:EZK-44-6:4.question: In Ezekiel 44, what duties would the Levites who had gone astray still have in the sanctuary?
written:EZK-44-6:4.answer: Guarding the temple gates and slaughtering the burnt offerings for the people
written:EZK-44-6:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-44-6:5.question: In Ezekiel 44, what did the LORD forbid the Levites who had gone astray to do?
written:EZK-44-6:5.answer: Approach Him to serve as priests or come near the most holy things

written:EZK-44-15:3.question: In Ezekiel 44, why must the priests take off their ministering garments and leave them in the holy chambers before going out to the outer court?
written:EZK-44-15:3.answer: So they do not transmit holiness to the people with their garments
written:EZK-44-15:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-44-15:7.question: In Ezekiel 44, what does the Lord say is the priests' inheritance in Israel?
written:EZK-44-15:7.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:EZK-45-13:4.question: In Ezekiel 45, where was the priest to put some of the blood from the sin offering when the sanctuary was purified?
written:EZK-45-13:4.answer: On the doorposts of the temple, the ledge of the altar, and the gateposts of the inner court

written:EZK-45-13:7.question: In Ezekiel 45, on what date does the second seven-day feast begin, for which the prince makes the same provision?
written:EZK-45-13:7.answer: The fifteenth day of the seventh month
written:EZK-45-13:7.why: also right: A: Ezekiel 45:25 gives the 15th of the seventh month for the second seven-day feast, so D is the answer. But A (the 15th of the first month) is the start date of the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread (Lev 23:6), which falls in the Passover period; a reader who counts that as a second feast could argue for A. The section's 'second' feast is clearly the seventh-month one.

written:EZK-46-1:4.question: In Ezekiel's vision, what must the prince offer on the day of the New Moon as his burnt offering?
written:EZK-46-1:4.answer: A young bull, six lambs, and a ram, all unblemished
written:EZK-46-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-46-1:5.question: In Ezekiel's vision, when the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, how must they leave if they entered by the north gate?
written:EZK-46-1:5.answer: By the south gate, not the gate they entered
written:EZK-46-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-46-1:6.question: In Ezekiel's vision, what is offered every morning as a regular burnt offering to the LORD?
written:EZK-46-1:6.answer: An unblemished year-old lamb with grain offering and oil
written:EZK-46-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-46-19:1.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the temple, why were the priests to boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering in the holy chambers at the western end?
written:EZK-46-19:1.answer: So they would not transmit holiness to the people in the outer court

written:EZK-46-19:3.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the temple, what did the man say the ovens in the four corner courts of the outer court were for?
written:EZK-46-19:3.answer: Cooking the sacrifices offered by the people, by those who minister at the temple

written:EZK-47-1:3.question: In Ezekiel's vision, what did the man hold in his hand as he went eastward and measured off a thousand cubits?
written:EZK-47-1:3.why: also right: D: The section says the man held a measuring line. Ezekiel 40:3 and 40:5 describe the same guiding man holding a measuring reed, so D is also true of him elsewhere in Scripture.

written:EZK-47-1:5.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the river from the temple, what places marked the area where fishermen would spread their nets?
written:EZK-47-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:EZK-47-13:2.question: In Ezekiel 47, why does the Lord say the land will fall to Israel as an inheritance?
written:EZK-47-13:2.answer: Because He swore with an uplifted hand to give it to their forefathers

written:EZK-48-23:1.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the land divided among the tribes, which tribe's portion is bordered by the territory of Simeon on the south side of Benjamin's portion, with Simeon's portion next to Benjamin's?

written:EZK-48-30:1.question: In Ezekiel's vision of the new city, what will be the name of the city from that day on?
written:EZK-48-30:1.why: also right: B, C: Ezekiel 48:35 gives the name as THE LORD IS THERE. Elsewhere Jerusalem is called "the city of the Great King" (Psalm 48:2; Matthew 5:35) and "The LORD Is Our Righteousness" (Jeremiah 33:16), so B and C are other scriptural names for the same city, though not the name in this vision.

written:DAN-2-14:1.question: In Daniel 2, after the king ordered the wise men of Babylon destroyed, whom did Daniel ask for time to give the interpretation?

written:DAN-3-8:2.question: When Nebuchadnezzar asked what god could deliver them from his hands, what did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego say God was able to do?
written:DAN-3-8:2.answer: Deliver them from the blazing fiery furnace and from the king's hand

written:DAN-4-4:4.question: Why did Nebuchadnezzar believe Daniel could explain his dream, since no mystery baffled him?
written:DAN-4-4:4.answer: The spirit of the holy gods was in him
written:DAN-4-4:4.why: also right: D: Section gives the spirit of the holy gods as the reason. D is true elsewhere (Daniel 2 records Daniel interpreting the king's statue dream), so it could be argued as a reason, though the section does not state it.

written:DAN-4-4:6.question: In Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what happened to the beasts of the field and the birds of the air because of the great tree?
written:DAN-4-4:6.answer: The beasts found shelter under it and the birds nested in its branches

written:DAN-4-4:8.question: According to the decree of the watchers in Nebuchadnezzar's dream, why was this decision made?
written:DAN-4-4:8.answer: So the living will know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind

written:DAN-4-19:1.question: In Daniel 4, when Daniel explained King Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great tree, whom did the tree represent?
written:DAN-4-19:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DAN-4-19:6.question: What advice did Daniel give Nebuchadnezzar after interpreting the dream, in hope that his prosperity might be extended?
written:DAN-4-19:6.answer: Break away from sins by doing what is right and showing mercy to the oppressed

written:DAN-4-28:2.question: In Daniel 4, according to the voice from heaven, until Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged what would seven times pass over him?
written:DAN-4-28:2.answer: That the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind
written:DAN-4-28:2.why: not clear on its own: The wording is garbled: it reads as if the seven times pass over him until he acknowledges something, but the sentence structure is tangled. Rewrite as, e.g., "Until Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged what, did the voice from heaven say seven times would pass over him?" The content answer is C (Daniel 4:25, 32).

written:DAN-4-34:2.question: In Daniel 4:37, what does Nebuchadnezzar say the King of heaven is able to do to those who walk in pride?
written:DAN-4-34:2.answer: He is able to humble them
written:DAN-4-34:2.why: also right: B: Daniel 4:37 says the King 'is able to humble those who walk in pride,' so A is the answer. B is defensible from elsewhere in Scripture: Luke 1:51 says God 'has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.'

written:DAN-7-15:1.question: In Daniel's vision of the four great beasts, what did the interpreter say the four beasts are?
written:DAN-7-15:1.answer: Four kings who will arise from the earth
written:DAN-7-15:1.why: also right: C: C is arguable: the beasts rose out of the great sea in the vision (7:2-3), and 7:23 calls them kingdoms. But the interpreter's own words in 7:17 are 'four kings who will arise from the earth,' so A is the answer.

written:DAN-8-1:6.question: In Daniel's vision, what happened to the goat's large horn at the height of his power?
written:DAN-8-1:6.answer: It was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place

written:DAN-9-20:3.question: When Gabriel explained the vision to Daniel, why did he say an answer had gone out at the beginning of Daniel's petitions?
written:DAN-9-20:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DAN-10-1:3.question: What did the heavenly messenger tell Daniel about why his words had been heard, when he said not to be afraid?
written:DAN-10-1:3.answer: From the first day he purposed to understand and humble himself before God

written:DAN-10-1:5.question: According to the messenger in Daniel 10, what vision did he come to explain to Daniel about his people?
written:DAN-10-1:5.answer: What will happen to Daniel's people in the latter days
written:DAN-10-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DAN-11-1:2.question: According to Daniel 11, what will the fourth king of Persia, who is far richer than all the others, do by the power of his wealth?
written:DAN-11-1:2.answer: Stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece
written:DAN-11-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-11-1:3.question: In Daniel's vision of the mighty king who rules with great authority, what will happen to his kingdom as soon as he is established?
written:DAN-11-1:3.answer: It will be broken up toward the four winds of heaven
written:DAN-11-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-11-1:5.question: In Daniel 11, what will the one from the daughter's family line take captive to Egypt after prevailing against the king of the North?
written:DAN-11-1:5.answer: Their gods, with metal images and precious vessels of silver and gold
written:DAN-11-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-11-1:7.question: In Daniel 11, how will the despicable person who takes the place of the tax-collector's sender seize the kingdom?
written:DAN-11-1:7.answer: By intrigue, in a time of peace
written:DAN-11-1:7.why: not clear on its own: "The tax-collector's sender" is an unnamed king from the previous verse (Daniel 11:20), so the question doesn't say whom it means. Read against Daniel 11:21, the answer is C (intrigue, in a time of peace), but the wording should name the king or give the verse.

written:DAN-11-1:8.question: In Daniel 11, what will the forces of the king of the North do to the temple fortress and the daily sacrifice?
written:DAN-11-1:8.answer: Desecrate the fortress, abolish the daily sacrifice, and set up the abomination of desolation

written:DAN-11-36:4.question: In Daniel 11, which three peoples will be delivered from the hand of the king who invades the Beautiful Land?
written:DAN-11-36:4.answer: Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites
written:DAN-11-36:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-11-36:5.question: At the end of Daniel 11, where will the king pitch his royal tents before he meets his end with no one to help him?
written:DAN-11-36:5.answer: Between the sea and the beautiful holy mountain
written:DAN-11-36:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-12-1:3.question: According to Daniel 12:2, what will happen to many who sleep in the dust of the earth?
written:DAN-12-1:3.answer: They will awake, some to everlasting life and others to everlasting contempt
written:DAN-12-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DAN-12-1:6.question: In Daniel 12:7, how did the man dressed in linen swear when he answered how long until the wonders were fulfilled?
written:DAN-12-1:6.answer: He raised both hands toward heaven and swore by Him who lives forever

written:HOS-2-1:1.question: In Hosea 2:1, what name does the LORD tell the people to call their sisters?
written:HOS-2-1:1.why: not clear on its own: No choice is correct. In Hosea 2:1 the LORD tells them to call their sisters "Ruhamah" ("Pitied" or "You have received mercy"), which is not offered. Choice B ("sons of the living God") comes from the nearby verses about the brothers, not the sisters.

written:HOS-2-1:2.question: In Hosea 2, why does the LORD tell the children to rebuke their mother?
written:HOS-2-1:2.answer: She is not His wife, and He is not her husband
written:HOS-2-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:HOS-2-1:4.question: In Hosea 2:6, how does the LORD say He will stop the unfaithful mother from following her lovers?
written:HOS-2-1:4.answer: He will hedge up her path with thorns and enclose her with a wall

written:HOS-2-1:5.question: In Hosea 2:7, what does the unfaithful mother say when she cannot catch her lovers?
written:HOS-2-1:5.answer: “I will return to my first husband, for then I was better off than now.”

written:HOS-2-14:3.question: In Hosea 2, with which creatures does the LORD say He will make a covenant on the day He restores Israel?
written:HOS-2-14:3.answer: The beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and creatures that crawl

written:HOS-4-1:5.question: In Hosea 4:13, where did the people sacrifice and burn offerings, because the shade was pleasant?
written:HOS-4-1:5.answer: On the mountaintops and hills, under oak, poplar, and terebinth
written:HOS-4-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:HOS-5-1:5.question: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, to whom did Ephraim turn and send for help, according to Hosea 5:13?
written:HOS-5-1:5.why: also right: D: Section names Assyria and the great king. Elsewhere in Hosea (7:11; 12:1) Ephraim also seeks Egypt, so Pharaoh/Egypt is attested in Scripture, though not in this verse.

written:HOS-5-1:6.question: In Hosea 5:14, to what animal does the LORD compare Himself in relation to Ephraim, saying He will tear them to pieces?
written:HOS-5-1:6.why: also right: A, D: 5:14 says lion. Hosea 13:7-8 has God comparing Himself to a leopard by the road and to a bear robbed of her cubs, attacking Ephraim, so leopard and bear are also attested comparisons elsewhere in Hosea. The question's wording ties the answer to 5:14, so lion is the answer.

written:HOS-6-1:1.question: In Hosea 6:6, what does God say He desires rather than sacrifice?
written:HOS-6-1:1.why: also right: A: Hosea 6:6 says God desires mercy, not sacrifice. Obedience is also defensible from 1 Samuel 15:22 ("To obey is better than sacrifice"), though Hosea does not use that word.

written:HOS-7-1:4.question: In Hosea 7:2, what do the people of Ephraim fail to consider in their hearts?
written:HOS-7-1:4.answer: That the LORD remembers all their evil
written:HOS-7-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:HOS-8-1:3.question: In Hosea 8, what did the LORD say about the kings and princes Israel set up?
written:HOS-8-1:3.answer: They were not set up by Him or with His approval
written:HOS-8-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:HOS-10-1:5.question: In Hosea 10:7, to what is Samaria's king compared when Samaria is carried off?
written:HOS-10-1:5.answer: A twig on the surface of the water
written:HOS-10-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:HOS-12-1:4.question: In Hosea 12:13, whom did the LORD use to bring Israel out of Egypt and to preserve him?
written:HOS-12-1:4.why: also right: B, C: Verse 13 names only 'a prophet' (Moses, unnamed here). Moses also judged the people (Ex 18:13-26), and Psalm 99:6 counts Moses among the LORD's priests, so B and C could be argued; the section's wording points to D.

written:HOS-13-9:1.question: In Hosea 13, what does the LORD say he will do for Israel with respect to the power of Sheol?
written:HOS-13-9:1.answer: He will ransom them from the power of Sheol
written:HOS-13-9:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: Hosea 13:14 is rendered as a promise in the KJV and NIV ("I will ransom them from the power of the grave"), but the ESV reads it as a rhetorical question ("Shall I ransom them...?") that is answered by the judgment that follows, so B could be argued from that reading.

written:JOL-2-1:5.question: According to Joel 2:10, what happens to the sun, moon and stars as the army advances?
written:JOL-2-1:5.answer: The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness
written:JOL-2-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:AMO-2-1:2.question: According to Amos 2:4, why did the LORD pronounce judgment on Judah?
written:AMO-2-1:2.answer: They rejected the Law of the LORD and did not keep His statutes

written:AMO-8-1:4.question: In Amos 8, what kind of famine did the Lord GOD say He would send on the land?
written:AMO-8-1:4.answer: A famine of hearing the words of the LORD
written:AMO-8-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JON-1-4:1.question: When the sailors on the ship to Tarshish asked Jonah about himself, how did Jonah describe the God he worships?
written:JON-1-4:1.answer: The God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land

written:MIC-3-1:2.question: In Micah 3, what did the LORD say would happen when the leaders of Jacob cried out to Him because of their evil?
written:MIC-3-1:2.answer: He would not answer them and would hide His face
written:MIC-3-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MIC-3-1:4.question: In Micah 3:11, what did the leaders, priests and prophets of Jerusalem do for money while claiming the LORD was among them?
written:MIC-3-1:4.answer: Leaders judged for a bribe, priests taught for a price, prophets practiced divination

written:MIC-4-6:4.question: In Micah 4:12-13, why do the nations gathered against Zion fail to understand the LORD's plan, and what does He say He has done with them?
written:MIC-4-6:4.answer: He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor
written:MIC-4-6:4.why: not clear on its own: The question asks two things, but the choices answer only the second. Its 'why' part (why the nations fail to understand) has no matching option, and the text only says they do not know the LORD's thoughts or plan. The keyed answer C ('gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor') is correct for what He has done.

written:MIC-7-1:2.question: In Micah 7:3, who are said to demand a bribe?
written:MIC-7-1:2.why: also right: B: 7:3 names only the prince and the judge. Micah 3:11 elsewhere says the priests teach for a price and the prophets divine for money, so B is arguably true from elsewhere in the book, though 7:3 does not say it.

written:NAM-3-1:6.question: In Nahum 3, what does the LORD say Nineveh's troops are like?
written:NAM-3-1:6.why: also right: A: 3:13 says the troops are like women. But 3:17 compares Nineveh's guards to swarming locusts, and guards could fairly be counted as troops, so A is arguable. D is the direct answer to 'troops'.

written:HAB-3-1:6.question: According to Habakkuk 3, for what purpose did God go forth and march across the earth?
written:HAB-3-1:6.answer: For the salvation of His people, to save His anointed
written:HAB-3-1:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ZEC-1-7:4.question: In Zechariah's vision, why was the LORD fiercely angry with the nations that were at ease?
written:ZEC-1-7:4.answer: They added to the calamity when He was only a little angry
written:ZEC-1-7:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ZEC-3-1:4.question: In Zechariah's vision, what did the angel of the LORD promise Joshua if he walked in the LORD's ways and kept His instructions?
written:ZEC-3-1:4.answer: He would govern the LORD's house and have charge of His courts

written:ZEC-4-1:5.question: In Zechariah's vision, what did the angel say the two olive trees by the lampstand represent?
written:ZEC-4-1:5.answer: The two anointed ones standing beside the Lord of all the earth
written:ZEC-4-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ZEC-6-1:2.question: In Zechariah's vision of the four chariots, what did the angel say the chariots were?
written:ZEC-6-1:2.answer: The four spirits of heaven, going forth from their station before the Lord of all the earth

written:ZEC-6-9:2.question: In Zechariah 6, what name does the LORD of Hosts give to the man who will build the temple of the LORD?
written:ZEC-6-9:2.why: also right: B: The section gives 'The Branch' directly (6:12). Option B is arguably also right because Zechariah 3:8 calls the Branch 'My servant the Branch', though 'Servant' is not the name given in chapter 6. Options A and C are Messianic titles elsewhere (Cornerstone, Shepherd), but they are not names the LORD gives this man in Zechariah 6.

written:ZEC-7-1:1.question: In the fourth year of King Darius, the people of Bethel sent men to ask the priests and prophets whether they should continue what practice in the fifth month?
written:ZEC-7-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:ZEC-12-1:3.question: In Zechariah 12:4, what will the LORD strike every horse of the attacking nations with?
written:ZEC-12-1:3.why: the section does not settle it: Verse 4 says the LORD strikes 'every horse' with panic, but then says He strikes 'all the horses of the nations' with blindness. The question targets the attacking nations' horses, and the text gives blindness for them, which is not an option. Panic is the best fit only for the generic 'every horse' wording.

written:ZEC-12-1:5.question: In Zechariah 12:8, how will the house of David be on the day the LORD defends the people of Jerusalem?
written:ZEC-12-1:5.answer: Like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them
written:ZEC-12-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ZEC-14-1:2.question: In Zechariah's vision of the day of the LORD, where will the LORD's feet stand when He fights against the nations?
written:ZEC-14-1:2.answer: On the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem
written:ZEC-14-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ZEC-14-1:3.question: In Zechariah 14, what will happen to the Mount of Olives when the LORD's feet stand on it?
written:ZEC-14-1:3.answer: It will be split in two from east to west, forming a great valley

written:MAL-2-1:2.question: In Malachi 2, with which ancestor of the priests did the LORD say He had made a covenant of life and peace?
written:MAL-2-1:2.why: also right: B: Malachi 2:4-5 names Levi. Phinehas also received a covenant of peace from the LORD in Numbers 25:12-13, so B is defensible from elsewhere in Scripture, though this section does not name him.

written:MAL-2-1:3.question: In Malachi 2, how did the LORD describe the priest Levi's response to the covenant of life and peace, which called for reverence?
written:MAL-2-1:3.answer: He revered the LORD and stood in awe of His name
written:MAL-2-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:MAL-2-10:1.question: In Malachi 2:11, how does the prophet say Judah profaned the LORD's beloved sanctuary?
written:MAL-2-10:1.answer: By marrying the daughter of a foreign god
written:MAL-2-10:1.why: also right: A, C: Malachi 2:11 names marriage to the daughter of a foreign god as the profaning. Elsewhere, idols set up in the temple profane it (Ezekiel 8), and Malachi 1:7-8, 12 say the defiled or blind and lame offerings on the altar profane it, so A and C could fairly be argued, though the prophet's stated cause here is D.

written:MAL-2-10:3.question: According to Malachi 2:14, why did the LORD no longer accept the offerings of the people?
written:MAL-2-10:3.answer: He was a witness between them and the wife of their youth, whom they had betrayed

written:MAL-2-10:4.question: In Malachi 2:16, what does the LORD, the God of Israel, say that He hates?
written:MAL-2-10:4.why: also right: B, C: Malachi 2:16 says 'For I hate divorce.' Scripture elsewhere says the LORD hates idolatry (Deuteronomy 12:31; 16:22) and pride (Proverbs 8:13), so B and C are true of God in other passages, though the section only names divorce.

written:MAT-9-27:3.question: When the crowds saw Jesus drive a demon out of a mute man so that he spoke, who accused Jesus of driving out demons by the prince of demons?
written:MAT-9-27:3.why: also right: A: Mark 3:22 says the scribes who came down from Jerusalem made the same charge ("by the prince of demons he drives out demons"), so option A is also right elsewhere in Scripture. The section itself names only the Pharisees, so D is the answer this section shows.

written:MAT-9-35:1.question: In Matthew 9, when Jesus saw the crowds and was moved with compassion, what were the crowds like, according to the verse?

written:MAT-10-5:2.question: When Jesus sent out the twelve, what did He say would be more bearable on the day of judgment than for a town that refused to welcome them?
written:MAT-10-5:2.why: also right: C: Matt 10:15 names Sodom and Gomorrah directly. Elsewhere, Matt 11:22 says Tyre and Sidon will fare more bearably than the unrepentant towns of Chorazin and Bethsaida, so Tyre and Sidon is a defensible answer from another passage, though the section itself does not mention it.

written:MAT-11-1:1.question: When John the Baptist heard in prison about the works of Christ, what did he do?
written:MAT-11-1:1.answer: He sent his disciples to ask Jesus if He was the One to come

written:MAT-12-22:1.question: In Matthew 12, when the Pharisees heard the crowds wondering about Jesus after He healed a blind and mute demon-possessed man, whom did they say He drove out demons by?
written:MAT-12-22:1.why: also right: C: The Pharisees say "Beelzebul, the prince of demons"; Beelzebul is also a name for Satan (Matt 10:25; Luke 11:15-18), and Jesus' reply in 12:26 treats the charge as Satan vs. Satan, so C is arguably also right.

written:MAT-12-46:1.question: In Matthew 12, when Jesus' mother and brothers stood outside wanting to speak to Him, whom did Jesus point to as His mother and brothers?
written:MAT-12-46:1.why: also right: A: Jesus points to 'His disciples.' Choice A, the twelve he sent out, is a narrower subset of the disciples, so it could be argued, but the passage names the group as disciples, not the twelve.

written:MAT-14-34:1.question: After Jesus and His disciples crossed the lake, at which place did they land?
written:MAT-14-34:1.why: not clear on its own: "The lake" is never named, and Jesus crossed the lake several times (Gerasenes, Dalmanutha, Capernaum). The intended answer is Gennesaret (Matt 14:34, Mark 6:53), but the question alone does not pin down which crossing it means.

written:MAT-16-1:1.question: In Matthew 16, which two groups of religious leaders came to test Jesus by asking Him for a sign from heaven?
written:MAT-16-1:1.why: also right: A: Choice B matches the section exactly (verse 1). Choice A is also arguable from elsewhere: Matthew 12:38 says some scribes and Pharisees asked Jesus for a sign, and scribes are the teachers of the law.

written:MAT-17-22:2.question: After Jesus told them in Galilee that He would be killed and raised on the third day, how did the disciples react?
written:MAT-17-22:2.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: C: Matthew 17:22-23 says the disciples were 'deeply grieved.' Mark 9:30-34 also places an argument about who was greatest right after the Galilee prediction, so C is arguable from Mark, though it happened later on the road to Capernaum. D (Peter rebuking Jesus) is from a different occasion at Caesarea Philippi, so it doesn't fit.

written:MAT-18-6:1.question: In Matthew 18:6, what does Jesus say would be better for a person who causes one of the little ones who believe in Him to stumble?
written:MAT-18-6:1.answer: To have a large millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the sea

written:MAT-21-33:4.question: After Jesus told the parable of the wicked tenants, what did the chief priests and Pharisees say the owner would do to the tenants?
written:MAT-21-33:4.answer: Bring them to a wretched end and rent the vineyard to other tenants

written:MAT-22-23:2.question: In Matthew 22, when Jesus told the Sadducees that God is not the God of the dead but of the living, which statement of God did He quote?
written:MAT-22-23:2.answer: “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”

written:MAT-22-41:1.question: When Jesus asked the assembled Pharisees whose son the Christ is, how did they answer?
written:MAT-22-41:1.why: also right: B: Abraham's is not the Pharisees' answer, but Matthew 1:1 calls Jesus the son of Abraham, so it could fairly be argued for from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:MAT-24-26:1.question: When Jesus warned his disciples not to believe claims that the Christ was in the wilderness or in the inner rooms, what did he say the coming of the Son of Man would be like?
written:MAT-24-26:1.answer: Lightning that comes from the east and flashes to the west
written:MAT-24-26:1.why: also right: D: D is not the simile in verse 27, but Jesus does liken his coming to a thief in the night in Matthew 24:43-44 (and 1 Thess 5:2 says the Lord's day comes like a thief), so it could be argued as a coming-simile elsewhere in Scripture.

written:MAT-27-62:1.question: In Matthew 27, why did the chief priests and Pharisees ask Pilate to have Jesus' tomb secured until the third day?
written:MAT-27-62:1.answer: So His disciples could not steal Him away and claim He had risen

written:MRK-16-12:2.question: When the two disciples who had seen the risen Jesus in the country went back and reported it to the rest, how did the rest respond?
written:MRK-16-12:2.answer: They did not believe them either
written:MRK-16-12:2.why: not clear on its own: "In the country" points to Mark 16:12-13, where the others did not believe them (D). But the question doesn't name a Gospel, and Luke 24:33-35 (the Emmaus disciples returning to the Eleven) has the group affirming the risen Lord, which a reader could fairly match to C. Needs a named Gospel or passage.

written:LUK-16-19:3.question: In Jesus' account of the rich man and Lazarus, why did Abraham say the rich man in Hades could not receive help from Lazarus?
written:LUK-16-19:3.answer: A great chasm had been fixed between them that no one could cross

written:LUK-21-34:1.question: In Jesus' teaching in Luke 21 about the coming day, where did He spend each night during the days He taught at the temple?
written:LUK-21-34:1.why: also right: D: Luke 21:37 says He spent each night on the Mount of Olives. Elsewhere in that same final week, Matthew 21:17 and Mark 11:11 say He lodged in Bethany, and John 12:1 places the house of Lazarus there. Bethany lies on the Mount's eastern slope, so D could fairly be argued for, though the section's answer is C.

written:JHN-4-27:1.question: In John 4, when the disciples urged Jesus to eat something, what did Jesus say his food was?
written:JHN-4-27:1.answer: To do the will of Him who sent Him and finish His work

written:JHN-4-39:2.question: According to the Samaritans in John 4, what did they know Jesus truly is, after hearing Him for themselves?
written:JHN-4-39:2.why: also right: A, B, C: The section settles D as the Samaritans' statement. But the stem asks what they knew Jesus "truly is," and elsewhere Scripture also calls Jesus King of Israel (John 1:49; Matt 2:2), the prophet like Moses (Deut 18:15; Acts 3:22), and Son of David (Matt 1:1; 22:42). Those are true of Jesus, though the Samaritans did not say them here.

written:JHN-7-1:2.question: What did Jesus' brothers urge Him to do as the Feast of Tabernacles drew near?
written:JHN-7-1:2.answer: Leave Galilee and go to Judea to show Himself
written:JHN-7-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JHN-7-37:1.question: In John 7, on the last and greatest day of the feast, what did Jesus say streams of living water would flow from within the one who believes in Him?

written:JHN-8-12:2.question: When the Pharisees objected that Jesus was testifying about Himself, what reason did Jesus give for His testimony being valid?
written:JHN-8-12:2.answer: He knew where He came from and where He was going
written:JHN-8-12:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JHN-8-12:3.question: In John 8, who did Jesus say also testifies about Him, alongside Himself, in keeping with the Law's requirement of two witnesses?
written:JHN-8-12:3.why: also right: A, B, C: The section names only the Father as the second witness. But the other choices are arguably true elsewhere: the Holy Spirit testifies about Jesus (John 15:26) and descended on Him (Luke 3:22); John the Baptist bore witness to Him (John 1:34; 5:33); Moses wrote of Him (John 5:46). The question's framing (who Jesus said testifies alongside Himself in this passage) still points to D.

written:JHN-8-12:4.question: Where was Jesus teaching when He spoke to the Pharisees about His testimony, and why did no one seize Him?
written:JHN-8-12:4.answer: In the temple courts near the treasury; His hour had not yet come

written:JHN-8-12:6.question: In John 8, what did Jesus say the Jews would know when they had lifted up the Son of Man?
written:JHN-8-12:6.answer: That He is He and does nothing on His own
written:JHN-8-12:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JHN-8-48:3.question: In John 8, what did Jesus say Abraham did regarding His day?
written:JHN-8-48:3.answer: He rejoiced that he would see it, saw it, and was glad
written:JHN-8-48:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JHN-9-13:5.question: In John 9, what did the Pharisees do to the healed man after he said they were instructing them?
written:JHN-9-13:5.why: not clear on its own: The premise is garbled: in John 9:34 it is the Pharisees who say "would you teach us?" to the man, not the man who says they are instructing them. The question also does not say which exchange it means. The answer (they cast him out) is still B, but the wording should be fixed.

written:JHN-12-20:6.question: In John 12, what did Jesus say will happen to the prince of this world now that judgment is upon the world?
written:JHN-12-20:6.why: also right: C, D: The section says Jesus stated the prince of this world 'will be cast out' (A). Elsewhere, Revelation 20:2 binds Satan for a thousand years (D), and Revelation 20:9-10 has fire from heaven and Satan thrown into the lake of fire (C). Those are true of Satan elsewhere, but Jesus does not say them in John 12, so A is the answer the question asks for.

written:JHN-13-1:4.question: After washing the disciples’ feet, Jesus said that no servant is greater than whom?
written:JHN-13-1:4.why: also right: D: D, 'the one he serves,' is a near-paraphrase of 'his master' since a servant's master is the one he serves. The text says 'his master' (C), so C is the keyed answer.

written:JHN-14-27:1.question: In the Upper Room discourse, why did Jesus say the disciples ought to rejoice that he was going to the Father, if they loved him?
written:JHN-14-27:1.answer: Because the Father is greater than he
written:JHN-14-27:1.why: also right: C: Verse 28 gives the reason directly: 'because the Father is greater than I.' C is not Jesus's stated reason here, but John 16:7 says it is to the disciples' advantage that he go away so the Helper (the Spirit) can come, so C could fairly be argued from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JHN-15-18:1.question: In the Upper Room teaching in John 15, why did Jesus say the world would hate His disciples?
written:JHN-15-18:1.answer: Because they are not of the world, but He chose them out of it

written:JHN-16-1:2.question: In Jesus' warning to his disciples about persecution, why did he say people would do these things to them?
written:JHN-16-1:2.answer: They have not known the Father or Jesus
written:JHN-16-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JHN-17-6:1.question: In His prayer for His disciples in John 17, what does Jesus say is truth when He asks the Father to sanctify them?
written:JHN-17-6:1.why: also right: C, D: Jesus says "Your word is truth" (17:17). Other choices are also stated elsewhere in Scripture: "Your law is truth" (Psalm 119:142, BSB) and "the Spirit is the truth" (1 John 5:6, BSB). Neither is what Jesus says in this prayer, so B is the only correct answer to the question as asked.

written:ACT-5-12:1.question: In Acts 5, where did the believers gather with one accord while the apostles performed many signs and wonders?
written:ACT-5-12:1.why: also right: D: Acts 5:12 names Solomon's Colonnade. D is a broader location that also fits: Solomon's Colonnade stood on the east side of the temple's outer court, the Court of the Gentiles. The text does not name that court, so D is arguable but not the intended answer. B and C are other gatherings (Acts 12:12; Acts 1:13-14, 2:1) and do not fit this event.

written:ACT-5-12:2.question: In the early church in Jerusalem, why did people lay the sick on cots and mats in the streets as Peter passed by?
written:ACT-5-12:2.answer: So that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them

written:ACT-5-17:2.question: After the angel freed the apostles from the jail, what did he tell them to do?
written:ACT-5-17:2.answer: Stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life

written:ACT-5-33:1.question: In Acts 5, after the Sanhedrin yielded to Gamaliel and had the apostles flogged, how did the apostles feel as they left?
written:ACT-5-33:1.answer: They rejoiced that they were counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name

written:ACT-6-8:1.question: When men from the Synagogue of the Freedmen argued with Stephen in Jerusalem, why could they not defeat him?
written:ACT-6-8:1.answer: They could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke

written:ACT-10-17:2.question: When the Spirit told Peter to go downstairs and accompany the men sent by Cornelius, what reason did the Spirit give for going without hesitation?
written:ACT-10-17:2.answer: The Spirit had sent the men
written:ACT-10-17:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:ACT-10-24:1.question: When Cornelius met Peter at his house in Caesarea and fell at his feet to worship him, what did Peter say?
written:ACT-10-24:1.answer: “Stand up, I am only a man myself.”
written:ACT-10-24:1.why: a quotation not word for word in the BSB text

written:ACT-18-12:2.question: When the Jews accused Paul before Gallio in Corinth, how did Gallio respond to their complaint about their own law?
written:ACT-18-12:2.answer: He refused to judge it and drove them away
written:ACT-18-12:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ACT-22-22:1.question: In Jerusalem, when Paul said God would send him far away to the Gentiles, how did the crowd respond?
written:ACT-22-22:1.answer: They shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”

written:ACT-22-22:3.question: As the soldiers stretched Paul out to strap him down, what did Paul ask the centurion?
written:ACT-22-22:3.answer: Whether it was lawful to flog a Roman citizen without a trial
written:ACT-22-22:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ACT-23-23:2.question: In his letter to Governor Felix, what did Claudius Lysias say he found about the accusation against Paul?
written:ACT-23-23:2.answer: It involved questions about their own law, with no charge worthy of death or imprisonment

written:ACT-24-10:2.question: When Paul defended himself before Felix, what name did he give to the way of worship that his accusers called a sect?

written:ACT-24-10:3.question: According to Paul's defense before Felix, why did he return to Jerusalem after several years?
written:ACT-24-10:3.answer: To bring alms to his people and to present offerings
written:ACT-24-10:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ACT-25-13:4.question: After Festus told King Agrippa about Paul's case, what did Agrippa say he would like to do?
written:ACT-25-13:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:ACT-25-23:3.question: Why did Festus bring Paul before King Agrippa, so that he could have something to write to the Emperor?
written:ACT-25-23:3.answer: It seemed unreasonable to send a prisoner without specifying the charges
written:ACT-25-23:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ACT-26-24:3.question: After Paul asked whether he believed the prophets, what did King Agrippa say to Paul?
written:ACT-26-24:3.answer: "Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?"

written:ROM-9-30:1.question: In Romans 9, why did Israel not attain the righteousness they pursued?
written:ROM-9-30:1.answer: Their pursuit was not by faith, but as if by works
written:ROM-9-30:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ROM-11-11:2.question: In Paul's picture of the olive tree in Romans 11, what does the Gentile believer represent?
written:ROM-11-11:2.answer: A wild olive shoot grafted in among the other branches
written:ROM-11-11:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ROM-15-14:2.question: In Romans 15, what does Paul say he has often been hindered from doing, because he aspired to preach where Christ was not known?
written:ROM-15-14:2.answer: Coming to the believers in Rome
written:ROM-15-14:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:ROM-16-25:1.question: In the closing doxology of Romans, what is God able to do for the believers, according to "my gospel" and the proclamation of Jesus Christ?
written:ROM-16-25:1.why: also right: A: "Deliver" is not in this doxology, but Scripture elsewhere says God is able to deliver (Daniel 3:17; 2 Corinthians 1:10), so it could be argued for. The text itself names strengthening, so B is the answer.

written:1CO-6-1:1.question: In 1 Corinthians 6, Paul asks whether the saints will judge something, and says that if so they are competent to judge trivial cases. What will the saints judge?
written:1CO-6-1:1.why: also right: A: 6:2 says the saints will judge the world. Elsewhere, Matthew 19:28 has the twelve apostles (saints) judging the twelve tribes of Israel, so A is also true somewhere in Scripture, though the section does not say it.

written:1CO-6-1:2.question: In 1 Corinthians 6, when believers in Corinth took their disputes to court, before whom was one brother bringing a lawsuit against another?
written:1CO-6-1:2.why: also right: D: 6:1 and 6:6 say the believers went before 'the unrighteous' and 'unbelievers'. A Roman governor is an unbeliever and Corinth was under Roman administration (cf. Acts 18:12, Gallio), so D could be argued, but the section never names a governor or Roman court.

written:1CO-7-25:3.question: In 1 Corinthians 7, what reason does Paul give for telling believers to hold loosely to the things of this world?
written:1CO-7-25:3.answer: This world in its present form is passing away
written:1CO-7-25:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CO-7-25:5.question: In 1 Corinthians 7, when a wife's husband dies, whom may she marry?
written:1CO-7-25:5.answer: Anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord
written:1CO-7-25:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CO-11-1:1.question: In 1 Corinthians 11, whom does Paul tell the Corinthians to imitate, just as he imitates Christ?
written:1CO-11-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CO-11-1:3.question: In 1 Corinthians 11, what does Paul say a man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors?

written:1CO-16-10:1.question: In 1 Corinthians 16, why does Paul tell the Corinthians to make sure Timothy has nothing to fear while he is with them?
written:1CO-16-10:1.answer: He is doing the work of the Lord, just as Paul is
written:1CO-16-10:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CO-16-10:2.question: In 1 Corinthians 16, what did Paul say about Apollos going to Corinth with the brothers?
written:1CO-16-10:2.answer: He was not at all inclined to go now, but will go when he has opportunity

written:2CO-1-3:2.question: According to Paul in 2 Corinthians 1:4, why does God comfort believers in all their troubles?
written:2CO-1-3:2.answer: So they can comfort others in any trouble with the comfort they received

written:2CO-1-3:3.question: In 2 Corinthians 1:8-9, why does Paul say he and Timothy felt they were under the sentence of death in Asia?
written:2CO-1-3:3.answer: So they would not trust in themselves, but in God, who raises the dead

written:2CO-4-1:2.question: In 2 Corinthians 4, Paul says he does not proclaim himself. Whom does he proclaim instead?
written:2CO-4-1:2.why: also right: B: The section says Paul proclaims 'Jesus Christ as Lord' (C). Option B is not stated here, but Scripture elsewhere presents Christ as the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24; Col 2:3) and as Teacher (Matt 23:10), so it could be argued for.

written:2CO-8-16:3.question: Why does Paul say he is taking great care in how he administers the generous gift?
written:2CO-8-16:3.answer: To do what is right in the eyes of the Lord and of men

written:2CO-10-1:5.question: In 2 Corinthians 10, why does Paul say he can claim a field of influence reaching to Corinth?
written:2CO-10-1:5.answer: He and his companions were the first to reach them with the gospel of Christ

written:2CO-12-11:2.question: In what way does Paul say the Corinthians were inferior to the other churches?
written:2CO-12-11:2.answer: Only that Paul was not a burden to them
written:2CO-12-11:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CO-12-11:3.question: When Paul told the Corinthians he was ready to visit them a third time, what reason did he give for not being a burden to them?
written:2CO-12-11:3.answer: He was not seeking their possessions, but them
written:2CO-12-11:3.why: also right: C: Option C is not the reason given in this section, but 2 Cor 11:9 says the brothers from Macedonia supplied Paul's needs so he would not burden the Corinthians, so it is a fair alternative reason from elsewhere in Scripture. Option A (tentmaking) is real, but 'in every city' overstates Acts 18:3, and it is not cited as the reason here.

written:2CO-12-11:4.question: Which man did Paul say he urged to visit the Corinthians, and ask whether he had exploited them?
written:2CO-12-11:4.why: also right: B: The section names Titus as the man Paul urged to visit and asked about exploitation. Option B is a partial match only: 1 Cor 16:12 says Paul urged Apollos to visit Corinth, but nothing elsewhere links Apollos to the exploitation question.

written:2CO-13-1:1.question: In 2 Corinthians 13:1, what does Paul say must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses?
written:2CO-13-1:1.why: also right: D: Verse 13:1 says "Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses." Choice D is a narrower case of the same rule, and 1 Timothy 5:19 applies the two-or-three-witness principle to accusations against an elder, so it could fairly be argued for.

written:2CO-13-11:1.question: In Paul's closing words to the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 13:11, what does he say "the God of" what "will be with you"?
written:2CO-13-11:1.answer: The God of love and peace
written:2CO-13-11:1.why: also right: A: A is not the wording of this verse, but 2 Corinthians 1:3 calls God "the Father of mercies" and "the God of all comfort," so A is loosely true elsewhere in Scripture. The verse itself settles B verbatim.

written:GAL-1-6:2.question: In Galatians 1:6, what does Paul say he is amazed the Galatians are doing?
written:GAL-1-6:2.answer: Quickly deserting the One who called them and turning to a different gospel

written:GAL-4-8:2.question: In Galatians 4:14, how does Paul say the Galatians welcomed him despite his illness being a trial to them?
written:GAL-4-8:2.answer: As if he were an angel of God, as if Christ Jesus Himself

written:GAL-4-8:5.question: In Galatians 4:19, what does Paul say he is in the pains of childbirth for, until it is formed in the Galatians?
written:GAL-4-8:5.answer: Until Christ is formed in them
written:GAL-4-8:5.why: not clear on its own: The question says "until it is formed in the Galatians" but never names what "it" is, so the pronoun has no antecedent. Reword to "until Christ is formed in the Galatians." The answer is still A (Gal. 4:19).

written:GAL-6-11:2.question: In Galatians 6:15, Paul says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What does he say counts?
written:GAL-6-11:2.why: also right: A: The section says "What counts is a new creation," so C is right. But 1 Corinthians 7:19 uses almost the same wording and says "What counts is keeping the commandments of God," so A (obedience to the law) could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:EPH-3-1:1.question: In Ephesians 3, what does Paul say the mystery of Christ is, as it concerns the Gentiles?
written:EPH-3-1:1.answer: Through the gospel the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the body, and partakers of the promise

written:1TI-5-17:1.question: In 1 Timothy 5, what does Paul say elders who lead effectively are worthy of?
written:1TI-5-17:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: 1 Timothy 5:17 says elders who rule well are worthy of "double honour" (timē). Double wages (D) is arguable because the context in v.18 cites pay for workers, so the honor may include material support, but the text says honor, not wages.

written:1TI-6-11:1.question: In 1 Timothy 6, before whom did Christ Jesus make the good confession in His testimony?
written:1TI-6-11:1.why: also right: A: The section names Pilate directly (6:13), so B is settled by the text. A is also arguable from the Gospels: Jesus made a confession before the high priest Caiaphas (Mark 14:61-62; Matthew 26:63-64), though 1 Timothy 6:13 refers only to Pilate.

written:2TI-2-1:1.question: In 2 Timothy 2:2, whom does Paul tell Timothy to entrust the things he heard from Paul among many witnesses?
written:2TI-2-1:1.answer: Faithful men who will be qualified to teach others
written:2TI-2-1:1.why: also right: C: Verse 2 names faithful men qualified to teach. Choice C is arguable as a narrower form: elders are faithful men qualified to teach (1 Tim 3:2; Titus 1:5-9), though Paul does not use the word 'elders' in this verse.

written:2TI-3-1:3.question: In 2 Timothy 3, Paul says that the men who oppose the truth are like which two men who opposed Moses?
written:2TI-3-1:3.why: also right: C: Section names Jannes and Jambres explicitly. Korah and Dathan also opposed Moses (Numbers 16), so C is true elsewhere in Scripture, but the question's wording points to the names given in this passage.

written:HEB-3-12:1.question: In Hebrews 3, what reason does the writer give for why the generation Moses led out of Egypt was unable to enter God's rest?
written:HEB-3-12:1.why: also right: A, D: Hebrews 3:19 names unbelief as the writer's stated reason.
