A (golden calf) and D (fear of giants) are sins of that same generation that other passages tie to their exclusion (1 Cor 10:5-10 on idolatry; Num 14 on fear and unbelief), so a reader could argue for them, but the section itself names only unbelief.

written:HEB-6-1:2.question: In Hebrews 6:7-8, what is the land that produces thorns and thistles said to be?
written:HEB-6-1:2.answer: Worthless, with its curse imminent and in the end burned
written:HEB-6-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1PE-4-12:2.question: In 1 Peter 4:16, how should a believer respond if he suffers as a Christian?
written:1PE-4-12:2.answer: Not be ashamed, but glorify God that he bears that name
written:1PE-4-12:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1JN-4-1:2.question: In 1 John 4:4, why does John tell believers they have overcome the false prophets?
written:1JN-4-1:2.answer: Greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world

written:REV-3-7:1.question: In Christ's message to the church in Philadelphia, what does He say He holds?
written:REV-3-7:1.why: also right: C, D: Also right elsewhere: Rev 2:1 has Christ holding the seven stars in His right hand (C), and Rev 1:18 has Him holding the keys of Death and Hades (D). The Philadelphia section itself names only the key of David.

written:REV-7-1:1.question: In Revelation 7, what were the four angels at the four corners of the earth doing with the four winds?
written:REV-7-1:1.answer: Holding them back so no wind would blow on land, sea, or trees

written:REV-8-6:4.question: In Revelation 8, what did John hear an eagle flying overhead cry out after the fourth trumpet?
written:REV-8-6:4.answer: “Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth”
written:REV-8-6:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:REV-9-1:4.question: In Revelation 9, who was the king ruling over the locusts from the Abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon?
written:REV-9-1:4.why: also right: C: Choice C is not the stated answer, but many commentators identify the fallen star (given the key to the pit) with the angel of the Abyss, so it could be argued; the section itself names the king as 'the angel of the Abyss' and does not explicitly equate him with the star.

written:REV-11-7:2.question: In Revelation 11, how long will the peoples, tribes, tongues and nations view the bodies of the two witnesses without letting them be laid in a tomb?
written:REV-11-7:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:REV-16-1:4.question: When the sixth angel poured out his bowl in Revelation 16, what happened to the great river Euphrates?
written:REV-16-1:4.answer: Its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings of the East

written:REV-16-17:2.question: When the seventh bowl of wrath was poured out, how did the great city of Revelation 16 change?
written:REV-16-17:2.answer: It was split into three parts
written:REV-16-17:2.why: also right: A, D: Section text says the city was split into three parts, so B is out. A is arguable only from Rev 18:21, where Babylon is cast down like a millstone into the sea, which is imagery of being cast down rather than a change in Rev 16. D is arguable from Rev 18:8-19, where Babylon is burned with fire and laid waste in one hour, but that is not stated in Rev 16 and is not the seventh bowl's described effect.

written:REV-17-6:3.question: In Revelation 17, what does the angel say the ten horns of the beast are?
written:REV-17-6:3.answer: Ten kings who will receive one hour of authority along with the beast

written:REV-18-9:4.question: Among the cargo the merchants of the earth sold to Babylon, which pair is listed at the very end of the cargo list in Revelation 18?
written:REV-18-9:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:REV-19-17:3.question: In Revelation 19, what did the kings of the earth and their armies assemble to do?
written:REV-19-17:3.answer: Wage war against the One seated on the horse and His army
written:REV-19-17:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:REV-21-9:3.question: In John's vision, who will be allowed to enter the New Jerusalem?
written:REV-21-9:3.answer: Only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life

written:EXO-29-1:2.question: In the consecration of Aaron and his sons, where was Moses to present them and wash them with water?
written:EXO-29-1:2.answer: At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
written:EXO-29-1:2.why: Exodus 29:4 says at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, but the bronze altar stood so near that entrance it could fairly be chosen, so that wrong choice was replaced.

written:LEV-1-1:1.question: In Leviticus 1, what kind of animal was a man to present if his burnt offering came from the herd?
written:LEV-1-1:1.why: The wrong choice about an unblemished lamb under one year was too close to the right answer and added a detail not in Leviticus 1, so it was replaced with the birds named for a burnt offering of birds (Lev 1:14).

written:LEV-26-1:5.question: In Leviticus 26, what does God promise to make among the obedient Israelites?
written:LEV-26-1:5.why: The wrong choice "His resting place of peace" meant almost the same as "dwelling place", so it was replaced with "His storehouse of grain", which is clearly wrong by Leviticus 26:11.

written:NUM-13-25:1.question: After the spies returned to Kadesh, which of them quieted the people before Moses and said, "We must go up and take possession of the land"?
written:NUM-13-25:1.why: cited verses missing or outside the section

written:JOS-2-8:1.question: When Rahab spoke to the two Israelite spies on her roof, what did she say the LORD had given to the Israelites?
written:JOS-2-8:1.why: The choice "The hill country" is part of the land God gave, so it could also be picked; it was replaced with "The wealth of Egypt", which Rahab never said.

written:1SA-15-10:2.question: According to the report Samuel received, what did Saul set up for himself at Carmel before going down to Gilgal?
written:1SA-15-10:2.why: One wrong choice, a stone pillar of twelve stones, is too much like a monument, so it was replaced with "A walled city", which is clearly wrong by 1 Samuel 15:12.

written:2SA-12-1:1.question: In Nathan's parable to David, what was the only thing the poor man had?
written:2SA-12-1:1.answer: One small ewe lamb that he had bought
written:2SA-12-1:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-18-19:4.question: While David waited for news of the battle, where was he sitting?
written:2SA-18-19:4.why: not clear on its own: The answer is A (2 Samuel 18:24, David sitting between the two gates at Mahanaim while awaiting news of Absalom's battle), but the question never names the battle or its context, so a quiz-taker cannot tell which battle is meant. Adding 'Absalom's rebellion' or 'the battle against Absalom' would fix it.

written:1CH-12-1:8.question: Who was the chief of the Thirty, upon whom the Spirit came, declaring "We are with you, O son of Jesse!"?
written:1CH-12-1:8.why: also right: D: Verse 18 names Amasai as chief of the Thirty and says the Spirit came on him, so A is settled by this section. Jashobeam (D) is named only as a Korahite here, but 1 Chronicles 11:11 links him to the leadership of the Thirty/Three, and some renderings call him chief of the Thirty, so D is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:JOB-14-1:2.question: In Job 14, to what does Job compare a man who comes forth and then withers away, besides a fleeting shadow?
written:JOB-14-1:2.why: The wrong choice "A tree" is in the same chapter (Job 14:7-9), where it is a contrast to man, so it could confuse readers; it was replaced with "A burning lamp", which is not in Job 14.

written:JOB-22-1:2.question: In Job 22, what did Eliphaz accuse Job of refusing to give the weary?
written:JOB-22-1:2.why: Job 22:7 says Job gave no water to the weary, but "Clothing" is also a charge in the same speech (22:6, about the naked), so it was replaced with "Gold", which is clearly wrong.

written:JOB-29-1:5.question: In Job 29, Job says he served as eyes to the blind. What does he say he was to the lame?
written:JOB-29-1:5.why: The wrong choice "A father" is something Job says of himself in the very next verse (to the needy), so I replaced it with "Arms", which is clearly wrong.

written:JOB-41-1:2.question: In Job 41:11, God says, "Who has given to Me that I should ___ him? Everything under heaven is Mine." What word completes the sentence?
written:JOB-41-1:2.why: a quotation not word for word in the BSB text

written:PSA-83-1:3.question: In Psalm 83, what did the Midianite leaders Zebah and Zalmunna say about the pastures of God?
written:PSA-83-1:3.answer: “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
written:PSA-83-1:3.why: not clear on its own: The question attributes the words to Zebah and Zalmunna, but Psalm 83:12 gives them to unnamed enemies ("who said"); the two Midianite kings are named only in verse 11, as foes whose fate is requested. The answer B matches the verse's wording in translations that render it "pastures" (NASB); ESV and KJV say "habitations". The premise should be corrected, e.g., "the enemies who plotted against Israel".

written:PSA-85-1:2.question: In Psalm 85, the psalmist says that "righteousness and peace" have done what to each other?
written:PSA-85-1:2.why: The wrong choice "They have joined together" means nearly the same as "kissed" (and describes a different pair in the same verse), so it was replaced with "They have sprouted from the earth," which Psalm 85:11 says of faithfulness.

written:PSA-98-1:3.question: In Psalm 98, which instruments are named for praising the LORD, the King, in the call to shout for joy?
written:PSA-98-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PRO-27-1:5.question: Proverbs 27:2 says, "Let another praise you, and not your own mouth." Whom does the verse then name as the one to praise you, and not your own lips?

written:SNG-4-1:2.question: In Song of Songs 4:4, the beloved's neck is compared to the tower of which king?
written:SNG-4-1:2.why: The answer (David) is right, but the question called the woman "the beloved" when in this book the man is "my beloved" and she is "my darling" and "my bride", so the question now says "the bride's neck".

written:ISA-13-1:1.question: Which prophet received the burden against Babylon that speaks of the Medes being stirred up against it?
written:ISA-13-1:1.why: also right: A: Isaiah 13:1 says the burden against Babylon was received by Isaiah son of Amoz, and 13:17 names the Medes. Jeremiah son of Hilkiah also prophesied against Babylon and mentioned the Medes (Jeremiah 51:11, 28), so a loose reading could credit him, but he did not receive this burden.

written:ISA-66-15:3.question: According to Isaiah 66:19, what will the survivors sent to the distant nations that have not heard of His fame do there?
written:ISA-66-15:3.answer: They will proclaim the LORD's glory among the nations
written:ISA-66-15:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-25-34:1.question: In Jeremiah 25, the LORD says the shepherds and leaders of the flock will fall and be shattered like what?
written:JER-25-34:1.why: The choice "dung on the ground" is what Jeremiah 25:33 says of the slain, so it could also seem right; it was replaced with "burned stubble."

written:EZK-48-8:2.question: In Ezekiel 48:11, why was the holy portion set apart for the priests, the descendants of Zadok?
written:EZK-48-8:2.answer: They kept the LORD's charge and did not go astray as the Levites did

written:1TH-3-1:1.question: In 1 Thessalonians 3:4, what did Paul say he and his companions kept warning the Thessalonians about when they were with them?
written:1TH-3-1:1.answer: That Paul and his companions would suffer persecution
written:1TH-3-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:REV-17-1:2.question: In John's vision of the woman sitting on a scarlet beast, what name was written on her forehead?
written:REV-17-1:2.answer: BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH
written:REV-17-1:2.why: the fix's right choice differs from its answer

written:EXO-39-1:1.question: In Exodus 39, who made the ephod for Aaron's holy garments?
written:EXO-39-1:1.why: not clear on its own: Exodus 39 never names the maker; it says only "they" (the skilled craftsmen). Bezalel and Oholiab both led that work (Exod 36:1-2), so the question has no single unambiguous answer.

written:EXO-39-8:1.question: In Exodus 39, which three gemstones made up the first row on the breastpiece?
written:EXO-39-8:1.answer: A ruby, a topaz, and an emerald
written:EXO-39-8:1.why: not clear on its own: No choice matches the usual rendering exactly: Exodus 39:10 lists carnelian, topaz, emerald (NIV) or sardius, topaz, carbuncle (KJV). A is the nearest match, but ruby is not carnelian, so the answer depends on translation.

written:LEV-5-1:1.question: In Leviticus 5, what must a person do after realizing he has incurred guilt in one of these ways, before bringing his offering?
written:LEV-5-1:1.answer: Confess the sin he has committed
written:LEV-5-1:1.why: not clear on its own: "These ways" refers to offenses the question never names, so the quiz-taker cannot tell which situation is meant. The answer is D (Lev 5:5, confess the sin), but the question needs to name the offenses (e.g., touching something unclean or an oath).

written:LEV-5-1:5.question: In Leviticus 5, what was a person NOT to put on the fine flour he brought as a sin offering?
written:LEV-5-1:5.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: Lev 5:11 bars only oil and frankincense. Leaven is barred from grain offerings in Lev 2:11, which a careful reader could apply here, so D is arguable outside Lev 5. The question's scope is Leviticus 5, so B is the intended answer.

written:LEV-6-14:5.question: How much fine flour were Aaron and his sons to present as a regular grain offering on the day Aaron was anointed?
written:LEV-6-14:5.why: also right: B: Lev 6:20 says a tenth of an ephah. An omer is a tenth of an ephah (Exodus 16:36), so 'an omer of fine flour' is the same amount, stated in another unit.

written:LEV-8-1:2.question: In the consecration of Aaron as priest, what did Moses place in the breastpiece?
written:LEV-8-1:2.why: also right: B: Leviticus 8:8 says Moses placed the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece. Exodus 28:17-21 and 39:10-14 also set twelve stones of Israel in the breastpiece, so B is true of the breastpiece elsewhere in Scripture, though Moses does not place them in this passage.

written:LEV-26-14:7.question: In Leviticus 26, why will the land enjoy its Sabbaths while Israel is in the land of their enemies?
written:LEV-26-14:7.answer: The land lies desolate and rests as it did not during Israel's Sabbaths

written:NUM-4-1:4.question: In Numbers 4, what color of cloth was spread over the table of the Presence before it was covered with fine leather?
written:NUM-4-1:4.why: picked B, not the writer's A: 4:7 puts a blue cloth directly over the table, but 4:8 then spreads a scarlet cloth over the table's items before the fine leather goes on, so scarlet is also spread over the table before the leather. The blue cloth is the one placed on the table itself, so B is the intended answer.

written:NUM-4-1:8.question: In Numbers 4, what were the Kohathites forbidden to do, even for a moment, on penalty of death?
written:NUM-4-1:8.answer: Go in and look at the holy objects
written:NUM-4-1:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-4-21:3.question: In Numbers 4, who was in charge of directing the work of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting?
written:NUM-4-21:3.answer: Ithamar son of Aaron the priest
written:NUM-4-21:3.why: also right: D: 4:28 names Ithamar explicitly. But 4:27 says the Gershonites' work is under the direction of Aaron and his sons, and Eleazar is one of those sons, so D is arguably also true.

written:NUM-4-29:2.question: In Numbers 4, under whose direction did the Merarite clans carry out their service at the Tent of Meeting?
written:NUM-4-29:2.answer: Ithamar son of Aaron the priest
written:NUM-4-29:2.why: also right: D: The section names Ithamar explicitly. Eleazar is also a fair answer from elsewhere: Numbers 3:32 makes him chief over the leaders of the Levites, which would include the Merarite clans, and 4:16 gives him oversight of the tabernacle. The section itself assigns the Merarites to Ithamar, so A is the intended answer.

written:NUM-9-15:4.question: In Numbers 9, how long did the Israelites stay camped when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days?
written:NUM-9-15:4.answer: As long as the cloud remained over it
written:NUM-9-15:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-20-1:2.question: At Kadesh, when the people had no water and quarreled with Moses and Aaron, where did Moses and Aaron go?
written:NUM-20-1:2.answer: To the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, where they fell facedown
written:NUM-20-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-26-1:2.question: Where were Moses and Eleazar when they gave the instruction for the second census of Israel in Numbers 26?
written:NUM-26-1:2.answer: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho
written:NUM-26-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NUM-36-1:2.question: In Numbers 36, what did the family heads of the clan of Gilead say would happen to the inheritance of Zelophehad's daughters when the Jubilee came, if they married into another tribe?
written:NUM-36-1:2.answer: It would still be added to the tribe they married into
written:NUM-36-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-1-19:3.question: According to Moses in Deuteronomy 1, what did the people ask to do before going up to take the land?
written:DEU-1-19:3.answer: Send men ahead to search out the land
written:DEU-1-19:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-1-26:2.question: In Deuteronomy 1, how did Moses say the LORD carried Israel in the wilderness?
written:DEU-1-26:2.answer: As a man carries his son
written:DEU-1-26:2.why: also right: B: Verse 31 states 'as a man carries his son,' so D is the answer. B is not the section's simile, but Deuteronomy 32:11 (Moses' song) pictures God bearing Israel on his wings like an eagle in a desert land, so it is a fair alternative elsewhere in Deuteronomy.

written:DEU-1-41:1.question: In Moses' account in Deuteronomy 1, who came out of the hill country and chased the Israelites after they went up to fight against the LORD's command?
written:DEU-1-41:1.answer: The Amorites who lived in the hills
written:DEU-1-41:1.why: also right: D: The section names the Amorites who lived in the hills. Numbers 14:45 (the parallel account) says the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in the hill country came down and beat them as far as Hormah, and Numbers 14:25 places the Amalekites and Canaanites in the valley, so D could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture. The question is anchored to Deuteronomy 1, so B is the answer.

written:DEU-2-24:1.question: In Deuteronomy 2, what did the LORD say He would begin to put upon all the nations under heaven because of Israel?
written:DEU-2-24:1.answer: The dread and fear of Israel
written:DEU-2-24:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-2-24:4.question: According to Moses, why did Sihon king of Heshbon refuse to let Israel pass through his land?
written:DEU-2-24:4.answer: The LORD had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate
written:DEU-2-24:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-3-12:4.question: What did Moses command the men of valor of the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh to do before they could settle east of the Jordan?
written:DEU-3-12:4.answer: Cross over armed for battle ahead of their brothers, the Israelites
written:DEU-3-12:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-3-23:3.question: According to Moses in Deuteronomy 3, why was the LORD angry with him and unwilling to listen to his plea?
written:DEU-3-23:3.answer: On account of the people of Israel
written:DEU-3-23:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-5-5:4.question: In Deuteronomy 5, how did the LORD bring Israel out of the land of Egypt, according to the Sabbath command?
written:DEU-5-5:4.answer: With a mighty hand and an outstretched arm
written:DEU-5-5:4.why: also right: B: B (strong east wind, parted sea) is true of the Exodus elsewhere (Exodus 14:21), but this section's Sabbath command gives A in its own wording.

written:DEU-5-22:4.question: In Deuteronomy 5, why did the LORD tell Moses to stand with Him while the people went back to their tents?
written:DEU-5-22:4.answer: So He could speak all the commandments, statutes and ordinances for Moses to teach

written:DEU-7-12:3.question: In Deuteronomy 7, what does the LORD promise to do with the terrible diseases Israel knew in Egypt?
written:DEU-7-12:3.answer: Inflict them on all who hate Israel
written:DEU-7-12:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-7-12:6.question: In Deuteronomy 7, why should Israel not be terrified of the nations in Canaan?
written:DEU-7-12:6.answer: The LORD their God, who is among them, is a great and awesome God

written:DEU-9-7:7.question: What did Moses do with the golden calf after he burned it in the fire?
written:DEU-9-7:7.answer: He ground it to fine powder and cast it into the mountain stream

written:DEU-9-7:8.question: In Moses' prayer, why did he say the Egyptians might claim the LORD had brought Israel out into the wilderness?
written:DEU-9-7:8.answer: To kill them, because He was not able to bring them into the land

written:DEU-11-1:3.question: In Deuteronomy 11, what did the LORD do to the Egyptian army, horses and chariots as they pursued Israel?
written:DEU-11-1:3.answer: He made the waters of the Red Sea engulf them
written:DEU-11-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-14-1:1.question: In Deuteronomy 14, what two mourning practices for the dead does Moses forbid the Israelites because they are sons of the LORD?
written:DEU-14-1:1.answer: Cutting themselves and shaving their foreheads
written:DEU-14-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-14-1:4.question: In Deuteronomy 14, what may the Israelites do with a carcass, which they are not to eat themselves?
written:DEU-14-1:4.answer: Give it to the foreigner within their gates, or sell it to a foreigner

written:DEU-15-12:3.question: In Deuteronomy 15, why should a master not regard it as a hardship to set his Hebrew servant free?
written:DEU-15-12:3.answer: His service was worth twice a hired hand's wages
written:DEU-15-12:3.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: D: Deut 15:18 (Hebrew 'mishneh sekhar', KJV/NIV/NASB) says the servant's six years were worth double a hired hand's wages. ESV says 'half the wages of a hired servant,' which describes the master's cost and could lead a quiz-taker to D; D's 'worth only half' inverts the intended sense, so C is the answer.

written:DEU-15-19:2.question: In Deuteronomy 15, what kind of firstborn animal were the Israelites not to sacrifice to the LORD their God?
written:DEU-15-19:2.answer: One that was lame, blind, or seriously flawed
written:DEU-15-19:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-16-13:3.question: According to Deuteronomy 16, how was each man to appear before the LORD at the feasts, rather than empty-handed?
written:DEU-16-13:3.answer: With a gift as he was able, according to the LORD's blessing

written:DEU-23-9:1.question: In Deuteronomy 23, why must Israel's camp be kept holy when they go out against their enemies?
written:DEU-23-9:1.answer: The LORD walks throughout the camp to protect them and deliver their enemies

written:DEU-32-1:1.question: In the Song of Moses, how does Moses describe God when he says "His work is perfect; all His ways are just"?
written:DEU-32-1:1.why: also right: A, D: The verse itself says 'He is the Rock,' so C is settled by the section. Elsewhere Scripture also calls God a fortress and a shield (Psalm 18:2 'my rock, my fortress... my shield'), so A and D are true of God in other passages, though Moses does not use those titles here.

written:DEU-32-1:2.question: In the Song of Moses, what does God say He did to Jacob, His people, in the desert, comparing Himself to an eagle that stirs up its nest?
written:DEU-32-1:2.answer: He spread His wings to catch them and carried them on His pinions

written:JOS-24-14:2.question: In Joshua 24, what did Joshua say the LORD would do if the people forsook Him and served foreign gods?
written:JOS-24-14:2.answer: Bring disaster on them and consume them
written:JOS-24-14:2.why: also right: B: Joshua 24:20 says disaster and consumption. B is not in Joshua 24, but Joshua warns in 23:13-16 that they will perish from the good land, and Deuteronomy 28:63-64 speaks of uprooting and scattering, so it could fairly be argued.

written:JDG-2-6:1.question: In Judges 2, the Israelites served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of which other group of leaders?
written:JDG-2-6:1.answer: The elders who outlived him and had seen the LORD's great works

written:2SA-1-1:3.question: What did the Amalekite say he took from Saul and brought to David?
written:2SA-1-1:3.answer: The crown from his head and the band from his arm
written:2SA-1-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2SA-1-1:6.question: What question did David ask the Amalekite before ordering him to be executed?
written:2SA-1-1:6.answer: Why he was not afraid to lift his hand to destroy the LORD's anointed

written:2KI-1-1:2.question: What did the LORD say through Elijah would happen to King Ahaziah after he fell and was injured?
written:2KI-1-1:2.answer: He would not get up from his bed but would surely die
written:2KI-1-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2KI-1-1:6.question: What did Elijah say would happen when the first captain told him, "Man of God, the king declares, 'Come down!'"?
written:2KI-1-1:6.answer: Fire would come down from heaven and consume the captain and his fifty men

written:2KI-1-1:7.question: How many captains did King Ahaziah send to Elijah, each with fifty men, before Elijah went down to the king?
written:2KI-1-1:7.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2KI-1-1:8.question: What did the third captain do when he came up to Elijah?
written:2KI-1-1:8.answer: He fell on his knees and begged that the lives of his men be precious

written:2KI-23-4:2.question: In 2 Kings 23, what did Josiah do with the Asherah pole he brought out of the house of the LORD?
written:2KI-23-4:2.answer: Burned it, ground it to powder, and threw the dust on common graves

written:2KI-23-4:8.question: When Josiah saw a monument at Bethel and asked about it, whose tomb did the men of the city say it was?
written:2KI-23-4:8.answer: The man of God who came from Judah
written:2KI-23-4:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-1-1:1.question: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 1, which son of Canaan is named as his firstborn?
written:1CH-1-1:1.why: The answer Sidon is right, but two wrong choices ("Amor" and "Jebus") are names the BSB does not give, so they were replaced with real names from the same genealogy (Ham's other sons).

written:1CH-1-1:4.question: According to 1 Chronicles 1, how many sons did Noah's son Japheth have?
written:1CH-1-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CH-1-38:2.question: In 1 Chronicles 1, how many sons of Seir are named, from Lotan through Dishan?
written:1CH-1-38:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CH-11-1:2.question: When all Israel came to David at Hebron, what did the LORD his God say to David about his role over Israel?
written:1CH-11-1:2.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: A: 1 Chronicles 11:2 has the LORD saying 'You shall shepherd My people Israel.' Choice A echoes 2 Samuel 3:18, where the LORD's promise to save Israel from the Philistines by David's hand is relayed at Hebron before the elders come to him, so a careful reader could argue for it, though it is not what was said when all Israel came.

written:1CH-11-10:1.question: In the list of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11, who was chief of the officers?
written:1CH-11-10:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: A: 1 Chr 11:11 names Jashobeam son of Hachmoni as chief of the officers (the Thirty). But 11:20 calls Abishai the brother of Joab chief of the Thirty, so a careful reader could argue for A.

written:1CH-11-10:2.question: When three of the thirty chief men went down to David while the Philistines were encamped in the Valley of Rephaim, where did they meet him?
written:1CH-11-10:2.answer: At the rock by the cave of Adullam
written:1CH-11-10:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-11-10:7.question: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was most honored among the Thirty. Over what did David appoint him?
written:1CH-11-10:7.why: also right: C: The section says David appointed Benaiah over his guard. Elsewhere Benaiah commanded the army (1 Chr 27:5-6 as commander of a monthly division; 1 Kings 2:35 and 4:4 as commander of the army), so 'over the army of Israel' is true of him in Scripture, though this section does not say David appointed him over it.

written:1CH-13-1:1.question: In 1 Chronicles 13, why did David say the ark of God should be brought back?
written:1CH-13-1:1.answer: Because they did not inquire of God in the days of Saul
written:1CH-13-1:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-14-8:2.question: In David's second battle against the Philistines in the valley, what was the signal for him to move out to battle?
written:1CH-14-8:2.answer: The sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees
written:1CH-14-8:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-14-8:4.question: After David's victories over the Philistines, what did the LORD cause all nations to do?
written:1CH-14-8:4.why: also right: D: Verse 17 says the LORD caused all nations to fear 'him', most naturally David (the nearest antecedent after 'David's fame'), though the pronoun is grammatically open. Elsewhere (2 Sam 8:2, 6, 10) nations bring tribute to David after his victories, so D is arguable from Scripture beyond this section, though this section only states fear.

written:1CH-15-25:1.question: When David and the elders of Israel went to bring the ark of the covenant up to Jerusalem, whose house did they bring it from?
written:1CH-15-25:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: The wording matches 1 Chronicles 15:25 ("David and the elders of Israel... went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom"). Choice B is a weaker alternative: in 1 Chronicles 13:7 the ark is carried out of Abinadab's house on the first, failed attempt.

written:1CH-17-1:5.question: God promised to plant Israel in a place of their own, to be disturbed no more. Who would no longer oppress them?
written:1CH-17-1:5.why: also right: A: The text names 'the sons of wickedness' as the oppressors (17:9-10), so D is the section's answer. A is arguable only from elsewhere in Scripture: the Philistines and Amalekites oppressed Israel in the judges period, which 17:10 refers back to. The section itself does not name them.

written:1CH-17-1:6.question: What did God declare that the LORD Himself would build for David?
written:1CH-17-1:6.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CH-19-1:4.question: When David heard that the Ammonites had hired chariots and the king of Maacah, whom did he send out with the entire army of mighty men?
written:1CH-19-1:4.why: also right: B: 19:8 names Joab. Abishai is also sent out with the army in 19:11 of this same section (and commands a division in 2 Sam 10:10), so B is arguable, though the question's answer as stated is Joab. C and D are not in this campaign; Abner was already dead.

written:1CH-19-10:2.question: When Joab arrayed his forces against the Arameans and Abishai's against the Ammonites, what did Joab say he would do if the Ammonites were too strong for Abishai?
written:1CH-19-10:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:1CH-21-7:2.question: In 1 Chronicles 21, what three options did the LORD offer David through Gad as the consequence of the census?
written:1CH-21-7:2.answer: Three years of famine, three months of defeat, or three days of plague

written:1CH-21-18:1.question: In 1 Chronicles 21, whose threshing floor did David go to in order to build an altar to the LORD?
written:1CH-21-18:1.why: also right: C: Araunah is another name for Ornan in 2 Samuel 24, so C names the same man, though Scripture calls him Jebusite, not Hittite.

written:1CH-29-21:1.question: After Solomon was anointed king a second time in 1 Chronicles 29, how many bulls, rams, and lambs were offered as burnt offerings the day before?
written:1CH-29-21:1.why: the section does not settle it: The count (a thousand of each) is stated in 29:21, but the question's timing is wrong: the text says the sacrifices were offered 'the next day' after the assembly, and the feasting and second anointing happened 'that day' (29:22), not the day before.

written:2CH-1-1:2.question: Why did Solomon and the whole assembly go to the high place at Gibeon?
written:2CH-1-1:2.answer: God’s Tent of Meeting, made by Moses, was located there
written:2CH-1-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-1-1:4.question: In Solomon’s prayer at Gibeon, why did he say he needed wisdom and knowledge?
written:2CH-1-1:4.answer: To lead God’s great people, who were as numerous as the dust

written:2CH-2-1:3.question: In his message to Hiram, what did Solomon say the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot do?
written:2CH-2-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-2-1:5.question: Besides cedar, which logs from Lebanon did Solomon ask Hiram to send for the temple?
written:2CH-2-1:5.why: not clear on its own: The second item, algum/almug, is the same Hebrew word in both choices. The first item is the Hebrew berosh, which translations render as fir, cypress, or pine (e.g., ESV says cypress, KJV says fir), so the correct answer depends on the translation.

written:2CH-2-11:3.question: According to Hiram's letter, from which tribe's daughters did the mother of Huram-abi come?
written:2CH-2-11:3.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: C: Hiram's letter (2 Chronicles 2:14) says the mother was of the daughters of Dan. The parallel account in 1 Kings 7:14 calls her a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, so C is right in that passage, though not in Hiram's letter.

written:2CH-3-1:1.question: When Solomon began to build the temple in Jerusalem, whose threshing floor had David prepared as the place for it?
written:2CH-3-1:1.why: also right: A: The section names Ornan the Jebusite. A, Araunah, is the same man under another name form (2 Samuel 24:16; 1 Chronicles 21:15 use Araunah), though 'Hittite' is a mislabel since Scripture calls him a Jebusite.

written:2CH-3-5:2.question: In 2 Chronicles 3, what wood did Solomon use to panel the main room of the temple before overlaying it with fine gold?
written:2CH-3-5:2.why: also right: C: 2 Chr 3:5 names cypress for the main room paneling. Elsewhere, 1 Kings 6:15-18 says the interior walls of the temple were lined with cedar boards, so cedar (C) could fairly be argued for by another passage. The section's own text settles it as cypress.

written:2CH-3-10:2.question: In the Most Holy Place of Solomon's temple, what was the total wingspan of the two cherubim?
written:2CH-3-10:2.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: A: 2 Chronicles 3:13 says the cherubim's wings extended twenty cubits in total, spanning the room's width. 1 Kings 6:24 gives ten cubits from wingtip to wingtip for each single cherub, so A is defensible only if read as per-cherub.

written:2CH-4-1:2.question: In 2 Chronicles 4, how many baths could the Sea of cast metal hold?
written:2CH-4-1:2.why: also right: A: 1 Kings 7:26 says the same Sea held two thousand baths, so A is defensible from elsewhere in Scripture. The section itself says three thousand.

written:2CH-4-19:1.question: In 2 Chronicles 4, on which table did Solomon have gold furnishings made to hold the Bread of the Presence?
written:2CH-4-19:1.answer: The tables on which the Bread of the Presence was placed
written:2CH-4-19:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-4-19:2.question: When Solomon made the gold doors of the temple, which doors were among them besides the doors of the main hall?
written:2CH-4-19:2.answer: The inner doors to the Most Holy Place
written:2CH-4-19:2.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: A: 1 Kings 7:50 names the gold hinges/doors of the inner house (the Most Holy Place) and the doors of the temple house. 2 Chronicles 4:22 says 'the entry of the house' was also gold, so a careful reader could argue for the porch entrance (A), but the question's 'doors' wording points to C.

written:2CH-6-12:4.question: In Solomon's prayer, what did he ask God to keep for David concerning the throne of Israel?
written:2CH-6-12:4.answer: That David would never fail to have a man to sit before God on the throne

written:2CH-6-12:7.question: In Solomon's prayer, why did he ask God to answer the foreigner who came from a distant land and prayed toward the temple?
written:2CH-6-12:7.answer: So all the peoples of the earth will know God's name and fear Him

written:2CH-8-1:5.question: In keeping with whose ordinances did Solomon appoint the divisions of the priests over their service and the Levites for their duties?
written:2CH-8-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-8-1:7.question: How many chief officers who were supervisors served King Solomon, according to 2 Chronicles 8?
written:2CH-8-1:7.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: 2 Chronicles 8:10 says 250, but 1 Kings 9:23 gives 550 chief officers, so B is right elsewhere in the Bible; the question's 2 Chronicles 8 scope points to C.

written:2CH-8-1:8.question: Where did Solomon offer burnt offerings to the LORD after finishing the house of the LORD?
written:2CH-8-1:8.answer: On the altar he had built in front of the portico
written:2CH-8-1:8.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-9-1:5.question: What did King Solomon make from the algum wood brought from Ophir?
written:2CH-9-1:5.answer: Steps for the house of the LORD and his palace, and lyres and harps

written:2CH-9-13:2.question: Where did King Solomon put the gold shields he had made?
written:2CH-9-13:2.answer: In the House of the Forest of Lebanon
written:2CH-9-13:2.why: the section does not settle it: 9:16 says the king put the three hundred small gold shields in the House of the Forest of Lebanon, but the section never says where the two hundred large shields went, so the question's 'the gold shields he had made' is only partly settled by the text.

written:2CH-9-13:6.question: Why did all the kings of the earth seek an audience with Solomon?
written:2CH-9-13:6.answer: To hear the wisdom God had put in his heart
written:2CH-9-13:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-10-1:4.question: Whose advice did Rehoboam reject in favor of the counsel of the young men who had grown up with him?
written:2CH-10-1:4.answer: The elders who had served his father Solomon
written:2CH-10-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-14-1:5.question: Why did King Asa build fortified cities in Judah during the years of peace?
written:2CH-14-1:5.answer: Because the land was at peace and the LORD had given him rest

written:2CH-18-1:5.question: Where were Ahab and Jehoshaphat sitting on their thrones, dressed in royal attire, while the prophets prophesied before them?
written:2CH-18-1:5.answer: At the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria
written:2CH-18-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-18-12:2.question: After Micaiah first told Ahab to go up and triumph, how did Ahab respond?
written:2CH-18-12:2.answer: He asked how many times he must make Micaiah swear to tell only the truth

written:2CH-18-12:3.question: In 2 Chronicles 18, what did Ahab complain to Jehoshaphat about Micaiah?
written:2CH-18-12:3.answer: That Micaiah never prophesies good for him, but only bad
written:2CH-18-12:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-18-12:5.question: In Micaiah's vision, what did the LORD tell the spirit who offered to entice Ahab?
written:2CH-18-12:5.answer: “You will surely entice him and prevail. Go and do it.”
written:2CH-18-12:5.why: a quotation not word for word in the BSB text

written:2CH-18-12:6.question: When Zedekiah struck Micaiah, what question did he ask?
written:2CH-18-12:6.answer: Which way the Spirit of the LORD went when He departed from him to speak with Micaiah

written:2CH-18-12:7.question: How did Micaiah answer when Ahab said to imprison him until he returned safely?
written:2CH-18-12:7.answer: “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.”
written:2CH-18-12:7.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-18-28:1.question: In 2 Chronicles 18, what order did the king of Aram give his chariot commanders before the battle at Ramoth-gilead?
written:2CH-18-28:1.answer: Fight no one except the king of Israel
written:2CH-18-28:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-18-28:2.question: When the Aramean chariot commanders mistook Jehoshaphat for the king of Israel and turned to fight him, what happened?
written:2CH-18-28:2.answer: Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him and drew them away
written:2CH-18-28:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-18-28:3.question: How was the king of Israel wounded in the battle at Ramoth-gilead?
written:2CH-18-28:3.answer: A man drew his bow without special aim and struck him between the joints of his armor

written:2CH-20-31:2.question: In 2 Chronicles 20, whose way did Jehoshaphat walk in, without turning away from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD?
written:2CH-20-31:2.why: also right: C: Also_right C: 2 Chronicles 17:3 says Jehoshaphat walked in the first ways of his father David, and David is his forefather, so this is true elsewhere in Scripture. This section names Asa directly, so A is the intended answer. B (Ahab) is not an ancestor, and D (Rehoboam) was his great-grandfather, not grandfather, and did evil.

written:2CH-22-1:3.question: According to 2 Chronicles 22, who was Ahaziah's counselor in wickedness, leading him to walk in the ways of the house of Ahab?
written:2CH-22-1:3.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:2CH-22-8:1.question: In 2 Chronicles 22, why did the people bury King Ahaziah of Judah after Jehu's soldiers had put him to death?
written:2CH-22-8:1.answer: He was the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart

written:2CH-23-12:3.question: Why did Jehoiada the priest command that Athaliah be brought out between the ranks before being put to death?
written:2CH-23-12:3.answer: She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD

written:2CH-23-16:3.question: After Jehoiada gave oversight of the LORD's house to the Levitical priests, whom did the text say had appointed them to offer burnt offerings with rejoicing and song?

written:2CH-25-17:2.question: According to 2 Chronicles 25, why would Amaziah not listen to Jehoash's warning, when Amaziah of Judah had challenged him to meet face to face?
written:2CH-25-17:2.answer: It came from God, to deliver them into Jehoash's hand, because they had sought Edom's gods

written:2CH-25-17:4.question: After breaking down part of Jerusalem's wall, from whom or where did Jehoash take the gold, silver and articles, and what else did he take before returning to Samaria?
written:2CH-25-17:4.why: not clear on its own: Compound question: the 'from whom or where' part (the gold, silver and vessels taken from the house of God, kept with Obed-edom, and the king's treasuries) has no matching choice. Only A (hostages) fits the 'what else' part, and it does not answer the first part. Needs rewording or a choice that covers the treasury.

written:2CH-25-25:2.question: According to 2 Chronicles 25, after Amaziah's conspirators killed him at Lachish, how was his body brought back to Judah?
written:2CH-25-25:2.answer: On horses, then buried with his fathers in the City of Judah
written:2CH-25-25:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-26-1:2.question: Who instructed King Uzziah of Judah in the fear of God, during whose days he sought God?
written:2CH-26-1:2.why: not clear on its own: 2 Chronicles 26:5 says Uzziah 'sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God,' but it never says Zechariah instructed him in the fear of God, so the question assumes something the text does not state. The name 'Zechariah' is also unqualified, though the verse is the only one tying Uzziah's seeking God to a named person.

written:2CH-27-1:3.question: After King Jotham of Judah defeated the king of the Ammonites, what did the Ammonites give him each year for three years?
written:2CH-27-1:3.answer: A hundred talents of silver and ten thousand cors each of wheat and barley

written:2CH-28-16:4.question: After Ahaz gathered up the articles of the house of God, what did he do with them?
written:2CH-28-16:4.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: C: 2 Chr 28:24 says Ahaz cut the vessels of God's house in pieces. 2 Kings 16:8 separately says he sent gold and silver from the LORD's house to the king of Assyria, so C is true of that passage, but the question's wording follows Chronicles.

written:2CH-29-1:8.question: Into which place did the Levites carry the unclean things they brought out of the temple of the LORD?
written:2CH-29-1:8.why: also right: B: The section names the Kidron Valley. Option B (Valley of Jehoshaphat) is not named in this section; it appears only in Joel 3:2, 12, and is traditionally identified with the Kidron Valley, but the text itself does not equate them.

written:2CH-32-9:3.question: In Sennacherib's message to Jerusalem, what did he say Hezekiah had told Judah and Jerusalem about worship, after removing the high places and altars?
written:2CH-32-9:3.answer: “You must worship before one altar, and on it you shall burn sacrifices”

written:2CH-32-9:4.question: What argument did Sennacherib use to claim that the God of Hezekiah could not deliver Jerusalem from his hand?
written:2CH-32-9:4.answer: No god of any nation or kingdom had delivered his people from Assyria

written:2CH-32-20:2.question: After the LORD's angel destroyed the Assyrian commanders, what happened to King Sennacherib when he entered the temple of his god?
written:2CH-32-20:2.answer: Some of his own sons struck him down with the sword
written:2CH-32-20:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-32-24:1.question: After Hezekiah recovered from his mortal illness, why did wrath come upon him, Judah and Jerusalem?
written:2CH-32-24:1.answer: His heart was proud and he did not repay the favor shown him

written:2CH-32-24:3.question: What did Hezekiah do with the Spring of Gihon?
written:2CH-32-24:3.answer: He blocked its upper outlet and channeled it down to the west side of the City of David

written:2CH-32-24:4.question: When ambassadors from the rulers of Babylon came to Hezekiah, why did God leave him alone?
written:2CH-32-24:4.answer: To test him, that He might know all that was in his heart

written:2CH-33-1:4.question: According to God's words to David and Solomon, on what condition would God never again cause the Israelites to leave the land?
written:2CH-33-1:4.answer: If they were careful to do all He commanded through Moses
written:2CH-33-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-33-1:5.question: What was the result of Manasseh leading the people of Judah and Jerusalem astray?
written:2CH-33-1:5.answer: They did greater evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed
written:2CH-33-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-34-8:2.question: In 2 Chronicles 34, whom did the Levites at the doors collect the temple money from, according to the list of peoples?
written:2CH-34-8:2.answer: The people of Manasseh and Ephraim, and the remnant of Israel
written:2CH-34-8:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-34-8:4.question: In the temple repairs under Josiah, what skill did the other Levites who were over the laborers all have?
written:2CH-34-8:4.answer: They were skilled with musical instruments
written:2CH-34-8:4.why: not clear on its own: "The other Levites" refers to Jahath and Obadiah, who are never named in the question, so a quiz-taker cannot tell who is being set apart. The answer is A (2 Chronicles 34:12), but the question should name Jahath and Obadiah as the overseers.

written:2CH-34-14:3.question: After hearing the words of the Law, why did King Josiah say he wanted the LORD to be consulted?
written:2CH-34-14:3.answer: The LORD's wrath was poured out because their fathers had not kept his word

written:2CH-34-22:2.question: According to Huldah, why would the LORD bring calamity on Jerusalem and its people?
written:2CH-34-22:2.answer: They had forsaken Him and burned incense to other gods
written:2CH-34-22:2.why: also right: A: A is not stated in this section, but Scripture elsewhere ties Judah's downfall to Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood and his defiling of the temple (2 Kings 21:4-16; 24:3-4).

written:2CH-34-29:1.question: When King Josiah made a covenant before the LORD at the house of the LORD, what did he promise to do?
written:2CH-34-29:1.answer: Follow the LORD and keep His commandments with all his heart and soul

written:2CH-35-1:4.question: In Josiah's Passover, according to whose written instructions were the Levites told to prepare themselves by families in their divisions?
written:2CH-35-1:4.answer: David king of Israel and his son Solomon
written:2CH-35-1:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:2CH-35-20:3.question: On what battlefield did the archers shoot King Josiah, so that he said, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded!”?
written:2CH-35-20:3.why: also right: D: The section names the Plain of Megiddo, so A is the direct answer. The Plain of Megiddo lies within the broader Plain of Jezreel (Esdraelon), so D is a broader form of the same battlefield and could fairly be argued for.

written:2CH-36-9:1.question: How old was Jehoiachin when he became king of Judah?
written:2CH-36-9:1.why: also right somewhere in the Bible: B: 2 Kings 24:8 says Jehoiachin was eighteen when he began to reign. 2 Chronicles 36:9 says he was eight, so B is also a Bible answer. The Kings account is the more common reading, so C is the pick.

written:NEH-7-4:2.question: When Nehemiah gathered the people to be enrolled, what did he find written in the register of those who had first returned to Jerusalem?
written:NEH-7-4:2.answer: The list of the people who came up from captivity
written:NEH-7-4:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:NEH-13-23:1.question: In Nehemiah 13, what happened to about half of the children of the Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab?
written:NEH-13-23:1.answer: They spoke the language of Ashdod but could not speak the language of Judah

written:NEH-13-23:2.question: When Nehemiah confronted the Jews who had married foreign women, which earlier king of Israel did he name as an example of someone led into sin by foreign women?
written:NEH-13-23:2.why: also right: C: Verse 13:26 names Solomon. Ahab was also led into sin by a foreign wife, Jezebel (1 Kings 16:31; 21:25), so C could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture, though the section names only Solomon.

written:PSA-18-1:5.question: In Psalm 18, David says God's way is perfect. What does he say about the word of the LORD in the same verse?
written:PSA-18-1:5.why: also right: A, C: Verse 30 says the word of the LORD is flawless (D). Elsewhere Scripture says God's word endures forever (Isa 40:8; Ps 119:89) and is a lamp to my feet (Ps 119:105), so A and C are true of the word of the LORD in other passages, though neither is what this verse says.

written:PSA-37-1:2.question: In Psalm 37, what does David say will happen to the swords and bows of the wicked who draw them against the poor and needy?
written:PSA-37-1:2.answer: Their swords will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be broken

written:PSA-56-1:2.question: In Psalm 56, when the psalmist is afraid, what does he say he does?
written:PSA-56-1:2.answer: He puts his trust in God
written:PSA-56-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-57-1:2.question: In Psalm 57:4, David says he lies down among ravenous men whose teeth are like what?
written:PSA-57-1:2.why: The question said David lies down among 'ravenous men' and that their teeth are 'like' something; the BSB says he lies down with ravenous beasts, with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, so the wording now matches.

written:PSA-59-1:2.question: In Psalm 59, David says that God laughs at his enemies. Whom else does David say God scoffs at?
written:PSA-59-1:2.why: also right: A: Psalm 59:8 says God scoffs at 'all the nations' (B). Option A is not in this section, but Psalm 2:4 says the Lord scoffs at the kings and rulers of the earth, so it could fairly be argued from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:PSA-59-1:5.question: In Psalm 59, what does David say he will do in the morning?
written:PSA-59-1:5.answer: Sing of God's strength and proclaim His loving devotion
written:PSA-59-1:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-63-1:2.question: In Psalm 63, where does David say he will sing for joy, because God is his help?
written:PSA-63-1:2.answer: In the shadow of God's wings
written:PSA-63-1:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PSA-99-1:1.question: In Psalm 99, above which winged beings is the LORD said to be enthroned?
written:PSA-99-1:1.why: also right: C: Psalm 99:1 names the cherubim. Elsewhere, Ezekiel 10:20 identifies the Ezekiel 'living creatures' as cherubim, so C is arguable as another name for the same winged beings.

written:PRO-5-1:4.question: In Proverbs 5:9-10, what will happen to a man's wealth and labors if he goes near the forbidden woman?
written:PRO-5-1:4.answer: Strangers will feast on his wealth, and his labors will enrich a foreigner's house

written:PRO-11-1:2.question: According to Proverbs 11:2, what follows when pride comes?
written:PRO-11-1:2.why: also right: D: Proverbs 11:2 says disgrace follows pride, but Proverbs 16:18 says pride goes before destruction, so D is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:PRO-11-1:3.question: According to Proverbs 11:2, what comes with humility?
written:PRO-11-1:3.why: also right: A, B, D: 11:2 settles wisdom, but elsewhere humility brings honor (15:33, 18:12) and humility with the fear of the LORD brings riches, honor, and life (22:4), so A, B, and D are all arguable.

written:PRO-21-1:2.question: According to Proverbs 21:3, what is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice?
written:PRO-21-1:2.why: also right: D: 21:3 names only righteousness and justice. Hosea 6:6 and Matthew 9:13 say God desires mercy rather than sacrifice, so mercy in D has scriptural support, though the choice also includes hospitality, which is not in the claim.

written:ECC-5-8:5.question: In Ecclesiastes 5, what does the Preacher say he has seen to be good and fitting during the few days of life God has given a man?
written:ECC-5-8:5.answer: To eat and drink and find satisfaction in his labor
written:ECC-5-8:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:ISA-34-5:2.question: In Isaiah 34, in which city of Edom does the LORD say He has a sacrifice?
written:ISA-34-5:2.why: also right: B, D: Bozrah is named in the text. Teman is also an Edomite place elsewhere (Amos 1:12, Jer 49:7, Obad 9), and Sela is often identified with Edomite Petra, though Scripture does not explicitly place Sela in Edom.

written:ISA-34-5:5.question: In Isaiah 34, what does the LORD tell people to search and read, saying that not one of the creatures in Edom will go missing?
written:ISA-34-5:5.why: also right: A: The text says 'the scroll of the LORD' and the creatures are owls and birds of prey, not 'creatures in Edom' in the general sense, but C is clearly stated. Choice A is arguably a narrower form of the scroll of the LORD (the Law as God's book, cf. 2 Chr 17:9), though this section does not identify it as the Law of Moses.

written:ISA-37-8:2.question: In Sennacherib's message to Hezekiah, which question did he ask to show that the gods of conquered nations had not saved them?
written:ISA-37-8:2.answer: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by his fathers rescue those nations?

written:ISA-37-14:2.question: In his prayer, Hezekiah asked the LORD to listen to the words Sennacherib had sent to defy whom?
written:ISA-37-14:2.why: also right: B, C: The section says the letter defied "the living God" (37:17), so D is settled. B ("God of Hezekiah's fathers") and C ("Holy One of Jacob") are other titles for the same God, though neither wording appears in this passage.

written:ISA-37-14:3.question: When Hezekiah asked the LORD to save Judah from Sennacherib's hand, what reason did he give?
written:ISA-37-14:3.answer: So all the kingdoms of the earth would know He alone is God

written:ISA-39-1:4.question: In Isaiah 39, what did Isaiah say would happen to some of Hezekiah’s descendants?
written:ISA-39-1:4.answer: They would be taken away to be eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace

written:JER-14-19:1.question: In the prayer of Jeremiah 14:19-22, what do the people say they acknowledge to the LORD besides the guilt of their fathers?
written:JER-14-19:1.why: also right: D: Verse 20 states 'We acknowledge our wickedness.' D is arguable because Baal worship is a specific form of that wickedness, and Jeremiah names it elsewhere (e.g., 2:23, 9:14), though this prayer does not mention Baal.

written:JER-14-19:2.question: In Jeremiah's prayer for Judah, what do the people ask the LORD to remember and not break, for the sake of His name?
written:JER-14-19:2.why: also right: A: Verse 21 asks God to remember 'Your covenant with us; do not break it.' A is arguable because the Sinai covenant with Israel was recorded on stone tablets, so the law on tablets is a narrower detail of that covenant, though the prayer itself names only the covenant.

written:JER-17-19:2.question: Where did the LORD tell Jeremiah to stand first to deliver His message about the Sabbath, in addition to all the other gates of Jerusalem?
written:JER-17-19:2.answer: The gate of the people, used by the kings of Judah
written:JER-17-19:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-18-18:3.question: In Jeremiah 18, what did Jeremiah say he had done before the LORD for the people who plotted against him?
written:JER-18-18:3.answer: Stood before Him to speak good on their behalf
written:JER-18-18:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-40-7:2.question: In Jeremiah 40, what did Gedaliah tell the commanders and their men to gather and store in jars while living in the cities they had taken?
written:JER-40-7:2.answer: Wine grapes, summer fruit, and oil
written:JER-40-7:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-40-13:2.question: When Johanan privately offered to kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah in secret, how did Gedaliah son of Ahikam respond?
written:JER-40-13:2.answer: He forbade it, saying that what Johanan said about Ishmael was a lie

written:JER-41-1:3.question: Besides Gedaliah, whom else did Ishmael kill at Mizpah?
written:JER-41-1:3.answer: All the Jews with Gedaliah and the Chaldean soldiers there
written:JER-41-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JER-51-15:1.question: In Jeremiah 51, by what does the LORD establish the world?
written:JER-51-15:1.why: also right: B: Verse 15 says the LORD established the world by His wisdom. B (strength) is a near-synonym of the 'power' by which He made the earth in the same verse, so it is arguably also supported, though the text does not say He established the world by strength.

written:JER-52-12:2.question: When Nebuzaradan entered Jerusalem, besides the house of the LORD and the houses of the city, which building did he burn down?
written:JER-52-12:2.why: also right: A: The House of the Forest of Lebanon was a building in Solomon's palace complex, so it could arguably fall under 'the royal palace,' though neither this section nor 2 Kings names it as burned.

written:LAM-1-1:1.question: In Lamentations 1:1, what has the city of Jerusalem, once great among the nations, become?
written:LAM-1-1:1.why: also right: D: 1:1 says she has become a widow and, in the same verse, the princess of the provinces has become a slave. D, 'captive queen,' is a loose paraphrase of the princess-turned-slave clause, though the text says 'princess,' not 'queen.' 'Widow' is the direct answer.

written:EZK-26-1:8.question: In Ezekiel 26, what will the princes of the sea do when they see Tyre's downfall?
written:EZK-26-1:8.answer: Come down from their thrones, remove their robes, and sit on the ground trembling

written:EZK-34-11:4.question: In Ezekiel 34:16, which of these does the Lord say He will do for His flock?
written:EZK-34-11:4.why: also right: C: 34:16 says He will destroy the sleek and strong, so 'weaken the strong ones' is a loose but arguable match. 'Bind up the broken' is the exact wording and the only item the Lord says He does for the flock.

written:AMO-5-4:3.question: In Amos 5:8, what does the LORD do to the waters of the sea, as part of showing His power?
written:AMO-5-4:3.answer: Summons them and pours them over the earth
written:AMO-5-4:3.why: also right: B: 5:8 says He summons the sea's waters and pours them over the earth (D). B is not stated in this verse, but the LORD did part the sea for Israel elsewhere (Exodus 14:21-22; Joshua 3:16), so it could be argued for from the wider Bible.

written:MIC-2-6:2.question: In Micah 2:11, what would the preacher say who is "just the preacher for this people"?
written:MIC-2-6:2.answer: “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink”
written:MIC-2-6:2.why: not clear on its own: The quoted phrase "just the preacher for this people" is not Micah's wording (it paraphrases "prophet of this people"), and the question never says the speaker is a lying prophet, so it is unclear whom it means. Micah 2:11 gives wine and strong drink (B). A ("peace and safety") is what false prophets preached elsewhere (Micah 3:5; Jeremiah 6:14), so a reader could fairly argue for it.

written:ZEC-8-1:1.question: In Zechariah 8:3, what will Jerusalem be called when the LORD returns to Zion and dwells in Jerusalem?
written:ZEC-8-1:1.why: also right: B: Option B, "City of Righteousness," is a name Scripture gives Jerusalem in Isaiah 1:26, though it is not the name given in Zechariah 8:3.

written:ZEC-8-1:4.question: In Zechariah 8:7-8, from which lands does the LORD promise to save His people and bring them back to Jerusalem?
written:ZEC-8-1:4.answer: From the land of the east and the land of the west
written:ZEC-8-1:4.why: also right: C: Option C, north and south, is a promised gathering in other passages (e.g., Isaiah 43:5-6), though Zechariah 8:7-8 itself names only east and west.

written:MAT-11-7:4.question: In Matthew 11, what did Jesus say people called the Son of Man because He came eating and drinking?
written:MAT-11-7:4.answer: A glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners
written:MAT-11-7:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MAT-12-1:3.question: In Matthew 12, Jesus said that something was "greater than the temple" and was there. What did Jesus say about it?
written:MAT-12-1:3.answer: Something greater than the temple is here
written:MAT-12-1:3.why: not clear on its own: The stem never names the thing Jesus is talking about ('something was greater than the temple and was there'), so 'it' is unclear, and choice B just repeats the stem's own wording. Reword to something like: 'In Matthew 12:6, what did Jesus say is greater than the temple?' with a choice naming Jesus himself.

written:MRK-3-1:1.question: After Jesus healed the man with the withered hand in the synagogue, with whom did the Pharisees begin plotting how they might kill Him?
written:MRK-3-1:1.why: also right: C: Mark 3:6 names the Herodians directly. Elsewhere, the chief priests and Pharisees jointly plotted to kill Jesus (John 11:53, 57; Matthew 27:62), so C could be argued for from other Scripture, though not from this section.

written:MRK-4-13:2.question: In Jesus' explanation of the parable of the sower in Mark 4, why do those represented by the seeds on rocky ground quickly fall away?
written:MRK-4-13:2.answer: They have no root, and trouble or persecution comes because of the word

written:MRK-6-14:2.question: Why did Herod protect John the Baptist from Herodias, who wanted to kill him?
written:MRK-6-14:2.answer: He feared John, knowing he was a righteous and holy man
written:MRK-6-14:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-6-14:6.question: After John the Baptist was beheaded, what did his disciples do when they heard about it?
written:MRK-6-14:6.answer: They took his body and placed it in a tomb
written:MRK-6-14:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-6-45:1.question: In Mark 6, after Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and go on ahead, where did he go to pray?
written:MRK-6-45:1.why: The question and answer match Mark 6:46, but one wrong choice used the old "desert place" wording, so it now reads "a secluded place" in modern language like the others.

written:MRK-8-11:2.question: In Mark 8, after the Pharisees demanded a sign from heaven, what did Jesus do when He left them?
written:MRK-8-11:2.answer: He got back into the boat and crossed to the other side
written:MRK-8-11:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-8-27:1.question: In Mark 8, when Jesus asked His disciples on the way to the villages around Caesarea Philippi who people said He was, which of these did they say people were calling Him?
written:MRK-8-27:1.why: also right: B, D: The section explicitly names Elijah. Its unnamed "one of the prophets" could be argued to cover Isaiah (B) or Moses (D), since both were prophets, but the section does not name them.

written:MRK-8-31:2.question: When Jesus spoke frankly about His coming suffering and death, what did Peter do?
written:MRK-8-31:2.answer: He took Jesus aside and began to rebuke Him
written:MRK-8-31:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:MRK-8-34:2.question: In Jesus' teaching to the crowd and His disciples in Mark 8, who will be ashamed of a person who is ashamed of Jesus and His words?
written:MRK-8-34:2.answer: The Son of Man, when He comes in His Father’s glory
written:MRK-8-34:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-9-1:3.question: As Jesus, Peter, James, and John came down from the mountain, what did Jesus order them to do?
written:MRK-9-1:3.answer: Tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen

written:MRK-9-42:1.question: In Jesus' teaching in Mark 9 about causing one of the little ones who believe in Him to stumble, what does He say would be better for that person?
written:MRK-9-42:1.answer: To have a large millstone hung around his neck and be thrown into the sea

written:MRK-10-35:3.question: When James and John asked Jesus for places in His glory, what did Jesus say about sitting at His right or left?
written:MRK-10-35:3.answer: It is not His to grant; the seats belong to those for whom they are prepared

written:MRK-12-35:1.question: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, whom did He ask how they could say that the Christ is the Son of David?
written:MRK-12-35:1.why: the section does not settle it: The scribes are named as the subject of Jesus' question ('How can the scribes say...'), not as its addressee. The section never says whom He asked; the only audience mentioned is the large crowd in 12:37. B is the intended pick by elimination, but the text does not settle it.

written:MRK-13-1:3.question: In Mark 13, what did Jesus say wars and rumors of wars are, when He told His disciples not to be alarmed?
written:MRK-13-1:3.answer: Things that must happen, though the end is still to come
written:MRK-13-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-14-32:2.question: In Gethsemane, what Aramaic word for God did Jesus use when he began his prayer?
written:MRK-14-32:2.why: also right: D: The section shows Jesus saying "Abba, Father" at the start of his prayer, but it never calls Abba Aramaic or says it names God. Those points come from outside knowledge. Choice D, "Eloi," is also an Aramaic-form word meaning "my God" (Mark 15:34), so it could fairly be argued for.

written:MRK-14-32:4.question: In Gethsemane, how many times did Jesus return and find his disciples sleeping before he said, “Rise, let us go”?
written:MRK-14-32:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:MRK-14-53:2.question: While Jesus was being questioned by the high priest in Mark 14, where did Peter go and what did he do there?
written:MRK-14-53:2.answer: He sat in the courtyard with the officers, warming himself by the fire

written:MRK-16-1:2.question: After the women ran from Jesus' tomb trembling and bewildered, what did they do in their fear?
written:MRK-16-1:2.answer: They did not say a word to anyone
written:MRK-16-1:2.why: not clear on its own: Answer A matches Mark 16:8, but the question never names which women or which Gospel. In Matthew 28:8 and Luke 24:9 the women do tell the disciples, so C is also right in those accounts.

written:LUK-6-46:1.question: In Jesus' teaching in Luke 6:46, what does He ask people who call Him 'Lord, Lord'?
written:LUK-6-46:1.answer: Why they call Him 'Lord, Lord' but do not do what He says

written:LUK-7-18:1.question: When John the Baptist sent two of his disciples to Jesus in Luke 7, what did he tell them to ask?
written:LUK-7-18:1.answer: Whether Jesus was the One who was to come, or if they should look for someone else

written:LUK-8-16:1.question: In Jesus' lesson of the lamp in Luke 8, what does Jesus say a person does NOT do with a lit lamp: cover it with what?
written:LUK-8-16:1.why: also right: C: Luke 8:16 says the lamp is not covered with a jar. The parallel lamp saying in Mark 4:21 (NASB) puts it under a "basket," so C is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture, though Luke's own word is jar.

written:LUK-10-1:3.question: Jesus told the seventy-two that if a town refused to welcome them, it would be more bearable on that day for which city than for that town?
written:LUK-10-1:3.why: also right: C: Sodom is named in the section (10:12). Tyre is outside the excerpt but Luke 10:13-14 says it would be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at judgment than for the unrepentant towns, so Tyre fits the same pattern, though the excerpt itself settles only Sodom.

written:LUK-10-21:1.question: In Jesus' prayer of thanksgiving in Luke 10, to whom did God reveal "these things" while hiding them from the wise and learned?
written:LUK-10-21:1.why: not clear on its own: "These things" has no antecedent in the question itself, so a quiz-taker cannot tell what is meant without the passage. The answer is D (Luke 10:21, "revealed them to little children").

written:LUK-11-37:3.question: In Luke 11, Jesus said the Pharisees paid tithes of mint, rue, and every herb but disregarded what?
written:LUK-11-37:3.answer: Justice and the love of God
written:LUK-11-37:3.why: also right: D: Luke 11:42 names justice and the love of God. Matthew 23:23 has Jesus list the Pharisees' neglect of 'justice, mercy and faithfulness,' so 'mercy and faithfulness' is also defensible from Scripture.

written:LUK-11-37:4.question: In Luke 11, Jesus said the Pharisees loved the chief seats in the synagogues and what else?
written:LUK-11-37:4.why: also right: A: Luke 11:43 gives the marketplace greetings as the 'what else.' Luke 20:46 and Matthew 23:6 also say the Pharisees loved the places of honor at banquets, so A is true of them elsewhere in Scripture.

written:LUK-14-15:2.question: In Jesus' parable of the great banquet, after the servant reported that there was still room, what did the master tell him to do?
written:LUK-14-15:2.answer: Go to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in
written:LUK-14-15:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-17-20:2.question: In Luke 17, to what did Jesus compare the coming of the Son of Man in His day?
written:LUK-17-20:2.answer: Lightning that flashes and lights up the sky from end to end
written:LUK-17-20:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-17-20:4.question: In Luke 17, what were people doing up to the day Noah entered the ark, according to Jesus?
written:LUK-17-20:4.answer: Eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage
written:LUK-17-20:4.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-19-11:1.question: Why did Jesus tell the parable of the ten minas?
written:LUK-19-11:1.answer: He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently

written:LUK-19-41:2.question: In Luke 19, why did Jesus say Jerusalem would be leveled and not one stone left on another?
written:LUK-19-41:2.answer: Because it did not recognize the time of its visitation from God
written:LUK-19-41:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-24-13:2.question: At the table in Emmaus, what did Jesus do just before the two disciples' eyes were opened and they recognized Him?
written:LUK-24-13:2.answer: He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them
written:LUK-24-13:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JHN-13-18:3.question: Why did some disciples think Jesus told Judas to do quickly what he was about to do, since Judas kept the money bag?
written:JHN-13-18:3.answer: To buy what was needed for the feast, or give to the poor

written:JHN-20-10:1.question: When Mary Magdalene bent down to look into Jesus' empty tomb, what did she see?
written:JHN-20-10:1.answer: Two angels in white sitting where Jesus' body had lain
written:JHN-20-10:1.why: also right: A: Choice A is a true detail of the tomb (the linen cloths lay apart, per John 20:5-7, and Mary looked inside), though this section says only that she saw the two angels. B and C do not match this section; B resembles Luke 24:4's two men, a different visit.

written:JHN-20-10:2.question: When Jesus spoke her name outside the tomb, what did Mary Magdalene call him in Hebrew?
written:JHN-20-10:2.why: also right: C: The text gives 'Rabboni.' C ('Rabbi,' meaning 'Master') is the broader root of that title and close in meaning, so it could be argued, though it is not the word the text gives.

written:JHN-20-10:3.question: What message did Jesus tell Mary Magdalene to take to his brothers outside the tomb?
written:JHN-20-10:3.answer: “I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.”

written:ACT-4-23:2.question: In Acts 4, what happened after the believers had prayed together?
written:ACT-4-23:2.answer: Their meeting place was shaken and they were filled with the Holy Spirit

written:ACT-7-9:2.question: According to Stephen in Acts 7, how many relatives in all did Joseph send for to come to Egypt with his father Jacob?
written:ACT-7-9:2.why: also right: B: Stephen's text says seventy-five, which follows the Septuagint of Genesis 46:27. The Hebrew text of Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5 gives seventy for Jacob's household going to Egypt, so 'Seventy' could be argued from elsewhere in Scripture, though it is not Stephen's figure.

written:ACT-7-15:1.question: In Stephen's speech in Acts 7, to which city were the bones of Jacob and our fathers carried back from Egypt for burial?
written:ACT-7-15:1.why: also right: A: Acts 7:16 says the bones were carried back to Shechem. Hebron is arguable only for Jacob alone: Genesis 50:13 buries him in the cave of Machpelah, which is in Hebron. Stephen's account, which the question asks about, gives Shechem.

written:1CO-9-1:2.question: In defending his rights as an apostle, which Law of Moses command about an animal does Paul quote?
written:1CO-9-1:2.answer: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain
written:1CO-9-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CO-9-1:5.question: According to Paul, why did he and Barnabas not use their right to support from the Corinthians?
written:1CO-9-1:5.answer: They would put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ

written:2CO-4-7:2.question: According to Paul in 2 Corinthians 4:7, why do we have the treasure in jars of clay?
written:2CO-4-7:2.answer: To show the surpassingly great power is from God, not from us
written:2CO-4-7:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PHP-2-19:4.question: Why was Epaphroditus distressed, according to Paul's letter to the Philippians?
written:PHP-2-19:4.answer: The Philippians had heard he was ill
written:PHP-2-19:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:PHP-4-21:2.question: How does Paul close his letter to the Philippians?
written:PHP-4-21:2.answer: With a prayer that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with their spirit

written:TIT-1-5:1.question: In Titus 1, why did Paul leave Titus in Crete?
written:TIT-1-5:1.answer: To set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town

written:TIT-3-9:1.question: In Titus 3:10, how many warnings should Titus give a divisive man before rejecting him?
written:TIT-3-9:1.answer: Two warnings: a first and a second
written:TIT-3-9:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:HEB-3-7:1.question: In Hebrews 3, God says He swore on oath in His anger about the generation that tested Him in the wilderness. What did He swear about them?
written:HEB-3-7:1.answer: They shall never enter My rest
written:HEB-3-7:1.why: also right: C: C is also defensible from elsewhere: Numbers 14:21-30 records God swearing that that generation would not see or enter the land He promised. This section itself says only "They shall never enter My rest," so D is the answer it settles.

written:HEB-11-20:1.question: In Hebrews 11, what did Jacob do, by faith, as he was dying, regarding Joseph's sons?
written:HEB-11-20:1.why: also right: B: The section says Jacob blessed each of Joseph's sons, so C is correct. But Genesis 48:5, the same deathbed scene, has Jacob adopting Ephraim and Manasseh as his own sons, so B is also true of this event and the section does not rule it out.

written:REV-13-1:5.question: According to Revelation 13, whose names have been written from the foundation of the world in the Book of Life, so that they do not worship the beast?
written:REV-13-1:5.why: also right: B: 13:8 says the Book of Life belongs to the Lamb, but it does not say whose names are written in it; the saints (B) are implied by the call to perseverance in 13:10 and could fairly be argued for. The question's wording also mixes up the book's owner with the people whose names are written.

written:REV-18-1:2.question: In Revelation 18, what does Babylon say in her heart as she glorifies herself and lives in luxury?
written:REV-18-1:2.answer: “I sit as queen; I am not a widow and will never see grief.”
