written:REV-18-1:3.question: In Revelation 18, in how much time will the plagues of death, grief, and famine come upon Babylon?
written:REV-18-1:3.why: also right: D: 18:8 says the plagues of death, grief, and famine come 'in one day,' which settles the answer. But 'in one hour' is used for Babylon's judgment in 18:10, 17, and 19 (outside this section), so D is arguable from elsewhere in Revelation.

written:DEU-19-1:4.question: In Deuteronomy 19, what were the Israelites to do if the LORD enlarged their territory and they carefully kept His commandments?
written:DEU-19-1:4.answer: Add three more cities to the first three
written:DEU-19-1:4.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:DEU-19-1:5.question: In Deuteronomy 19, what was to happen to a man who hated his neighbor, lay in wait, killed him, and fled to a city of refuge?
written:DEU-19-1:5.answer: The elders of his city bring him back and hand him over to the avenger of blood

written:DEU-26-1:5.question: In the declaration of Deuteronomy 26, what did Israel do when the Egyptians mistreated them and put them to hard labor?
written:DEU-26-1:5.answer: They called out to the LORD, the God of their fathers
written:DEU-26-1:5.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:DEU-26-1:6.question: In the declaration of Deuteronomy 26, how did the LORD bring Israel out of Egypt?
written:DEU-26-1:6.answer: With a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders

written:DEU-28-15:6.question: In Deuteronomy 28, Israel's numbers once resembled what, before the LORD says they will be left few in number?
written:DEU-28-15:6.why: also right: C: Section says 'as numerous as the stars in the sky' (28:62). Elsewhere Scripture likens Israel's numbers to the sand of the seashore (Gen 22:17; Hos 1:10; 1 Kgs 4:20), so C could be argued, though the section itself names the stars.

written:DEU-28-15:7.question: In Deuteronomy 28, how will the LORD return disobedient Israel to Egypt?
written:DEU-28-15:7.answer: In ships, by a route they were told never to see again
written:DEU-28-15:7.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-13-8:1.question: In Joshua 13, what did the tribe of Levi receive as its inheritance instead of land?
written:JOS-13-8:1.answer: The offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel
written:JOS-13-8:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1CH-10-1:1.question: When wounded Saul told his armor-bearer to run him through with a sword, what was he afraid the uncircumcised Philistines would do to him?
written:1CH-10-1:1.why: not clear on its own: No choice matches. 1 Samuel 31:4 says Saul feared the Philistines would thrust him through and 'make sport of me' (mock him). B, 'torture,' is the nearest option but is not what the text says. Needs a corrected answer choice.

written:1CH-21-1:3.question: In Joab's report of David's census in 1 Chronicles 21, how many men who drew the sword were in all Israel?
written:1CH-21-1:3.why: also right: B, D: The section states 1,100,000 for all Israel, including Judah. The parallel account in 2 Samuel 24:9 gives 800,000 for Israel and 500,000 for Judah, so B (Israel alone) and D (the combined total) match that other report, but not this Chronicles report.

written:1CH-23-7:1.question: In 1 Chronicles 23, who were the two sons of Gershon listed as the Gershonites in David's division of the Levites?
written:1CH-23-7:1.why: also right: D: The section names Ladan and Shimei as the Gershonites (23:7). Elsewhere, Exodus 6:17 and 1 Chronicles 6:17 name Libni and Shimei as Gershon's sons, so D is also true of Gershon's sons in Scripture, though not in this chapter. Ladan is often identified with Libni, but that identification is not stated in this section.

written:2CH-34-3:2.question: When Josiah cleansed Judah and Jerusalem, what did he scatter the crushed idols over?
written:2CH-34-3:2.answer: The graves of those who had sacrificed to them
written:2CH-34-3:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-45-1:3.question: In Psalm 45, what is the scepter of the kingdom of the king whose throne endures forever and ever?
written:PSA-45-1:3.why: not clear on its own: Psalm 45:6 says the scepter is 'a right scepter' (uprightness/righteousness), which no choice states exactly; Justice (B) is only the nearest match, so the key may be wrong.

written:PSA-46-1:1.question: In Psalm 46, what does the psalmist say God does to weapons of war when He makes wars cease throughout the earth?
written:PSA-46-1:1.answer: He breaks the bow, shatters the spear, and burns the shields
written:PSA-46-1:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:PSA-141-1:2.question: In Psalm 141, what does the psalmist ask that his prayer be like, set before the LORD?
written:PSA-141-1:2.why: also right: D: The text says 'incense'. D ('a fragrant spice') is arguable because incense is compounded from fragrant spices (Exod 30:34-35), so it is a looser description of the same thing.

written:ISA-36-1:2.question: When Eliakim, Shebna and Joah asked the Rabshakeh to speak Aramaic, why did he refuse?
written:ISA-36-1:2.answer: His master sent him to speak to the men on the wall too

written:ISA-36-1:6.question: When the Rabshakeh came from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army, where did he stop?
written:ISA-36-1:6.answer: By the aqueduct of the upper pool
written:ISA-36-1:6.why: also right: B: The text says he stopped at the aqueduct of the upper pool, not at Gihon. The upper pool's conduit is traditionally fed from the Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley, so B is arguable, though the text never names Gihon.

written:ISA-59-1:1.question: In Isaiah 59:1, what does the LORD's arm not lack, as the verse says it is not too short for it?

written:JER-2-23:5.question: In Jeremiah 2:32, what does the LORD say His people have forgotten for days without number?
written:JER-2-23:5.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:JER-39-1:3.question: When Zedekiah and the soldiers of Jerusalem saw the Babylonian officials sitting in the Middle Gate, what did they do?
written:JER-39-1:3.answer: They fled the city at night by way of the king's garden

written:MRK-1-40:2.question: In Mark 1:45, what happened to Jesus' ministry because the healed leper spread the news openly?
written:MRK-1-40:2.answer: He could no longer enter a town in plain view
written:MRK-1-40:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:MRK-2-23:2.question: In Mark 2, during whose high priesthood did Jesus say David entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread?
written:MRK-2-23:2.why: also right: C: The section names Abiathar, so B is the answer it gives. But 1 Samuel 21:1-6 records that Ahimelech was the priest at Nob who gave David the bread, and Abiathar was Ahimelech's son, so Ahimelech is arguably right from elsewhere in Scripture. Zadok and Eli were not high priests at this event.

written:LUK-6-6:1.question: In Luke 6, when Jesus entered the synagogue on another Sabbath and saw a man with a withered hand, why were the scribes and Pharisees watching Him closely?
written:LUK-6-6:1.answer: To find a reason to accuse Him if He healed on the Sabbath

written:LUK-6-6:2.question: In Luke 6, what two-part question did Jesus ask the scribes and Pharisees before He healed the man's withered hand?
written:LUK-6-6:2.answer: Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or destroy it?

written:LUK-6-20:1.question: In Luke’s account of the Beatitudes, what does Jesus say will happen to those who weep now?
written:LUK-6-20:1.why: also right: B: Luke 6:21 says 'Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.' B ('comforted') is the Matthew 5:4 version of the mourners' blessing, so it is true elsewhere in Scripture, but it is not what Luke's account says.

written:LUK-8-26:3.question: In Luke 8, when the people of the region of the Gerasenes found the healed man, how was he sitting and what was his condition?
written:LUK-8-26:3.answer: Sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind
written:LUK-8-26:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-8-26:5.question: In Luke 8, after the healed man went away, where did he proclaim how much Jesus had done for him?
written:LUK-8-26:5.why: also right: C: Luke 8:39 says 'all over the town.' Mark 5:20 says the man proclaimed in the Decapolis, a broader region that includes the town, so C is arguable from another Gospel.

written:LUK-9-7:1.question: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that Jesus' disciples were doing, what did some people say about who was behind it?
written:LUK-9-7:1.answer: John had risen from the dead
written:LUK-9-7:1.why: also right: B, C, D: A is the only option the text states outright ("some were saying that John had risen from the dead"). But the text says only "a prophet of old had arisen," so Moses (C) or Isaiah (D) could fairly be argued as instances of that. David (B) is a weaker case, since Acts 2:30 calls him a prophet. The question also says "disciples were doing" where the text says "all that was happening."

written:LUK-9-18:2.question: In Luke 9, when Jesus asked who the crowds said He was, which of these did the disciples report people were saying?
written:LUK-9-18:2.why: also right: D: Luke names John the Baptist explicitly, so A is settled by the section. D (Jeremiah) is not named in Luke, but Luke's 'a prophet of old' does not exclude him, and Matthew 16:14 (parallel passage) lists Jeremiah among the crowd's opinions. Moses and Isaiah are not reported as opinions anywhere in the Gospel accounts.

written:LUK-9-28:2.question: In the days after Jesus was transfigured before Peter, John, and James, what did the disciples do about what they had seen?
written:LUK-9-28:2.answer: They kept it to themselves and told no one
written:LUK-9-28:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LUK-9-37:1.question: In Luke 9, when the man in the crowd begged Jesus to look at his son, what did he say about the boy?
written:LUK-9-37:1.why: also right: C: Choice C is logically true of an only son, since he is necessarily the firstborn. But the man said "only child," not "firstborn," so B is the answer the text supports.

written:LUK-9-37:2.question: In Luke 9, after the boy was brought to Him, what did Jesus do with the boy once the demon slammed him to the ground?
written:LUK-9-37:2.answer: He rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father

written:LUK-9-43:1.question: In Luke 9, after Jesus healed the boy with the demon, what did Jesus say the Son of Man was about to be delivered into?
written:LUK-9-43:1.why: also right: B: Romans are men, and Luke 18:32 says the Son of Man will be delivered over to the Gentiles, so B is a narrower truth found elsewhere. It is not the wording Jesus used here, which is 'the hands of men.' The healing premise comes from the surrounding chapter, not this section, but the answer does not depend on it.

written:LUK-11-14:3.question: In Jesus' saying in Luke 11 about a strong man guarding his house, what happens when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him?
written:LUK-11-14:3.answer: He takes away the armor the man trusted and divides up his plunder

written:LUK-17-1:1.question: In Jesus' teaching to His disciples in Luke 17, what would be better for a person than causing one of these little ones to stumble?
written:LUK-17-1:1.answer: Having a millstone hung around his neck and being thrown into the sea

written:LUK-18-18:3.question: In Luke 18, what did Jesus say those who leave home for the kingdom of God will receive in the age to come?
written:LUK-18-18:3.why: also right: D: Matthew 19:28, the parallel to this passage, promises the Twelve (who left everything to follow Jesus) that they will sit on twelve thrones, so D is arguably true of those who left home, though this section does not say it.

written:LUK-20-9:1.question: In Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants in Luke 20, how many servants did the owner send before he sent his beloved son?
written:LUK-20-9:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LUK-20-9:2.question: In Jesus' parable in Luke 20, what did the owner of the vineyard do after the tenants had planted nothing and he had rented it out to them?
written:LUK-20-9:2.answer: He went away for a long time
written:LUK-20-9:2.why: not clear on its own: The question's premise is wrong: in Luke 20:9 the owner planted the vineyard, not the tenants. The answer (he went into another country for a long while) is still D, but the wording should be fixed.

written:LUK-20-19:2.question: In Luke 20, what was the purpose of the spies sent to watch Jesus, who pretended to be sincere?
written:LUK-20-19:2.answer: To catch him in his words and hand him over to the governor

written:LUK-20-19:3.question: In Luke 20, how did the people react to Jesus' answer about giving to Caesar and to God?
written:LUK-20-19:3.answer: They were amazed and fell silent
written:LUK-20-19:3.why: the section does not settle it: The text says the opponents (the spies, the 'they' of v.26) were amazed and fell silent. It does not describe the people's reaction, so the question's premise is off. B is the closest match, but the subject is the opponents, not the people.

written:LUK-21-25:1.question: In Jesus' teaching about His return in Luke 21, what does He tell His followers to do when these things begin to happen?
written:LUK-21-25:1.answer: Stand up and lift up their heads
written:LUK-21-25:1.why: not clear on its own: "These things" has no antecedent in the question, so a quiz-taker can't tell which events are meant. D matches Luke 21:28 ("straighten up and raise your heads") after the cosmic signs of 21:25-27. A could be argued if "these things" meant the siege of Jerusalem in Luke 21:20-21, where the instruction is to flee to the mountains. B and C are not instructions Jesus gives at this point.

written:LUK-23-13:2.question: When Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people, what did he say about Herod's finding concerning Jesus?
written:LUK-23-13:2.answer: Herod also found nothing deserving of death, and sent Jesus back
written:LUK-23-13:2.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LUK-24-1:2.question: When the women reported the empty tomb to the Eleven and the others, how did the apostles react?
written:LUK-24-1:2.answer: Their words seemed like nonsense, and they did not believe the women.
written:LUK-24-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-24-1:3.question: After the women reported the empty tomb, which apostle got up and ran to the tomb, where he saw only the linen cloths?
written:LUK-24-1:3.why: also right: B: Luke 24:12 names Peter. John 20:3-8 says John also ran to the tomb with Peter, outran him, and saw the linen cloths lying there, so John is arguably right from elsewhere in Scripture. The section itself settles the answer as Peter.

written:JHN-18-28:4.question: According to Jesus, for what purpose was He born and did He come into the world?
written:JHN-18-28:4.why: also right: A, B: The section settles it ("For this reason I was born and have come into the world, to testify to the truth"), but Jesus states other purposes elsewhere: A matches Matthew 5:17 (came to fulfill the Law and the Prophets), and B matches Matthew 15:24 (sent only to the lost sheep of Israel). Both are arguable for 'what purpose He came,' so the question is weaker than it looks.

written:ROM-9-6:5.question: According to Romans 9:17, why did God raise up Pharaoh?
written:ROM-9-6:5.answer: To display His power in him and proclaim His name in all the earth

written:ROM-9-6:6.question: In Romans 9:21, what illustration does Paul use to answer the question of why God made people differently?
written:ROM-9-6:6.answer: A potter making vessels from the same lump of clay
written:ROM-9-6:6.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:GAL-2-1:2.question: In Galatians 2, why did Paul say the false brothers had come in under false pretenses?
written:GAL-2-1:2.answer: To spy on their freedom in Christ Jesus and enslave them
written:GAL-2-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:1PE-5-1:2.question: In 1 Peter 5:4, what will the elders receive when the Chief Shepherd appears?
written:1PE-5-1:2.answer: The crown of glory that will never fade away
written:1PE-5-1:2.why: also right: A, C: The text names the crown of glory that never fades (B), so B is the answer. A and C are crowns promised to faithful believers elsewhere (crown of life in Jas 1:12 and Rev 2:10; crown of righteousness in 2 Tim 4:8, which extends to all who love Christ's appearing), so a reader could argue for them. Neither wording matches 5:4, though.

written:1JN-1-1:1.question: In 1 John 1:3, with whom does the author say the fellowship of the apostles is, along with the Father?
written:1JN-1-1:1.why: also right: A: 1 John 1:3 names the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, as the fellowship's object. The Holy Spirit is not named in this verse, but 2 Corinthians 13:14 speaks of the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, so choice A is arguable from elsewhere in Scripture.

written:DEU-16-1:2.question: In Deuteronomy 16, where were the Israelites to offer the Passover sacrifice?
written:DEU-16-1:2.answer: At the place the LORD would choose as a dwelling for His Name

written:DEU-16-1:3.question: According to Deuteronomy 16, what were the Israelites to do on the seventh day of eating unleavened bread?
written:DEU-16-1:3.answer: Hold a solemn assembly to the LORD and do no work
written:DEU-16-1:3.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JOS-20-1:1.question: In Joshua 20, to whom did the LORD speak, telling him to have the Israelites designate the cities of refuge?

written:LUK-3-1:2.question: Why did Herod the tetrarch lock John the Baptist up in prison?
written:LUK-3-1:2.answer: John rebuked him about Herodias, his brother’s wife, and his evils
written:LUK-3-1:2.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:LUK-5-12:2.question: After Jesus healed the man with leprosy and the news spread to great crowds, what did Jesus frequently do, according to Luke 5:16?
written:LUK-5-12:2.answer: He withdrew to the wilderness to pray
written:LUK-5-12:2.why: also right: B, C, D: Luke 5:16 settles A. B, C and D each describe something Jesus did elsewhere (teaching from a boat by the Sea of Galilee, Mark 4:1; going up to Jerusalem for feasts, John 2:13; going to synagogues as his custom, Luke 4:16), but none is what this verse says he frequently did.

written:LUK-6-1:1.question: In Luke 6, what did Jesus' disciples do with the heads of grain after picking them as they passed through the grainfields on the Sabbath?
written:LUK-6-1:1.answer: Rubbed them in their hands and ate them
written:LUK-6-1:1.why: the answer's words are not in the cited verses

written:LUK-19-28:3.question: In Luke 19, why did the whole multitude of disciples begin to praise God joyfully in a loud voice as Jesus approached the descent from the Mount of Olives?
written:LUK-19-28:3.answer: For all the miracles they had seen
written:LUK-19-28:3.why: also right: B, C: Text says 'for all the miracles they had seen.' B (Jericho blind man, Luke 18:35-43) and C (Lazarus, John 11-12) are specific miracles the crowd had seen, so they are narrower instances that could fairly be argued.

written:LUK-22-63:1.question: In Luke 22, after Jesus was seized, what did the men who were holding Him do to Him?
written:LUK-22-63:1.answer: They mocked Him and beat Him
written:LUK-22-63:1.why: also right: D: D is not stated in Luke 22:63-65, but Mark 14:65 describes spitting on Jesus in this same scene (Jewish council, blindfolding, 'Prophesy!'), and John 18:12 says He was bound by the arresting party. The section itself settles C: they mocked and beat Him.

written:JHN-11-45:1.question: In John 11, who was the high priest that year who told the Sanhedrin it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish?
written:JHN-11-45:1.why: also right: D: Verse 11:49 names Caiaphas as high priest that year, and 11:51 repeats it. Annas is also called a high priest in Luke 3:2 and Acts 4:6, and John 18:13 identifies him as Caiaphas's father-in-law, so D is arguable in a looser sense. The question's 'that year' points to Caiaphas.

written:JHN-18-15:1.question: In John 18, when Peter stood outside at the door of the high priest's courtyard, who brought him in?
written:JHN-18-15:1.answer: The other disciple who was known to the high priest
written:JHN-18-15:1.why: the right choice is plainly the longest

written:JHN-18-15:2.question: In John 18, when the servant girl at the door asked Peter whether he was also one of Jesus' disciples, how did Peter answer?
written:JHN-18-15:2.why: also right: B, C: John's account gives "I am not" (D). Other Gospels record the same servant-girl exchange with different wording: Luke 22:57 has "Woman, I do not know Him" (B), and Mark 14:68 has "I neither know nor understand what you are talking about" (close in sense to C). A is not Peter's answer to anyone in any account; it is a paraphrase of the bystanders' remark in Matthew 26:73 and Mark 14:70, and Peter's reply there was an oath.

written:JHN-20-1:1.question: In John 20, who went to the tomb early on the first day of the week while it was still dark and saw that the stone had been removed?
written:JHN-20-1:1.why: also right: C: Mary the mother of James also went to the tomb at dawn (Matthew 28:1; Mark 16:1-4 says they saw the stone rolled away), so C is arguably right elsewhere in Scripture. Salome (A) is also in Mark 16:1 but Mark puts that visit after sunrise, not while still dark, so A does not fit the question's details.

written:JHN-12-12:1.question: In John 12, according to the account of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, why did the crowd go out to meet Him?
written:JHN-12-12:1.answer: They heard He had performed the sign of raising Lazarus
